operations.specification: Create a guest join endpoint for the discussion_board_guestusers table. This operation will create (or reuse, depending on business rules) a minimal guest placeholder account using an opaque anonymous_token, and then issue JWT access/refresh tokens for the guestUser actor. The path will be /auth/guestUser/join with POST method. Request body will carry whatever fingerprint or client-side identifier is needed to derive or propose anonymous_token; response body will be a standard authorized payload DTO for DiscussionBoardGuestUser. This endpoint is public (no prior auth) and uses authorizationType "join" and authorizationActor "guestUser".
operations.description:
This API operation registers or materializes a guest user placeholder account in the discussion board system based on the Prisma table discussion_board_guestusers.

The underlying discussion_board_guestusers table has an id primary key of type uuid that uniquely identifies each guest user placeholder record. The core business identifier stored for a guest is anonymous_token, a non-null string that serves as an opaque token or fingerprint to correlate the same unauthenticated visitor across visits. The schema enforces a unique index on anonymous_token so that the same token cannot map to multiple guest rows, which allows this endpoint to either create a new record or reuse an existing one when the same token is presented.

The table also has created_at and updated_at datetime fields that capture when the guest record was created and last updated. These timestamps must be maintained consistently whenever a new guest is created or when an existing guest record is touched as part of join processing. Additionally, there is a nullable deleted_at field that marks when a guest record has been closed or is no longer in active use. When deleted_at is not null, the system should treat the guest as inactive and either create a new record or restore the existing one according to business policy.

From a security perspective, this endpoint does not collect passwords or personally identifiable information. It instead relies on the opaque anonymous_token to represent the guest identity and then issues JWT tokens for the guestUser actor role. The token payload will internally reference the discussion_board_guestusers.id value so the backend can later resolve guest-specific state if needed, while still keeping the external interface minimal.

Validation rules should ensure that anonymous_token is a non-empty string that meets any length or pattern constraints defined at the DTO level, and that a single active guest record exists per token, in line with the unique index on anonymous_token. If an existing record is found with a non-null deleted_at timestamp, the implementation should either reject the join or clear deleted_at and update updated_at, depending on defined business rules.

This operation is typically the first step for guests that need a persistent identity for features like tracking read history or later conversion to a full member account. It works together with the guest token refresh endpoint, which uses the guest's refresh token to get a new access token without changing the underlying discussion_board_guestusers record.
operations.summary: Register or materialize a guest placeholder account in discussion_board_guestusers and issue JWT tokens for guestUser.

requestBody.description: Guest join payload containing the opaque token or fingerprint used to derive or look up anonymous_token in discussion_board_guestusers.

responseBody.description: Authorized guestUser session information including issued JWT tokens derived from discussion_board_guestusers.

operations.specification: Create a guest refresh endpoint for the discussion_board_guestusers table. This operation will validate a guest refresh token associated with a specific discussion_board_guestusers.id and then issue a new set of JWT access (and potentially refresh) tokens for the guestUser actor. The path will be /auth/guestUser/refresh with POST method. Request body will contain the refresh token and any required client context; response body will be the standard DiscussionBoardGuestUser authorized DTO. This endpoint is accessible with a valid refresh token, uses authorizationType "refresh", and authorizationActor "guestUser".
operations.description:
This API operation refreshes JWT tokens for a guestUser actor that is backed by a record in the discussion_board_guestusers table.

The discussion_board_guestusers table defines id as the uuid primary key for each guest placeholder account. It also stores anonymous_token as an opaque string used to correlate visits from the same unauthenticated visitor, with a unique index on anonymous_token to prevent conflicting identities. While anonymous_token is the primary business key at creation time, the refresh endpoint typically relies on the subject embedded in the refresh token, which should reference the id field so the system can reliably look up the correct guest record.

The table contains created_at and updated_at datetime fields that record when the guest entry was created and when it was last updated. During a refresh operation, implementations may choose to update updated_at to reflect recent activity, enabling activity-based retention policies for guest records. The nullable deleted_at field indicates that the guest record is no longer active; when deleted_at is not null, the refresh operation must treat the guest as deactivated and reject the refresh request, as no new tokens should be issued for closed guest identities.

From a security perspective, this endpoint requires a valid guest refresh token that has been previously issued by the join operation or a prior refresh. The refresh token is validated for integrity, expiration, and correct association with a discussion_board_guestusers.id. If validation succeeds and the underlying guest record exists and is not marked as deleted via deleted_at, the system issues a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token) encapsulated in the standardized authorization response.

Validation and error handling must properly distinguish between invalid or expired tokens, missing guest records, and records that have been logically closed via deleted_at. In each failure scenario, the endpoint should refuse to issue new tokens while avoiding leakage of internal details about token structure or underlying storage.

This operation is typically used after the guest has already been joined through the guest join endpoint. Clients first call /auth/guestUser/join to obtain initial tokens, then call /auth/guestUser/refresh when the access token is about to expire, ensuring a smooth guest browsing experience without re-materializing or changing the underlying discussion_board_guestusers record.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for an existing guestUser session backed by discussion_board_guestusers.

requestBody.description: Guest refresh payload containing the refresh token associated with a discussion_board_guestusers record.

responseBody.description: Refreshed authorized guestUser session information including new JWT tokens.

operations.specification: Create a registration (join) endpoint for member users of the discussionBoard service, backed by the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma table. This operation will accept necessary registration data in the request body (email, password, displayName, and optional profile fields) and create a new `discussion_board_memberusers` record with initial lifecycle state. After successful creation it will issue JWT access/refresh tokens for the newly registered member and return them using the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` response schema, which represents an authenticated member session including token information and minimal user identity. The endpoint will not directly touch session or restriction tables, but it will respect constraints implied by `account_status`, `email_verified`, and uniqueness of `email`.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new member user account in the discussionBoard service by inserting a row into the `discussion_board_memberusers` table and then issuing JWT tokens for immediate authenticated use.

The underlying `discussion_board_memberusers` schema defines `email` as the unique, primary contact field and login identifier, so the request body must include an email value that does not collide with existing rows. The `password_hash` column stores a hashed credential only; the API accepts a raw password field in the DTO, hashes it according to the platform’s password policy, and persists only the hash. The `display_name` column is required and is used as the public nickname shown on articles and comments, while optional profile fields like `bio` and `location` allow richer profile data to be stored at creation time.

Lifecycle-related columns such as `account_status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`, `last_login_at`, `closed_at`, and `closed_by_admin` are managed by business logic rather than user-supplied values. On registration, the account will typically be initialized with an `account_status` of `active`, `deleted_at` and `closed_at` set to null, `closed_by_admin` set to false, and timestamps filled using the application clock. The `email_verified` flag is set based on whether the service considers registration to imply verification; if a separate verification flow exists it should be initialized to false.

Security-wise, this endpoint is public (`authorizationActor` is null) but carefully validates input, enforces the uniqueness constraint on `email`, and ensures that `password_hash` is derived using a strong one-way hashing function with appropriate salts and cost factors. It does not allow clients to set lifecycle or audit fields directly, preserving integrity of `account_status`, deletion and closure timestamps, and administrative closure flags.

The response uses the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` schema, which encapsulates the issued JWT access and refresh tokens along with core member user identity derived from the newly created `discussion_board_memberusers` row. The provider should also update `last_login_at` to the current time when issuing tokens so that account lifecycle analytics remain accurate.

This join operation typically precedes future calls to the member login and refresh endpoints. Once registered, a member can use the login endpoint to obtain new tokens after logout or token expiry, and the refresh endpoint to rotate tokens without resubmitting credentials, all while the restrictions in `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` and notification preferences in `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` continue to govern behavior and messaging.
operations.summary: Register a new member user in `discussion_board_memberusers` and return JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration information for creating a discussionBoard member user account, including email, password, and profile fields.

responseBody.description: Authorized session payload for a newly registered member user, including JWT tokens and core identity.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Create a login endpoint for member users of the discussionBoard service, using credentials stored in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table. This operation will accept login credentials (email and password) in the request body, validate them against the `email` and `password_hash` fields, and, on success, issue JWT access and refresh tokens described by the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` response schema. It will also update the `last_login_at` column for the authenticated user and enforce lifecycle constraints defined by `account_status`, `deleted_at`, `closed_at`, and `closed_by_admin`.
operations.description:
This operation authenticates an existing member user by validating their credentials against the `discussion_board_memberusers` table and issues fresh JWT tokens for subsequent API access.

The `discussion_board_memberusers` schema designates `email` as the unique login identifier and primary contact field, while `password_hash` stores the hashed password. The request body therefore includes a plain-text password and email, which are used to locate the appropriate row by `email` and verify the provided password against `password_hash` using the configured hashing algorithm. No other schema fields are writable from this endpoint.

Account lifecycle flags and timestamps play a critical role in deciding whether a login is permitted. The `account_status` field indicates high-level states such as active, suspended, closed, or banned; the login handler must reject authentication when `account_status` does not represent an allowed state. Additionally, if `deleted_at` or `closed_at` are non-null, or if `closed_by_admin` is true, the operation should treat the account as unavailable for login even if credentials match, aligning with business rules for account closure. The `email_verified` column can also be used to block or warn on login for unverified accounts according to the service’s policy.

Upon successful authentication, the service updates `last_login_at` with the current timestamp to reflect this login event, while `updated_at` may also be refreshed. It then creates a JWT access token and refresh token bound to the member user’s `id` and the current security context. The response uses the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` schema to return these tokens alongside minimal identity details, enabling clients to attach the access token to subsequent API requests.

This endpoint is public (`authorizationActor` is null) because users must be able to submit credentials before being authenticated. However, rate limiting, IP-based monitoring, and checks against `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` (for example, full block states) should be implemented in the service logic that consumes this interface to mitigate abuse. The endpoint integrates naturally with the join and refresh operations: users first register via join, then repeatedly invoke login and refresh as needed to maintain authenticated sessions.
operations.summary: Authenticate a member user in `discussion_board_memberusers` using email and password and return JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for a discussionBoard member user, including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authorized session payload for an authenticated member user, including JWT tokens and core identity.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Create a token refresh endpoint for member users of the discussionBoard service that renews JWT access/refresh tokens without resubmitting credentials. This endpoint will validate an incoming refresh token associated with a `discussion_board_memberusers` record and, if valid and permitted by the user’s lifecycle state, will issue new tokens represented by the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` response schema. It will respect `account_status`, `deleted_at`, `closed_at`, `closed_by_admin`, and may consult `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` to reject refresh for fully blocked accounts, but it will not modify user profile fields or password hashes.
operations.description:
This operation refreshes JWT tokens for an already authenticated member user of the discussionBoard service, using a previously issued refresh token to avoid repeated credential entry.

The underlying identity still comes from the `discussion_board_memberusers` table, where `email` is the unique login identifier and `password_hash` holds the credential hash. However, unlike the login endpoint, this refresh endpoint does not accept or verify a password; instead, it receives a refresh token encoded in the request body or authorization context, validates its integrity and expiry, and maps it back to a specific member user `id`.

Before issuing new tokens, the service must confirm that the associated account remains in good standing. It should check `account_status` for disallowed values such as suspended, closed, or banned, and also consider `deleted_at` and `closed_at` timestamps and the `closed_by_admin` flag. If the account is no longer active by business rules, the refresh request must be rejected even if the token itself is structurally valid. The `email_verified` flag can participate in additional policy decisions, for example blocking refresh if verification has lapsed or been revoked.

When a refresh is accepted, timestamps like `updated_at` may be updated to reflect activity, and optional security hooks may log the event for audit purposes. The endpoint then mints a new set of JWT access and refresh tokens, encoded using the latest signing keys and policies, and returns them using the `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IAuthorized` schema. The refreshed access token enables continued access, while the new refresh token replaces the previous one according to the platform’s rotation rules.

From an access perspective, this endpoint is intended for authenticated contexts, but because the transport of the refresh token itself is the primary proof, the interface is marked with `authorizationActor` null while the implementation enforces token validation. It complements the join and login flows: new members obtain initial tokens via join, returning members use login with credentials, and long-lived clients rely on this refresh endpoint to maintain sessions without storing passwords, all within the constraints modeled by `discussion_board_memberusers` and related restriction records.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for a member user associated with `discussion_board_memberusers` using a valid refresh token.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload for a discussionBoard member user requesting new JWT tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized session payload for a member user after successful token refresh, including new JWT tokens and core identity.

operations.specification: Create a new administrator account in the discussion_board_adminusers table and issue initial JWT tokens for the adminUser actor. This operation will insert a new row into discussion_board_adminusers with the provided email, password_hash (derived from the plaintext password in the DTO at service level), display_name, and optional bio. It will initialize email_verified to false, account_status to an initial lifecycle state such as "active" according to business rules, and set created_at/updated_at timestamps while leaving deleted_at and last_login_at as null. After persistence, the authentication layer will generate access and refresh tokens for the new administrator and return them along with basic admin account information using the IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized response DTO.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new administrative user account for the discussionBoard service by creating a record in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table and then issuing initial authentication tokens specific to the `adminUser` actor.

At the database level, the operation persists core authentication and profile fields defined on `discussion_board_adminusers`, including `email`, `password_hash`, `display_name`, and the optional `bio` field. The service layer is responsible for hashing the incoming credential into `password_hash`, ensuring that plain-text passwords are never stored. The `email_verified` boolean is initialized based on business rules for admin onboarding (typically `false` until a verification flow completes), and `account_status` is set to a valid lifecycle value such as `"active"`. Timestamps `created_at` and `updated_at` are set to the current time, while `deleted_at` and `last_login_at` remain `null` for a newly created administrator.

From a security perspective, the endpoint is public because new administrators may be provisioned through this API according to operational policy, but it still enforces strict validation on `email` to respect the unique index on the `email` column and on password strength according to technical guidelines. If an email already exists in `discussion_board_adminusers.email`, the operation must fail with a clear error without creating a duplicate row. The newly created admin will be immediately treated as an `adminUser` actor for the purpose of JWT issuance, but subsequent access to privileged moderation APIs will still be controlled by those endpoints' `authorizationActor` configuration.

The operation is tightly coupled to the `discussion_board_adminusers` model, whose description highlights that it stores authentication credentials, basic profile fields, and lifecycle state for administrative users. By setting `account_status` appropriately and honoring `email_verified`, the system can later restrict or suspend access in cooperation with other admin management features. The `deleted_at` field is left `null` here, so that the admin account is fully usable until an explicit lifecycle change or soft deletion happens through another operation.

On successful registration, the service issues JWT tokens representing the `adminUser` actor and returns them using the `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized` response schema. This response encapsulates both token information and essential admin profile data derived from `discussion_board_adminusers`, such as `id`, `email`, `display_name`, `account_status`, and `email_verified`. Error responses include validation failures (e.g., invalid email format, weak password), uniqueness violations on `email`, and unexpected persistence errors, all surfaced with appropriate HTTP status codes.

This endpoint is typically used once per administrative account creation, and is logically followed by the admin login and refresh operations. Other business APIs, such as moderation of articles or processing of reports, depend on the existence of admin accounts created through this or equivalent provisioning flows but are not direct prerequisites for this operation.
operations.summary: Register a new administrative user in discussion_board_adminusers and issue initial adminUser JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration information required to create a new adminUser account, including email, credential, display name, and optional profile fields.

responseBody.description: Authorized adminUser session information including JWT tokens and basic admin account profile derived from discussion_board_adminusers.

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing administrator stored in the discussion_board_adminusers table using their email and credential, update last_login_at and possibly updated_at, and issue new JWT tokens for the adminUser actor. The operation validates the provided email against the unique email column and checks the submitted credential against the stored password_hash. On success, it writes the new login timestamp into last_login_at, may create a session record in discussion_board_adminuser_sessions for audit (with ip, href, referrer, created_at, and future expired_at), and returns tokens and basic admin info in IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized.
operations.description:
This operation performs login for an existing administrative account of the `adminUser` actor by validating credentials against the `discussion_board_adminusers` table and then issuing fresh JWT tokens.

The service first locates an administrator row using the unique `email` column on `discussion_board_adminusers`. If no row matches the provided email, or if the stored `password_hash` does not correspond to the supplied credential after hashing, the operation fails with an authentication error without revealing whether the email exists. It also checks lifecycle state via the `account_status` column, denying login for disallowed states such as suspended or closed as defined in business rules, and may consider the `deleted_at` timestamp to prevent login when an account has been logically removed.

When authentication succeeds, the service updates `last_login_at` in `discussion_board_adminusers` to the current timestamp and may also refresh `updated_at` to reflect the change. Additionally, it can insert a new row into `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`, populating `discussion_board_adminuser_id` with the administrator's `id`, capturing `ip`, `href`, and `referrer` from the incoming request context for audit purposes, and setting `created_at` and an eventual `expired_at` according to the session strategy. This session record provides traceable context for privileged admin activity.

Security-wise, this endpoint is public in terms of HTTP access because it must accept credentials from unauthenticated clients, but all subsequent access to administrative features is guarded by the tokens it issues. It enforces strict validation on the `email` format and credential structure and respects the `email_verified` column to optionally block or warn about logins from unverified admin accounts depending on policy. The `account_status` and `deleted_at` fields ensure that closed or banned admins cannot authenticate.

Upon successful login, the operation returns `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized`, which encapsulates both the JWT token pair and an admin profile projection based on `discussion_board_adminusers`, including fields such as `id`, `email`, `display_name`, `account_status`, and `email_verified`. Error responses cover invalid credentials, disallowed `account_status`, unverified email restrictions, and internal server failures, each mapped to appropriate HTTP status codes.

This endpoint is typically the primary entry point for admin sessions and is closely related to the admin refresh operation, which re-issues tokens based on a valid refresh token. It does not require prior calls beyond the existence of an admin account, usually created via the admin join endpoint or an internal provisioning process.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for an existing adminUser account, including email and credential information required for authentication.

responseBody.description: Authorized adminUser session information including freshly issued JWT tokens and admin profile summary derived from discussion_board_adminusers.

operations.specification: Refresh JWT tokens for an already authenticated administrator represented as an adminUser actor, without changing core account data in discussion_board_adminusers. The operation receives a refresh token, validates it against token storage or embedded claims that reference the admin's id from discussion_board_adminusers, checks lifecycle fields such as account_status, deleted_at, and email_verified, and ensures the session is still valid using discussion_board_adminuser_sessions (matching discussion_board_adminuser_id and checking expired_at). On success, it issues a new token pair encapsulated in IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized without modifying email, display_name, or other profile fields.
operations.description:
This operation renews JWT tokens for an administrative user who is already recognized as an `adminUser` actor, using a valid refresh token rather than credentials. It is designed to extend authenticated admin sessions while respecting account lifecycle and session policies defined in the database.

At the data layer, the operation ties the incoming refresh token to an administrator row in `discussion_board_adminusers`, typically by embedding the admin `id` in the token or by looking up a token store that references `discussion_board_adminusers.id`. Before issuing new tokens, it inspects lifecycle fields such as `account_status`, `deleted_at`, and optionally `email_verified` to ensure that the administrator is still allowed to act. If `account_status` indicates a suspended or closed state, or if `deleted_at` is non-null, the refresh attempt fails and no new tokens are issued.

The operation may also consult `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` to validate that the underlying admin session is still active. Using the `discussion_board_adminuser_id` foreign key and `created_at` or `expired_at` timestamps, it can confirm that the session has not been explicitly terminated or expired. If a corresponding session record is missing or has an `expired_at` earlier than the current time, the refresh request is rejected to prevent indefinite session extension.

From a security standpoint, this endpoint requires an existing refresh token and should not be publicly usable without prior authentication context. It does not accept credentials or modify sensitive fields like `password_hash` or `email`; instead, it focuses solely on re-issuing access and refresh tokens when the admin account and session remain valid. The tokens produced continue to represent the `adminUser` actor and are constrained by whatever scopes or claims the system assigns to administrators.

On success, the operation returns `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IAuthorized`, which contains the new JWT token set and a current snapshot of relevant admin information derived from `discussion_board_adminusers`, such as `id`, `email`, `display_name`, `account_status`, and `email_verified`. This allows clients to update any cached admin profile state alongside tokens. Failure responses include invalid or expired refresh tokens, disallowed account states, terminated sessions detected via `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions.expired_at`, and internal server errors.

This refresh endpoint is typically called after the admin login endpoint has already created both a database session record and an initial token set. It works in conjunction with logout or session invalidation features, which update `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions.expired_at` or revoke tokens so that subsequent refresh attempts fail as expected.
operations.summary: Refresh adminUser JWT tokens using a valid refresh token while validating discussion_board_adminusers and discussion_board_adminuser_sessions state.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload for an existing adminUser session, used to request new JWT tokens without resubmitting credentials.

responseBody.description: Refreshed JWT tokens and current admin profile snapshot for the adminUser actor, derived from discussion_board_adminusers.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of discussion articles from the Prisma table `discussion_board_articles`. It is designed as the primary list/search endpoint for the discussionBoard service, supporting browsing, basic search, and ordering by key fields such as creation time and category.

The endpoint uses HTTP PATCH on `/discussionBoard/articles` to allow a structured JSON request body that can grow over time with additional search and filter criteria without overloading query parameters. The request DTO is modeled as `IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest`, which encapsulates pagination (page number, page size), optional free-text search terms applied to text columns such as title and body, and filters such as category, visibility status, and created-at ranges.

The response is a paginated container `IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary` that returns summary projections of articles optimized for list views. Each summary includes fields derived from the `discussion_board_articles` schema such as the article identifier, title, summary preview, visibility status, and timestamps, along with basic category information. Implementation details such as specific column names or index types are left to the service layer but must remain consistent with the underlying Prisma model.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated collection of discussion board articles from the `discussion_board_articles` table to support browsing and search flows.

This operation is the main entry point for users to explore economic and political discussion content. It reads from the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model, which represents the core discussion topics. The request body type `IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest` allows clients to specify pagination options, sorting preferences (for example, newest first based on creation timestamp), and domain filters such as one or more category identifiers, visibility or moderation states to include, or created-at ranges for time-bounded browsing. When a free-text search string is provided, the implementation is expected to use appropriate indexes on text columns (for example, title and body) to efficiently search for matching articles.

From a security and permissions perspective, this endpoint is intentionally designed as a read-only operation and can be exposed either publicly or to any authenticated user depending on deployment policy. The API documentation models it with an empty `authorizationActors` list and `authorizationActor: null` to allow maximum flexibility; actual visibility rules, such as hiding logically removed or non-visible content or restricting some categories, are enforced inside the service layer based on the article’s status fields and category relationships, not by splitting the endpoint per actor. Implementations must ensure that records that should not be visible in normal browsing are excluded from list results according to the business rules defined against the Prisma schema.

This operation is closely related to the single-article retrieval endpoint `GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`, which should be used to obtain the full article body and complete metadata when a user selects a specific list item. Typical user flows will call this list endpoint first to obtain a paginated set of article summaries, then call the detail endpoint for a selected article. Error handling must validate pagination parameters and filter values in `IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest`, returning clear validation errors when requested pages are out of range or when filter values (such as moderation states or category identifiers) are invalid according to business rules and database constraints.
operations.summary: Search and list discussion_board_articles with pagination and filters.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for listing discussion board articles derived from the `discussion_board_articles` schema.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of discussion board article summaries matching the given search and filter criteria, based on the `discussion_board_articles` table.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the full detail of a single discussion article from the Prisma table `discussion_board_articles` using its primary key `id`. It serves as the main detail view endpoint for a selected article in the discussionBoard service.

The endpoint uses HTTP GET on `/discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`, where `articleId` is the UUID primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` record. The parameter is modeled explicitly in the path parameters as a string with `uuid` format. The operation returns a detailed DTO `IDiscussionBoardArticle` that exposes all necessary fields from the underlying schema such as identifier, title, body, optional summary, status or moderation information, timestamps, and category reference information, matching the actual Prisma model.

Because the `discussion_board_articles` table may use fields for logical deletion and business-level moderation or visibility, the operation must enforce visibility rules: normal clients should not be able to retrieve articles that are not meant to be visible according to those status fields unless business rules explicitly allow it (for example, admin-only access, which would be handled via a different actor-restricted endpoint). The operation is read-only and has no side effects other than optional analytics handled by other system components.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full detail of a single discussion article identified by its UUID primary key in the `discussion_board_articles` table.

This operation reads from the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model, which represents individual economic and political discussion topics, including title, body text, optional summary for previews, status or moderation information, and audit timestamps such as when the article was created and last updated. The implementation must map these fields in `IDiscussionBoardArticle` consistently with the schema and enforce any visibility or retention rules configured for the service.

The path parameter `articleId` is the primary key `id` of the `discussion_board_articles` record and is represented as a string with UUID format. When this endpoint is called, the implementation must load the target article by `id` and apply moderation and permission checks based on the article’s status and any associated category rules. If the article is not found or is not visible to the caller due to these rules, the operation should return an appropriate not-found or forbidden error instead of leaking the existence of hidden content.

This detail endpoint is typically used together with the list/search endpoint `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles`, where users first obtain a paginated list of article summaries and then call this endpoint to retrieve the selected article’s full body and metadata as modeled in `IDiscussionBoardArticle`. Error handling must validate the `articleId` format as a UUID and return clear error responses when invalid identifiers are supplied or when the referenced article does not exist in the `discussion_board_articles` table.
operations.summary: Get a single discussion_board_articles record by its UUID primary key.

The endpoint exposes a read-only view that, given an `articleId` identifying a record in `discussion_board_articles`, looks up the corresponding authorship record in `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` (if the article was created by a member user rather than an admin). Using that authorship record, it then joins to the `discussion_board_memberusers` table to return a DTO representing the member author information. The response focuses on author identity and profile fields appropriate to display as "article writer" information in the UI, not on article content itself.

This operation does not perform any modification of article or user data. It is a simple retrieval and therefore uses HTTP GET semantics with no request body. It should be implemented to cleanly handle the case where the target article either does not exist, or exists but was authored by an admin user instead of a member user, in which case an appropriate not-found error for the member author context should be returned.
operations.description:
Retrieve information about the member user who authored a particular discussion board article.

This operation is designed for cases where articles on the economic and political discussion board are written by registered member users stored in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table, and the authorship relationship is recorded in the `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` subsidiary table. The client supplies an `articleId` path parameter, which corresponds to the primary key of a row in `discussion_board_articles`. Using this identifier, the backend looks up an authorship link record in `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` and, from there, loads the associated member user account.

From a security and privacy standpoint, the response should contain only those member profile fields that are intended to be publicly visible as author information, such as display name, optional profile metadata allowed by the business rules, and any badge or status flags that are considered safe to expose. Sensitive data like authentication credentials, internal moderation flags that are not meant for general users, or contact details that are not part of the public profile must not be included in the DTO. The operation itself is read-only and can typically be exposed to all actors, because it only reveals author information that would already be visible wherever the article is displayed.

In terms of database relationships, this operation depends on a valid `discussion_board_articles` record and an associated `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` record for the given article. If the article was instead authored by an admin user, its authorship will be represented in `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers` and this member-author endpoint should respond as if no member author exists for that article. Implementations should therefore distinguish between the following error scenarios: the article does not exist at all, the article exists but has no member authorship record, or the article has been removed according to content removal rules. Appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages should allow clients to understand why member author information is unavailable, while not leaking unnecessary internal details.

This endpoint will commonly be used alongside other article-related operations, such as retrieving article details (`GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`) and listing comments or attachments associated with the same article. Clients may first fetch the article, and then call this endpoint to render a dedicated author panel that specifically reflects the member user who created it when applicable.

The backend then resolve the relevant `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers` record and, based on that, fetches the associated admin user profile.

From a security and governance perspective, the response must be limited to admin profile information that is intended for public exposure as an article author. This may include admin display name, title or role labels, and other non-sensitive metadata that conveys the administrator's status or function on the board. Internal-only fields such as privileged access scopes, internal staff notes, or contact information not meant for end users must never be included. Because the endpoint is read-only and only returns information that would normally be visible wherever admin-authored articles are presented, it can typically be made publicly accessible.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the current like engagement state for a specific discussion board article based on the underlying `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma model. It is designed to answer the question "has the current member already liked this article, and what is the current like count?" in a single, efficient call.

The operation targets records in the `discussion_board_article_likes` table, which represents per-member like engagement for articles in the economic and political discussion board. Each row in that table typically links a `discussion_board_memberusers` record to a `discussion_board_articles` record, reflecting that a particular member has expressed a like for that article. The aggregate like count for an article may be derived either by counting rows in this table for the article, or by a dedicated counter field on the article itself; this operation is responsible for exposing that information at the API layer, not for defining the storage strategy.

From a business perspective, this API is used by clients when rendering an article detail view or an article list card, so that they can display both the total number of likes and whether the currently authenticated member has already liked the article. If the requester is not authenticated as a member user, the operation still returns the article's like count while indicating that there is no member-specific like state. The article is identified by its UUID-based `articleId` path parameter, which corresponds directly to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` table.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any state in `discussion_board_article_likes` or related tables. It simply combines per-article aggregation from `discussion_board_article_likes` with article metadata from `discussion_board_articles`, and optionally the current member's like record, into a single DTO defined as `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike`. This DTO is expected to include fields such as the article identifier, total like count, and a boolean indicating whether the current member has liked the article.

The primary consumers of this endpoint are authenticated member users browsing the board, but the endpoint is also safe for public access if the service chooses to expose like counts publicly. Authorization is therefore modeled using the `memberUser` actor, leaving finer-grained role and visibility checks to downstream business logic and middleware.
operations.description:
Retrieve the like engagement state and count for a single discussion board article.

This operation reads from the `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma table, which stores per-member like records for articles, and from the `discussion_board_articles` table, which stores the core article metadata such as identifiers, titles, and category references. For the article identified by the `articleId` path parameter, the system computes the total number of active like records associated with that article and determines whether the current authenticated member user has a corresponding like entry.

In typical schema designs, `discussion_board_article_likes` will contain foreign keys referencing `discussion_board_articles` and `discussion_board_memberusers`, along with timestamp fields for when the like was created. The like operation is conceptually idempotent per member–article pair, and the database layer will usually enforce a uniqueness constraint on that pair. This read operation relies on those constraints to treat the presence or absence of a row as the authoritative source of truth for whether the member has liked the article.

Security-wise, this API does not expose any sensitive personal information. It returns only aggregate counts and a boolean flag `likedByCurrentMember` (or similarly named field) that indicates whether the caller, as identified from the session and associated `discussion_board_memberusers` record, has liked the target article. If the caller is unauthenticated or not a member user, the service implementation should treat the member context as absent and always return `false` for the member-specific like flag while still returning the global like count. Access control on which articles may be visible is enforced consistently with the visibility rules defined on `discussion_board_articles`.

From a validation perspective, the `articleId` path parameter must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing article row in `discussion_board_articles`. If the article does not exist, the service should respond with a not-found error. If the article exists but has no associated like records in `discussion_board_article_likes`, the operation returns a like count of zero. Because this is a read operation, it does not create or modify any records in `discussion_board_article_likes`.

Clients typically call this endpoint together with the article detail retrieval API (such as `GET /articles/{articleId}`) when rendering an article detail page. However, this endpoint can be cached or optimized independently because it focuses solely on engagement metrics. Error handling should clearly distinguish between invalid identifiers, missing articles, and internal server errors in the aggregation process.

operations.specification:
This operation toggles or sets the like state of the current authenticated member user for a specific article by creating or confirming a record in the `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma model. It implements the core engagement behavior of the discussion board, allowing members to express appreciation for economic and political discussion articles.

At the persistence layer, the `discussion_board_article_likes` table represents a many-to-many-like relationship between `discussion_board_memberusers` and `discussion_board_articles`. Each record typically contains a foreign key to a member user, a foreign key to an article, and timestamp metadata such as when the like was created. A uniqueness constraint on the combination of member user and article ensures that a member cannot register duplicate likes for the same article. This create operation will either insert such a record if the member has not yet liked the article or be implemented as idempotent if the like already exists.

The endpoint treats the authenticated actor as a member user derived from the session context, rather than trusting any user identifiers in the request body. The article itself is identified by the `articleId` path parameter, which maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` table. The request body, defined by `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike.ICreate`, may include optional metadata such as the client source or additional context, but it must not override the member or article identifiers controlled by the path and authentication context.

This operation is write-sensitive and requires an authenticated `memberUser` actor representing a valid `discussion_board_memberusers` record. It validates that the target article exists and is in a state that can accept likes (for example, not deleted or archived) before attempting to create the like record. If the member has already liked the article and the database enforces uniqueness, the implementation should either return the existing like state or simply succeed without creating a duplicate record, depending on the service's idempotency policy.

Error handling includes responding with not-found errors when the article does not exist, authorization errors when the caller is not authenticated as a member user, and conflict or generic errors if the uniqueness constraint is violated in a way that cannot be resolved automatically. On success, the operation returns the resulting like engagement state encapsulated in the `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike` DTO, which includes fields such as the article identifier, member identifier, and updated like count if the service chooses to compute and include it. The operation should be treated as idempotent at the business level: multiple calls when a like already exists must not create duplicate like records.

This operation is typically used in tandem with a complementary endpoint that allows unliking an article (often implemented as `DELETE /articles/{articleId}/likes`), as well as with the read-only like information retrieval endpoint defined at `GET /discussionBoard/memberUser/articles/{articleId}/likes`. Together, these APIs provide a complete like engagement feature for the discussion board.
operations.description:
Create or confirm a like engagement from the current member user for a specific discussion board article.

This operation operates primarily on the `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma model, which records individual member likes for articles in the discussion board. The endpoint uses the `articleId` path parameter to identify the article in `discussion_board_articles` and the authenticated session to identify the member user in `discussion_board_memberusers`. It then attempts to create a new like record in `discussion_board_article_likes` linking those two entities, or confirm the existing like in an idempotent way.

The associated Prisma schema for `discussion_board_article_likes` typically includes fields such as a primary key, foreign keys to the article and member user, and timestamps like `created_at`. A uniqueness constraint on the member–article pair (field names may vary) ensures that each member can only have a single like per article. The implementation of this API must respect that constraint by either checking for an existing record before insertion or handling uniqueness errors from the database in an idempotent manner.

Security and authorization are critical: only authenticated member users are allowed to like articles. The `authorizationActor` for this operation is therefore set to `memberUser`, with the expectation that downstream authentication middleware maps this to a valid `discussion_board_memberusers` record. The request body type `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike.ICreate` must not include member identifiers that could be used to impersonate another user; instead, the service ignores any such fields and uses the authenticated principal from the session.

Validation rules include verifying that the `articleId` path parameter is a valid UUID for an existing record in `discussion_board_articles`, and that the article is not in a state where likes are disallowed (for example, removed content according to moderation rules stored in related tables such as `discussion_board_reports`). If validation fails, the service returns appropriate error responses. On success, the operation returns an `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike` DTO reflecting the current like state for the member and article, which clients can use to update UI elements such as like buttons and counters.

This operation is typically used in tandem with a complementary endpoint that allows unliking an article (often implemented as `DELETE /articles/{articleId}/likes`), as well as with the read-only like information retrieval endpoint defined at `GET /discussionBoard/memberUser/articles/{articleId}/likes`. Together, these APIs provide a complete like engagement feature for the discussion board.

Delete an existing like record for a specific article by the currently authenticated member user, operating on the discussion_board_article_likes table. This endpoint models the "unlike" action, where a member removes their previous like from an article.

The operation will locate the like row in discussion_board_article_likes by combining the article identifier from the path parameter and the member user identifier derived from the authenticated session context (not from the URL). Because the Prisma schema is expected to enforce a unique composite index on (discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_memberuser_id), there can be at most one such row per member per article, so deletion is unambiguous.

On success, the API permanently removes the like row from the table. Since likes are engagement events and not subject to the content-level logical deletion rules that may be used for articles and member accounts, a hard delete is appropriate. The endpoint does not return a body; clients can infer success from the HTTP status and may subsequently refresh like counts via separate read endpoints implemented elsewhere.
operations.description:
Perform an "unlike" operation by deleting the existing like record for the target article in the discussion_board_article_likes table.

This operation is intended for authenticated member users who previously liked a given article and now want to remove that like. The path parameter carries the articleId, which corresponds to discussion_board_articles.id. The service also uses the authenticated member user's id from the session (mapped to discussion_board_memberusers.id) to find the exact like row. It then deletes the matching record in discussion_board_article_likes, leveraging the unique composite constraint on (discussion_board_article_id, discussion_board_memberuser_id) to guarantee that at most one record is affected.

From a security and authorization perspective, only the member user who created the like (or system-level administrative logic) should be allowed to remove it. The controller layer is expected to ensure that the authenticated principal is a member user and to pass the correct member user id into the provider. Admin users generally moderate content but do not need independent ownership over likes, so this endpoint is modeled for member actors. If the like does not exist, the implementation should return an appropriate not-found or idempotent success response according to service-wide conventions.

This deletion does not modify article content or member user records themselves. It only removes an engagement row from discussion_board_article_likes and may indirectly affect derived metrics such as like counts that are computed or materialized elsewhere. Related operations include the "like" creation endpoint (POST /articles/{articleId}/likes if defined) and list or detail endpoints that expose article like counts or whether the current member has liked a specific article. operations.specification:
Search and retrieve a paginated list of articles that a specific member user has liked, using the discussion_board_article_likes table as the primary source and joining to discussion_board_articles for article details. This endpoint exposes the "liked articles" view for a member's profile or history page.

The operation accepts a memberUserId path parameter, which corresponds to discussion_board_memberusers.id, and uses it to filter discussion_board_article_likes on discussion_board_memberuser_id. It then joins to discussion_board_articles via discussion_board_article_likes.discussion_board_article_id = discussion_board_articles.id to select article information for each like. The request body carries search and pagination criteria (sorting by creation date, filtering by category, moderation_state, or text fields) represented by the DTO IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.

The response returns a paginated list of article summaries in IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary, where each entry represents one liked article. While the likes table includes created_at for the engagement event itself, the summary focuses on article-level fields (title, category, moderation state), with sorting options configured via the request DTO. This endpoint can be used for "articles I liked" sections in the UI, profile pages, or analytics screens.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of articles that a given member user has liked by querying the discussion_board_article_likes and discussion_board_articles tables.

This operation is designed to support the "liked articles" view for a member user. The path parameter memberUserId identifies the member account in discussion_board_memberusers.id, and the backend filters discussion_board_article_likes on discussion_board_memberuser_id to find all like records for that member. For each like, the implementation joins to discussion_board_articles through the foreign key discussion_board_article_id to obtain the associated article. Articles that have been logically deleted or are in a non-visible moderation_state can be filtered out based on business rules, using the deleted_at and moderation_state fields defined on discussion_board_articles.

The request body follows the IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest schema and can express pagination, sorting, and filtering options. Typical filters include article category (via discussion_board_article_category_id), moderation_state constraints (such as only "Active" articles), and text search over title or body (supported by GIN indexes on these fields). Pagination parameters allow the client to scroll through liked articles in a stable order (for example, sorted by article created_at or by like created_at, depending on how IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest is designed). The endpoint responds with IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary, a paginated list of article summary objects optimized for list displays.

From a security perspective, this operation is restricted to authenticated member users. The memberUserId path parameter may represent either the current member viewing their own likes or another member whose public liked-articles list is being inspected, depending on business rules about profile visibility. The controller is responsible for enforcing whether a member can view another member's liked articles, using account_status and other profile fields from discussion_board_memberusers as needed. Errors should clearly differentiate between nonexistent member ids, members that exist but whose liked-articles list is not visible, and internal database or validation issues. Related operations include the like/unlike endpoints for individual articles and general article search endpoints that do not filter by likes.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of comments belonging to a single discussion article.

This operation reads from the discussion_board_comments table, which stores top-level text comments attached directly to discussion board articles. Each comment row includes the foreign key discussion_board_article_id referencing discussion_board_articles.id, the author_type discriminator for distinguishing member and admin authors, the body text, status, and lifecycle timestamps such as created_at and updated_at.

At minimum, the implementation must filter by discussion_board_article_id corresponding to the articleId path parameter so that only comments for the specified article are returned. Additional filtering based on the logical status of the comment should be applied in business logic so that callers only see comments that are considered visible according to the service’s moderation and visibility rules (for example, comments that have not been hidden or removed). Depending on configuration, privileged callers may be allowed to see additional statuses such as hidden or removed comments.

The request body uses the IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest DTO to carry pagination parameters (such as page index and page size), sorting options (for example, sort by created_at ascending to show oldest first or descending for newest first), and optional search criteria like text search against the body column. Internally, the core comment data is stored in the `discussion_board_comments` table, which contains fields such as the textual content, timestamps created by the database or application layer, and any structural relationships like parent comment references if nested discussions are supported. The request body is represented by the `IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate` DTO, which encapsulates only the fields that clients are allowed to set, such as comment content and, when supported, a parent comment identifier for replies. Fields that are system-managed—such as primary keys, creation timestamps, and foreign keys to the article and author—are populated by the service based on the path parameter and the authenticated user context rather than being supplied directly by the caller.

Authorization logic in the provider ensures that blocked or restricted accounts, as defined by the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` model, cannot create new comments even if they are nominally authenticated. On success, the API returns a fully populated `IDiscussionBoardComment` DTO representing the newly created comment, including core fields like identifier, content, creation timestamp, and any lightweight projections of related entities that the DTO defines (for example, minimal article and author information). Clients typically call this operation after retrieving article details via an article retrieval endpoint and then refresh the article’s comment list—via a separate comment listing or article detail API—to display the new comment in context. operations.specification:
This operation updates an existing top-level text comment associated with a discussion board article. It primarily manipulates the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model and, depending on ownership and auditing design, may reference `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` to verify the author and enforce permission rules.

The comment to update is uniquely identified by the combination of the `articleId` and `commentId` path parameters. The `articleId` parameter maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` table and is used to ensure that the specified comment actually belongs to the given article, preventing cross-article tampering. The `commentId` parameter maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_comments` table. When the request arrives, the service first loads the existing comment row and validates that both identifiers match the stored foreign key relationships.

The request body uses the `IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate` DTO, which reflects the updatable fields of the `discussion_board_comments` table—typically the textual content and possibly some flags such as whether the comment is marked as edited. System-managed fields like identifiers, creation timestamps, and article association are not directly writable and must not be altered by the client. The service logic enforces these constraints by only mapping allowed fields from the DTO to the underlying Prisma update operation.

Authorization and ownership enforcement are central to this operation. The service checks whether the authenticated actor is the original author of the comment (by inspecting ownership information from `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` or `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`) or an administrator with elevated moderation permissions. Requirements and Prisma schema comments for related restriction models, such as `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions`, must be consulted to ensure that restricted members cannot edit their comments and that admins follow the moderation policy for editing other users’ content.

On success, the operation returns an updated `IDiscussionBoardComment` DTO that contains the latest state of the comment, reflecting all changes applied through the update. This enables clients to immediately refresh their user interface without requiring an additional fetch call. If either the article or comment cannot be found, a 404 error is returned. If the authenticated user lacks permission to modify the comment, the service responds with a suitable 403 status, and validation failures in the request body yield 400-level responses with detailed error messages.
operations.description:
Update an existing comment that belongs to a specific discussion board article.

This operation enables an authenticated user—either the original member author or a privileged administrator—to modify the content of a comment that has previously been created on a discussion board article. The target comment is located using the `articleId` and `commentId` path parameters, which map respectively to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` model and the primary key of the `discussion_board_comments` model. By requiring both identifiers, the API ensures that the comment being updated is indeed associated with the specified article, protecting against accidental or malicious updates across article boundaries.

The request body is represented by the `IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate` DTO, which corresponds to the subset of `discussion_board_comments` fields that are allowed to change after creation. In most cases this will include the textual content of the comment and potentially an `edited` flag or similar metadata, while immutable fields like the comment’s identifier, original creation timestamp, and foreign keys to the article and author remain untouched. The service maps only these permitted fields to the underlying Prisma update on the `discussion_board_comments` table, thereby honoring the schema’s non-null and length constraints as described in its comments.

Ownership and permission checks are enforced using the ownership subtype tables `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`, along with any restriction information from `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions`. For member-authored comments, the service verifies that the current authenticated member user matches the owner recorded in the corresponding subtype row and that the account is not currently restricted from editing content. For administrator-authored comments, or when admins are allowed to edit member comments for moderation purposes, the service ensures that the authenticated admin user has appropriate privileges according to the moderation rules defined in the requirements and schema documentation.

The endpoint is secured for authenticated actors only, with `authorizationActors` indicating that both member and admin roles may access it, though their effective permissions differ according to business rules. On success, the API returns the updated `IDiscussionBoardComment` DTO reflecting the latest persisted state, allowing clients to update the displayed comment in place. Error responses include 404 when either the article or comment cannot be found, 403 for insufficient permissions or restrictions, and 400-level responses for invalid update payloads—such as content that violates length limits or other validation rules derived from the Prisma schema comments.

From a business perspective, this deletion is intended for cases where a comment must be removed due to user request, policy violations, or administrative moderation actions. Security and authorization are enforced based on the caller's ability to view the underlying article: only callers who can see the article should be allowed to list its attachments.

The operation complements other attachment-related endpoints such as uploading attachments when creating or editing an article and downloading a single attachment. operations.description:

When PUT /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} is called, the implementation must validate both articleId and attachmentId as UUIDs and then fetch the attachment whose id equals attachmentId and whose discussion_board_article_id equals articleId. If no such combination exists, the API should respond with an error indicating that the attachment is not found in the context of that article. The controller should therefore require authentication for memberUser and adminUser actors and pass the authenticated principal into business logic, which will check ownership or role permissions before applying updates. This operation is typically used alongside a creation endpoint like POST /articles/{articleId}/attachments for adding new attachments, retrieval endpoints that list or show attachments for an article, and the DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} operation that removes an attachment from active use by marking it deleted according to the deleted_at semantics present in the Prisma schema.

operations.description:

Authorization components should therefore enforce roles for memberUser and adminUser and then delegate more granular checks (like ownership) to the domain service. The response will return a paginated list of session summaries using the IPageIDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISummary type so that clients can display concise session rows without transferring all detailed fields.

This operation is read-only with respect to the underlying sessions; it does not create, update, or delete session entries. Its main purpose is to support features like "view all sessions for this member" pages and security dashboards, where an admin user or potentially the member themselves can review active or historical sessions and decide whether to terminate one via a separate dedicated revoke operation. Because session lifecycle management (creation, refresh, revocation) is owned by a specialized authentication subsystem, this API strictly lists sessions already recorded in the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table and must not assume control over token issuance or invalidation.

Within that scope, the request body uses the IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.IRequest structure to specify search filters, date range constraints, sorting options, and pagination parameters so that callers can efficiently navigate a potentially large set of sessions for a single member.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation should typically be accessible either to privileged administrative actors responsible for monitoring account activity, or to the member user themself when viewing their own account security page. The exact enforcement of whether a given caller is allowed to see another member's sessions is handled in business logic based on the authenticated principal and the memberUserId path parameter. For revoking or invalidating sessions, separate dedicated operations must be used that interact with the underlying authentication and token infrastructure.

The operation reads the restriction row associated with the given memberUsers record and maps it into a IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction DTO. In the database design, discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions is a subsidiary model that tracks the restriction status for each discussion_board_memberusers account. Its fields typically include a foreign key to the member user, one or more flags or enumerations describing the restriction type (for example, read-only, comment-banned, or fully blocked), timestamps for when the restriction was applied and when it will expire, and optional descriptive fields explaining the reason or administrative decision behind the restriction. This API operation uses the memberUserId path parameter to locate the corresponding restriction record and returns it as an IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction representation.

From a security and permission perspective, this operation is intended primarily for authenticated member users to check their own restriction status before attempting actions such as posting an article or adding a comment. The authorizationActors array is therefore set to ["memberUser"], and business logic in the implementation must ensure that a member cannot read another member’s restriction details by enforcing that the path memberUserId matches the authenticated principal.

This operation is closely related to content moderation workflows described in the requirements. When admins impose or lift restrictions as a result of reports processed through the discussion_board_reports family of tables, the corresponding restriction record in discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions changes state. While those write operations are handled by dedicated moderation APIs, this read-only endpoint provides a simple way for member-facing clients to check the effective restriction state before allowing UI interactions, and it should handle missing records gracefully, for example by returning an indication that no restriction is currently applied when the schema or DTO supports such representation.

The implementation must enforce the unique index on discussion_board_memberuser_id, guaranteeing at most one restriction record per member user. If a restriction already exists, the provider should return a validation error and direct clients to the corresponding PUT endpoint instead of silently overwriting data.

The response body returns the created IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction entity, allowing administrative tools to display the current restriction state immediately after creation. Downstream article, comment, and attachment creation flows will check this restriction row to decide whether a member user is allowed to post or must be blocked according to the restriction_level and active window defined by started_at and ended_at.

Create a new restriction state for the specified member user in the discussionBoard system.

This endpoint is backed by the discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions table, whose schema description states that it represents the current restriction state for each memberUser account. The foreign key column discussion_board_memberuser_id (non-null and unique) references discussion_board_memberusers.id and ensures that there is at most one restriction record per member user. Additional plain fields include restriction_level, reason_category, started_at, ended_at, created_at, and updated_at. These fields collectively describe which moderation restriction applies, why it was applied, and over what time window it is effective.

When a client invokes this POST operation, it supplies a memberUserId path parameter that holds the UUID primary key of the target member user in the discussion_board_memberusers table. In the request body, the IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction.ICreate DTO must provide a restriction_level value such as posting_restriction or full_block, and a reason_category such as repeated_violations, hate_abuse, or spam_advertising. It must also specify started_at to mark when the restriction becomes effective. The ended_at field may be omitted or set to null to represent an ongoing restriction that is lifted later through updates.

From a security perspective, only administrative actors should be permitted to call this endpoint, because it directly affects member users’ ability to create articles, comments, and attachments. The provider implementation should validate that the referenced member user exists, that their current account state in discussion_board_memberusers allows restrictions to be applied, and that no existing restriction record already uses the same discussion_board_memberuser_id. If a restriction already exists, the service should reject the request, returning a clear error that the restriction must be modified via the PUT /memberUsers/{memberUserId}/restriction endpoint instead of creating a duplicate row.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with moderation and reporting flows that originate from the discussion_board_reports and related tables. After a restriction is created, other API operations that handle article and comment creation will consult the restriction_level and timing fields to decide whether to allow or block user-generated content. Error handling must cover cases such as invalid memberUserId, invalid or unsupported restriction_level or reason_category values, and database constraint violations on the unique index of discussion_board_memberuser_id. In such cases, no partial data should be persisted and the client should receive a descriptive message for corrective action.

When a client issues this PUT request, it supplies memberUserId as a path parameter representing the UUID primary key of the member user (discussion_board_memberusers.id). The service then resolves the corresponding restriction row where discussion_board_memberuser_id equals that memberUserId. The request body uses the IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction.IUpdate DTO to specify which fields should change, such as escalating the restriction_level from posting_restriction to full_block, adjusting reason_category after further review, or setting an ended_at timestamp to lift a restriction while keeping a historical record.

Access to this operation should be restricted to administrative actors responsible for content and account moderation. Implementations should validate that a restriction record actually exists for the given member user before applying updates; if none is found, the service should return an error indicating that the POST /memberUsers/{memberUserId}/restriction endpoint must be used to create one. Additional validation should ensure that updated values remain consistent with policy, such as verifying that ended_at is not earlier than started_at and that restriction_level and reason_category values fall within the supported set used across the moderation domain.

Because other parts of the system—especially article, comment, and attachment creation logic—depend on this restriction record to enforce posting permissions, any updates performed by this operation have immediate, system-wide impact. Error cases include attempts to update a non-existent restriction, providing invalid or unsupported values, or targeting a member user that does not exist or has been fully closed or deactivated in discussion_board_memberusers based on the account state and closure-related fields defined there. In such cases, the operation must fail cleanly, leaving existing restriction data unchanged and returning clear diagnostic information to the client.
