operations.specification:
This operation removes an existing restriction record associated with a specific member user in the discussion board domain. It targets the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` Prisma model, which stores the current restriction state for each member user account (for example, temporary bans or posting limitations).

The endpoint performs a hard delete of the restriction row for the given member user identifier, effectively lifting any active restriction and restoring the user's normal interaction capabilities defined elsewhere in the system. The implementation must verify that a restriction actually exists for the given member user; if not, it should return a suitable not-found error. Because this modifies user moderation state, it is restricted to administrative actors.

The operation does not require a request body; all required context is provided through the path parameter `memberUserId`, which is treated as the unique identifier of the target member user in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table. On success, it returns no content, signaling that any active restriction row for the member user has been removed from `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions`.
operations.description:
Remove the current restriction state record for a specific member user, thereby lifting any active restriction associated with that account.

This operation works against the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` Prisma table, which represents the current restriction state for each member user account. A row in this table typically indicates that the corresponding member user is under some form of restriction, such as being blocked from posting, commenting, or creating new content. By deleting the restriction row for the given member user, the system returns that user to an unrestricted state as far as the discussion board moderation rules are concerned.

From a security and authorization perspective, only administrative actors should be allowed to modify restriction states, because these changes directly influence a member user's ability to participate in the board. The underlying implementation must therefore enforce appropriate checks to ensure that only users with admin privileges can call this endpoint successfully. Member users themselves must not be permitted to lift their own restrictions.

In terms of database behavior, the operation performs a hard delete on the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` row associated with the specified `memberUserId`. If there is no existing restriction row for this member user, the service should return a not-found error or an equivalent response indicating that no active restriction exists. This operation is typically used together with the restriction creation or update endpoints that initially place a member user under restriction, forming part of the overall content moderation workflow for the discussion board.
operations.summary: Lift the current restriction for a member user by deleting its record in discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of report records for the discussion board service. It operates on the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model, which is the central entity representing a single user report about an article, comment, or attachment.

The endpoint uses the HTTP PATCH method to support complex search, filtering, and sorting criteria in the request body. Clients can supply parameters such as report status, target type (article, comment, attachment), reporter type (member user or admin user), creation date ranges, and pagination options. The system responds with a paginated collection of report summaries, optimized for administrative review and moderation workflows.

This operation is intended for administrative actors who manage reported content and must triage, inspect, and act upon reports. It does not modify any data in `discussion_board_reports` or its subsidiary link tables (`discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`, `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`, `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`); it only reads and aggregates information for listing and filtering. The response type returns summaries that may include basic information about the report, status, and target reference identifiers, suitable for listing screens and dashboard-like overviews.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of reports registered in the discussion board system for administrative review.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model, which stores central report records describing issues raised by users or administrators against specific pieces of content. Each report may be associated with an article, comment, or attachment through subsidiary link tables such as `discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, and `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`. Additional link tables like `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers` track whether a report was created by a member user or an admin user.

The endpoint accepts a rich set of search criteria in the request body, allowing administrators to filter reports by status (for example, open, in review, resolved), target type, reporter type, and creation or update time ranges. Pagination parameters such as page index and page size enable efficient browsing of large report volumes, and sorting options can be used to prioritize more recent or more severe reports. This design lets moderation staff quickly find the most urgent or relevant reports to act upon.

Security-wise, access to this operation is restricted to administrative actors because reports often contain sensitive information about user behavior, policy violations, and potentially problematic content. The implementation must enforce that only adminUser actors can invoke this API successfully. The operation is read-only and does not change the state of reports or associated content; it is typically used alongside detail retrieval and update endpoints that allow admins to inspect and resolve individual reports.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of discussion_board_reports for moderation purposes.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of discussion board report summaries matching the given search and filter criteria.

operations.specification:
Retrieve detailed information about a single discussion board report from the Prisma model "discussion_board_reports". This operation reads one record identified by its primary key and returns all relevant fields, including relationships to associated article, comment, attachment, and reporting actor link entities, as defined in the Prisma schema. It is a read-only operation intended for administrative review of how a particular report was filed and its current handling status.

The operation will use the unique report identifier as a path parameter. It must not modify any data in the reports or related tables. Instead, it focuses on presenting a comprehensive view of the report for moderation purposes, potentially including status, reason, timestamps, and references to target content and reporter link records, depending on how the schema is structured.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single discussion board report record for detailed inspection by an authorized actor.

This operation targets the Prisma table that stores central report metadata for articles, comments, and attachments. It looks up the report using its unique identifier and returns the full report object shaped as `IDiscussionBoardReport`. The description and field coverage must align with the Prisma schema comments for `discussion_board_reports`, including fields such as status, category, reason text, timestamps, and any foreign keys to link tables that connect the report to articles, comments, attachments, and reporting users.

From a security perspective, this endpoint should be restricted to administrative or internal moderation tooling, because reports may contain sensitive notes, internal status, or personal information about reporters or reported users. The `authorizationActors` will therefore use the `adminUser` role rather than generic end users. The implementation must enforce that only appropriately authenticated and authorized actors can read this data, while normal board visitors or member users cannot fetch arbitrary reports.

The operation is purely read-only and does not change any state in the `discussion_board_reports` table or its related entities. It should be used together with the listing and search endpoint on reports (for example, a future `PATCH /reports` search) where moderators first narrow down to a set of reports and then call this detail endpoint for a specific `reportId`. Error handling should clearly distinguish between a missing report (not found), lack of permission (forbidden), and other server-side issues.
operations.summary: Get detailed information of a single report from discussion_board_reports

operations.specification:
Create a new discussion board report record in the Prisma model "discussion_board_reports" when a user reports problematic content. This operation is responsible for inserting a central report entity that captures what is being reported (article, comment, or attachment) and the high-level reason/category, plus any free-text explanation, according to the schema comments.

The detailed associations to specific articles, comments, attachments, or reporting users may be handled by subsidiary link tables such as `discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`, `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`, and `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`. The DTO type `IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate` is expected to encapsulate the required data for creating the primary report and any necessary linkage information, following the database design.

This is a write operation that must validate input based on the Prisma field definitions (for example, enumerated categories, length limits on reason text, and required foreign keys). It should not allow callers to manipulate internal moderation status fields that are reserved for administrators; those are managed by separate admin-only operations if defined.
operations.description:
Create a new discussion board report describing problematic content on the board.

This operation writes to the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma table, which centralizes each report filed by a user or admin about an article, comment, or attachment. The request body is shaped as `IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate` and must include all data required by the schema comments, such as the report category, description, and identifiers that indicate which content is being reported. The service will translate these fields into an inserted row in `discussion_board_reports` and may also populate related link entities like `discussion_board_report_of_articles` or `discussion_board_report_of_comments` depending on which target type is specified.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is typically callable by authenticated member users who wish to report content, and may also be used by administrators filing reports for tracking purposes. The implementation must not expose or allow setting internal moderation-only fields such as resolution notes or final status at creation time; those are updated later by separate admin workflows. The endpoint should also implement validation logic based on the schema: enforcing maximum lengths on reason text, verifying that referenced articles, comments, or attachments exist and are in a reportable state, and rejecting malformed or contradictory combinations (for example, specifying both article and comment targets when only one is allowed).

This creation endpoint is usually used in conjunction with moderation views that list and inspect reports. Once a report is created through `POST /reports`, administrators will later retrieve it (for example, using `GET /reports/{reportId}`) to review, triage, and resolve the reported issue. Error handling must clearly communicate validation failures to the caller and avoid leaking internal moderation details in user-facing error messages.

operations.specification:
Update an existing discussion board report record in the Prisma table `discussion_board_reports`. This operation allows authorized administrative users (modeled as `discussion_board_adminusers`) to modify the status, resolution details, and moderator notes of a user-submitted report about an article, comment, or attachment. It is strictly aligned with the fields actually defined in the `discussion_board_reports` model and must not assume any additional audit or deletion-related fields beyond what exists in that schema.

The endpoint uses the path parameter `reportId` to identify the specific report record. The request body is defined by the DTO type `IDiscussionBoardReport.IUpdate`, which exposes only the mutable fields of the report, such as status, resolution category, resolution message, and any administrative memo fields determined by the Prisma model. The service implementation must validate that requested status transitions comply with the business rules defined in the moderation and reporting requirements, for example allowing transitions from pending to resolved or dismissed, and optionally preventing modification once a report is finalized.

On success, this operation responds with the fully updated report resource using the DTO type `IDiscussionBoardReport`. This representation reflects the latest status and moderation metadata stored in `discussion_board_reports`, and the service layer may enrich it with related entities (such as links from subsidiary tables like `discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, or `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`) according to read-model design. Security-wise, the endpoint is restricted to the `adminUser` actor, and member users cannot modify report records directly.
operations.description:
Update the status and moderation details of a specific discussion board report record identified by `reportId`.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model, which serves as the central entity for all reports filed against articles, comments, or attachments on the economic and political discussion board. Each report typically stores information such as the reporting actor, a reference to the reported resource, the reason category, free-text description, and the current handling status. Administrators, represented by the `discussion_board_adminusers` table in the database, use this endpoint to progress a report through its lifecycle when they review and act upon the reported content.

The request body type `IDiscussionBoardReport.IUpdate` is designed to include only those fields that may change after the report is first created, such as the moderation status (for example, pending, inReview, resolved, dismissed), resolution notes, or outcome codes. Fields that identify the reporter or the target resource remain immutable and are therefore not part of the update DTO. The implementation must check that the given `reportId` corresponds to an existing record, and that the requested update is compatible with any status-transition rules defined in the reporting and moderation requirements.

Only administrative users should be allowed to perform this action. Accordingly, `authorizationActors` is set to `["adminUser"]`, meaning the controller layer will require authentication as an admin user and inject the corresponding identity into the service. If the `reportId` does not exist, the provider should respond with a not-found error. If the update violates domain rules (for example, attempting to modify a locked or archived report), the provider should respond with an appropriate error describing why the operation cannot be completed. This endpoint is expected to be used together with report listing and detail retrieval APIs that admins rely on to triage and review reported content.

operations.specification:
Permanently delete an existing discussion board report record from the Prisma table `discussion_board_reports`. This operation removes the core report entity for a given `reportId` and is intended for exceptional administrative cleanup scenarios, such as removing duplicated or test reports, in accordance with the reporting and retention requirements. Because the schema for `discussion_board_reports` may or may not define archival or status flags, this API is designed as a hard delete that directly removes the row, rather than relying on any implied soft-deletion mechanism.

The endpoint uses the `reportId` path parameter to identify the report to be removed. There is no request body. When invoked, the service must delete the row from `discussion_board_reports` and handle any dependent records in subsidiary models such as `discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`, `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`, and `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers` according to the relational constraints configured in Prisma (for example, via cascading deletes or explicit manual cleanup). The API’s responsibility is limited to guaranteeing that once the operation succeeds, the specified report record no longer exists in the system.

Due to the sensitive nature of moderation history, this capability is restricted to the `adminUser` actor and should be governed by clear operational policies. Many systems choose to retain reports indefinitely; in this design, the presence of this endpoint implies that the requirements allow removal under certain circumstances. Implementations should therefore consider extra guardrails such as only deleting reports in resolved or dismissed states, or logging the deletion decision in a separate audit facility if such a mechanism exists outside this schema. The endpoint returns no response body; clients rely on the success status code to confirm that the resource has been removed.
operations.description:
Delete a specific discussion board report record from the `discussion_board_reports` table using its `reportId` as identifier.

This operation directly targets the central reporting entity used to track complaints about articles, comments, or attachments on the discussion board. Each record in `discussion_board_reports` corresponds to a single report instance. When administrators decide that some reports must be removed entirely—for example, because they were created during testing, are exact duplicates created by mistake, or must be purged under a data retention policy—they can call this endpoint to erase the associated record.

Only administrative users represented by `discussion_board_adminusers` are allowed to perform this deletion, which is reflected by setting `authorizationActors` to `["adminUser"]`. The service must ensure that the provided `reportId` matches an existing report before attempting deletion and should respond with an appropriate not-found error when no such record exists. If the report is linked to other rows in subsidiary tables, the implementation must conform to the configured Prisma relations, either relying on cascade rules or performing explicit cleanup to maintain referential integrity. Because the primary signal of success is the HTTP status code indicating that the delete operation completed, the response body is left null.
operations.summary: Delete a discussion board report in the `discussion_board_reports` table by reportId.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the full report information for a single discussion board report that targets an article, including the core report fields from the discussion_board_reports table and the associated article link from the discussion_board_report_of_articles table.

This GET operation is designed as a detail retrieval endpoint for moderation and audit workflows. Given a specific reportId (UUID primary key of discussion_board_reports), it loads the corresponding report row and joins it with the article link row in discussion_board_report_of_articles when the report's target_type indicates an article. The resulting DTO, IDiscussionBoardReportOfArticle, is expected to expose both the base report metadata (reason_code, description, status, action, reporter_type, timestamps) and the article association (discussion_board_article_id and related minimal article context if defined at DTO level).

The endpoint is read-only and does not modify any data in either table. It is intended for use by administrative actors reviewing the queue of article reports. Application logic must handle cases where a report exists but does not have an article link (e.g., if target_type is not "article"), by returning an appropriate error such as 404 or a domain-specific validation error. No request body is required, and the response is a single aggregated object, not a collection.

This operation is directly associated with the discussion_board_reports table as the primary entity and the discussion_board_report_of_articles table as a subsidiary link entity. It must never create, update, or delete report rows, in line with the schema description that reports are append-only audit records.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single discussion board report that targets an article, combining the core report record from discussion_board_reports with its article association from discussion_board_report_of_articles.

The underlying discussion_board_reports table is the central entity representing a single user report about an article, comment, or attachment. Each row stores the primary key id, target_type discriminator, reporter_type discriminator, reason_code, optional free-text description, status, action, and created_at and updated_at timestamps. The schema comments state that this table is used as the primary moderation queue and that reports are append-only audit records whose lifecycle is independent from the target content and reporting account. This endpoint respects that model by performing only read operations.

To represent article-specific targeting, the discussion_board_report_of_articles subsidiary table links a single report to a specific article through the discussion_board_report_id and discussion_board_article_id foreign keys. According to its schema description, each link row enforces a 1:1 association between a report and an article while allowing many reports per article overall. The created_at column on the link row captures when this association was created, typically mirroring the report creation time.

When this endpoint is called with a reportId path parameter, the implementation must first look up the corresponding row in discussion_board_reports. It should validate that the report exists and that it is conceptually an article-targeting report, which may be inferred both from target_type (expected to be "article") and the presence of a link row in discussion_board_report_of_articles. If no report is found, or if the report does not have a corresponding article link, the API should return a 404 or a well-defined domain error rather than a partial or misleading payload.

Security-wise, this operation is designed primarily for administrator actors who perform moderation tasks. The schema for discussion_board_reports mentions reporter_type with values such as "memberuser" and "adminuser" and workflow-oriented status and action fields such as "submitted", "in_review", "resolved" and "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", "restrict_user". The endpoint should not be exposed as a public read for all users, because report records often contain sensitive information about accusations, abuse, and internal moderation decisions.

This operation is typically used after a list or queue endpoint that searches and paginates reports, for example a PATCH /reports operation that returns summary information from discussion_board_reports. A moderator would first filter the queue, and then call this GET /reports/{reportId}/article endpoint for article-targeting reports to inspect the full context. Error handling should clearly distinguish between missing reports, reports that exist but are not article-type, and internal server failures, enabling moderation tooling to present appropriate feedback.

As specified in the Prisma schema comments, this endpoint must not attempt to modify the status or action fields; those changes should be handled by dedicated update operations. It also must not create or remove link rows in discussion_board_report_of_articles. Its sole responsibility is to return a single IDiscussionBoardReportOfArticle DTO that faithfully reflects the current state of both the base report and its article association.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the full report information for a single discussion board report that targets a comment, including the core report fields from the discussion_board_reports table and the associated comment link from the discussion_board_report_of_comments table.

This GET operation is designed as a detail retrieval endpoint for moderation and audit workflows focused on reported comments. Given a specific reportId (UUID primary key of discussion_board_reports), it loads the corresponding report row and joins it with the comment link row in discussion_board_report_of_comments when the report's target_type indicates a comment. The resulting DTO, IDiscussionBoardReportOfComment, is expected to expose both the base report metadata (reason_code, description, status, action, reporter_type, timestamps) and the comment association (discussion_board_comment_id and any attached comment context defined at DTO level).

The endpoint is strictly read-only and does not modify any data in either table. It is intended for use by administrative actors reviewing comment reports. Application logic must handle cases where the report exists but is not associated with a comment (for example, target_type is "article" or "attachment") by returning an appropriate error such as 404 or a domain-specific validation error. No request body is required, and the response is a single aggregated object.

This operation is directly associated with the discussion_board_reports table as the primary entity and the discussion_board_report_of_comments table as a subsidiary link entity. It must never create, update, or delete report rows or link rows, which is consistent with the schema description that reports function as append-only audit records within the moderation system.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a single discussion board report that targets a comment, combining the core report record from discussion_board_reports with its comment association from discussion_board_report_of_comments.

The discussion_board_reports table stores the central representation of user reports against various content types. Each row includes the id primary key, a target_type discriminator (with values such as "article", "comment", or "attachment"), a reporter_type discriminator (for example "memberuser" or "adminuser"), a reason_code for the primary reason category, an optional free-text description, a workflow-oriented status (for example "submitted", "in_review", "resolved"), an action describing the administrative decision (for example "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", "restrict_user"), and created_at and updated_at timestamps. The schema description emphasizes that this table drives moderation queues and that reports operate as append-only audit records.

To capture which specific comment was targeted, the discussion_board_report_of_comments subsidiary table associates a single report with a single comment via discussion_board_report_id and discussion_board_comment_id. According to its Prisma description, this table enforces a 1:1 relationship between a report and a comment while still allowing many reports against the same comment, and it records its own created_at timestamp for the association.

When a client invokes this endpoint with a reportId, the service implementation must first resolve that id against discussion_board_reports. It must then verify that the report corresponds to a comment target, both logically by checking target_type (expected "comment") and structurally by verifying the existence of an association row in discussion_board_report_of_comments. If no report is found, or if the report does not have a matching comment association, the endpoint should return a 404 or a clearly defined domain error rather than a malformed or partially populated DTO.

The description of discussion_board_reports makes clear that reports may contain sensitive details and internal moderation decisions. Therefore, this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors responsible for moderation. It should not be exposed for general browsing or to regular members. Access control must ensure that only authorized admins can inspect the details of comment reports.

Typical usage involves first listing or searching reports through a separate index endpoint, then calling this GET /reports/{reportId}/comment operation when a moderator selects a specific comment-targeting report. The response IDiscussionBoardReportOfComment object should reflect the current state of both the report and its comment association at the time of retrieval. Error handling should distinguish cleanly between "report not found", "report not a comment report", and unexpected server failures so that moderation tools can present appropriate messaging.

In alignment with the Prisma schema documentation, this operation must not alter the status, action, or any other fields of the underlying report or association. Changes to moderation decisions belong in dedicated update operations, and any creation of reports or associations must be handled through separate endpoints and workflows.
operations.summary: Get a single comment-targeting report from discussion_board_reports with its comment link from discussion_board_report_of_comments.

operations.specification:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific discussion board report's attachment entity, using the report's identifier as input. This operation is primarily associated with the Prisma table `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`, which links a central report record from `discussion_board_reports` to a concrete attachment record from `discussion_board_attachments`. The purpose is to allow moderators or administrative users to inspect the exact file attachment that was reported, together with its contextual metadata, without needing to manually join tables on the client side.

The endpoint accepts a single path parameter `reportId`, which represents the unique identifier of a report stored in the `discussion_board_reports` table. Internally, the implementation will look up the corresponding `discussion_board_report_of_attachments` row for that report, then resolve the associated `discussion_board_attachments` record that contains file name, URI, content type, size, and linkage back to the owning article. If the report is not of type "attachment" or has no linked attachment record, the service should return a not-found error.

The response returns an enriched view type `IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IInvert`, which composes the link entity together with the underlying attachment and the parent report in a convenient structure. This invert-oriented DTO allows the client to see, in one call, which attachment was reported, basic information about the report itself (such as reason, status, and timestamps), and essential attachment fields required for decision-making, while omitting any heavy collections that could cause circular references.
operations.description:
Retrieve the attachment information associated with a specific discussion board report.

This operation focuses on the `discussion_board_report_of_attachments` Prisma model, which is a subsidiary entity that connects a central report record from `discussion_board_reports` to an attachment stored in `discussion_board_attachments`. The link entity typically contains the foreign keys to both the report and the attachment and may include description comments clarifying that each report can point to exactly one attachment when the report target type is an attachment. By using the `reportId` path parameter, the server can efficiently locate the mapping row and then load the attachment metadata and relevant report details required for moderation.

From an authorization perspective, this endpoint is intended for administrative actors who are responsible for handling user reports and moderating content on the discussion board. The `authorizationActors` therefore contain `adminUser`, indicating that only authenticated admin-level users may access this detailed attachment-report relationship. Member users and guest users should not be able to inspect other users' reports or the detailed linkage between reports and attachments, as this would expose internal moderation workflows and potentially sensitive metadata.

In terms of data structure, the response uses the `IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IInvert` DTO, which is designed as an inverted composition view. Instead of the usual direction where an attachment might have a collection of related reports, this invert type centers around the report-to-attachment link and embeds a compact representation of the related report and the attachment. The underlying Prisma schema comments likely emphasize that heavy one-to-many collections must be trimmed from the parent entities to avoid circular references and unnecessary payload size, so the invert DTO should include only the necessary fields for decision-making, such as report reason, current status, createdAt/updatedAt timestamps, and the attachment's display name and URI.

Error handling should cover cases where the `reportId` does not exist in `discussion_board_reports`, where the report exists but has no associated `discussion_board_report_of_attachments` record, or where the linkage points to an attachment that has already been removed from `discussion_board_attachments`. In such scenarios, the implementation should return a 404-style not found response with a clear error message. This operation is typically used together with list operations on reports (for example, a search endpoint returning many reports) and other detail endpoints, such as viewing the reported article or comment, to give moderators a full picture of the incident they are reviewing.
operations.summary: Get the attachment link detail for a specific report from `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the reporting member user associated with a specific discussion board report using the report identifier as input. This operation is based on the Prisma subsidiary table `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`, which serves as a link between the central `discussion_board_reports` table and the reporting actor stored in `discussion_board_memberusers`. The intent is to expose, in a single call, who filed the report, together with essential context about the report, without requiring the client to navigate through multiple relations.

The endpoint accepts a `reportId` path parameter that uniquely identifies a report record in `discussion_board_reports`. Using that identifier, the implementation will query the `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers` table to locate the link row that indicates which member user created the report. It will then load the corresponding member user entity from `discussion_board_memberusers`, possibly including fields such as display name, account status, and basic profile attributes relevant for moderation decisions.

The operation returns a composed DTO `IDiscussionBoardReportOfMemberuser.IInvert`, which represents an inverted view centered on the report-to-member-user relationship. This view type is intended to provide both the link metadata and a compact representation of the memberUser and report objects, allowing the moderation UI to show who reported the content, under what circumstances, and with which status, while avoiding circular references and large collections.
operations.description:
Retrieve the member user who reported a specific piece of content, using the report identifier as input.

This endpoint is built around the `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers` Prisma model, described as a subsidiary entity that associates a single report from `discussion_board_reports` with the member user that acted as the reporter. According to typical schema comments for such link tables, each row indicates that a particular member user has filed a report, and it may store additional linkage metadata such as which session was used, or timestamps distinct from the main report entity. By supplying the `reportId` as a path parameter, the backend locates this link row and resolves the associated member user record from `discussion_board_memberusers`.

From a security and permissions perspective, this operation is restricted to administrative users who have responsibility for handling reports and managing accounts. The `authorizationActors` array therefore includes only `adminUser`. Ordinary member users or guests must not be able to retrieve the identities of reporters for arbitrary reports, as that could lead to retaliation, privacy issues, or undermining of the reporting process. Authorization decorators in the controller and guards in the service layer will ensure that only authenticated admins can successfully execute this call.

The response uses the `IDiscussionBoardReportOfMemberuser.IInvert` DTO, an inverted composition structure that centers on the report-to-member-user link while embedding concise information about both the report and the member user. Schema design guidance for invert types stresses that parent collections (for example, a member user's full list of reports or a report's full list of related entities) must be omitted to avoid circular references and oversized payloads. Instead, the DTO should include only the fields necessary for moderation workflows, such as member user identifiers, display name, restriction status, and key report properties like reason, category, and current handling status.

Error handling must cover several scenarios. If the `reportId` does not correspond to any row in `discussion_board_reports`, the operation should return a not-found response. If the report exists but is not associated with a member user reporter (for example, it may have been created by an admin and therefore stored in `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`), the service should also respond with a not-found or business-rule error indicating that there is no member user reporter for this report. Additionally, if the linked member user account has been removed or is in an inaccessible state, the implementation must either return a not-found error or a sanitized representation according to business rules on account deletion and retention.

This endpoint is commonly used with broader report listing/search operations and other report detail endpoints, such as those retrieving the reported article, comment, or attachment. Together, they form a complete moderation toolset for administrators working within the discussion board service.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the admin user reporter link for a given report from the discussion_board_report_of_adminusers subsidiary table.

This operation reads from the discussion_board_report_of_adminusers Prisma model, which represents a 1:1 link between a row in discussion_board_reports and the admin user who submitted that report. The endpoint is designed for internal moderation tooling where administrators or support staff need to see which adminUser account filed a particular report.

The operation accepts a single path parameter reportId, which corresponds to discussion_board_reports.id (UUID). It looks up the associated discussion_board_report_of_adminusers row via the discussion_board_report_id foreign key and returns a DTO representing the admin reporter association, including references to the report and the admin user as defined in the IDiscussionBoardReportOfAdminusers interface.

Because the underlying table is subsidiary and purely relational, this API is read-only and does not provide any capability to modify or delete records; it simply exposes the existing association for display in admin panels and audit views.
operations.description:
Get the admin user reporter association for a specific report identified by its UUID.

This endpoint operates on the discussion_board_report_of_adminusers Prisma table, whose primary key id uniquely identifies the association between a report and its admin user reporter. The key business field used for lookup in this operation is discussion_board_report_id, which is a foreign key referencing discussion_board_reports.id and is constrained to be unique, ensuring that at most one admin user association exists per report. The request path parameter reportId is mapped to this discussion_board_report_id value.

The response is modeled by the IDiscussionBoardReportOfAdminusers DTO, which reflects the schema fields including id, discussion_board_report_id, discussion_board_adminuser_id, and created_at. Implementations should also load the related admin user entity (via the adminUser relation to discussion_board_adminusers) when building higher-level views, although this operation's primary responsibility is to expose the reporter link itself as a stable, audit-friendly object.

Security-wise, this operation is restricted to administrative actors only, as it reveals which administrator filed a given report. This information is considered sensitive and is intended for internal moderation workflows, fraud investigations, and support back-office tools rather than for general end-user consumption. Authorization checks should verify that the caller has an adminUser role before returning any data.

If the specified reportId does not have an associated admin reporter row in discussion_board_report_of_adminusers—either because the report was filed by a member user instead, or because the reportId is invalid—the implementation should return a 404-style error indicating that no admin reporter is associated with the given report. This makes the behavior predictable for clients building admin UIs: they can distinguish “no such report” or “not reported by an admin” from successful lookups that return a populated association object.

This operation is typically used in conjunction with broader report listing endpoints (for example, a PATCH /reports search) and report detail retrieval (e.g., GET /reports/{reportId}). Admin console flows would first locate the report of interest, then call this endpoint when they specifically need to know which adminUser account submitted that report.

operations.specification:
Retrieve aggregated statistics about reports grouped by their target type from the discussion_board_reports primary table.

This operation reads from the discussion_board_reports Prisma model, which is the central entity representing user reports about articles, comments, or attachments. It performs aggregation queries grouping by target_type and optionally filtering by time ranges, statuses, actions, or reason codes as specified by the client in the request body.

The API is designed for admin dashboards and moderation analytics. It executes read-only aggregation logic (e.g., COUNT(*) per target_type, possibly broken down by status or action) and returns a DTO describing per-target-type counts and related metrics. No report records are modified as part of this operation; it is purely analytical and used to monitor volume and distribution of reports across different content types.
operations.description:
Get report statistics grouped by target type using aggregated data from the discussion_board_reports table.

This endpoint operates primarily on the discussion_board_reports Prisma model, whose fields include target_type, reporter_type, reason_code, description, status, action, created_at, and updated_at. The core idea is to provide administrators with an at-a-glance summary of how many reports exist for each target_type (such as "article", "comment", or "attachment") within a given time window or filtered by workflow status and action.

The request body uses the IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget.IRequest DTO and typically includes optional filters like createdAtFrom, createdAtTo, status list, action list, and reason_code list. These filters are applied to the underlying discussion_board_reports rows before grouping. For example, an adminUser might request “all submitted and in_review reports over the last 7 days” to see whether a particular content type is receiving disproportionate complaints.

The response is defined by IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget, which returns an array of per-target-type buckets, each containing the targetType value and one or more numeric metrics such as totalReportCount, openReportCount (for non-resolved statuses), and resolvedReportCount (for status = "resolved"). Implementations may extend this structure further (e.g., counts segmented by action) as long as they stay consistent with the DTO definition referenced here.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors because it exposes system-wide moderation statistics that are not meant for general users. Authorization should ensure only adminUser actors can call this endpoint. Since the operation is read-only and aggregates data, there is no impact on the underlying discussion_board_reports records, and no side effects beyond normal logging and metrics.

This operation is typically used by admin dashboards, scheduled reporting jobs, or monitoring tools. It complements more detailed report listing APIs (which would return individual report rows) by providing a high-level overview, helping admins decide where to focus moderation resources or whether particular content types need stricter guidelines or tooling.
operations.summary: Get aggregated report statistics by target_type from discussion_board_reports.

operations.specification:
This operation computes aggregated report statistics grouped by reason_code from the discussion_board_reports Prisma table. It performs a read-only analytical query that filters rows in discussion_board_reports according to criteria supplied in the request body, then groups the remaining rows by the reason_code column and calculates counts (and potentially other aggregate metrics) for each distinct reason.

The underlying discussion_board_reports model holds one row per report submitted for problematic content. It defines core columns such as target_type (what kind of content was reported, like "article", "comment", or "attachment"), reporter_type (whether the report was filed by a member user or an admin user), reason_code (a machine-friendly category such as "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", or "other"), description (optional free-text explanation when the reporter wants to add context), status (workflow state like "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved"), action (the moderation decision such as "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", or "restrict_user"), and timestamps created_at and updated_at.

Because the statistics must support flexible filtering, this endpoint is exposed as a PATCH method and accepts a complex JSON request body of type IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics.IRequest. The service implementation will interpret that DTO to apply filters on created_at/updated_at ranges, target_type values, reporter_type, reason_code subsets, status, and action, all on top of discussion_board_reports and, when required, its subsidiary link tables. After filtering, it will run a GROUP BY reason_code aggregation and return analytical records through the IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics response type. No records are inserted, updated, or deleted by this operation; it is purely read-only.

Although subsidiary models such as discussion_board_report_of_articles, discussion_board_report_of_comments, discussion_board_report_of_attachments, discussion_board_report_of_memberusers, and discussion_board_report_of_adminusers may be joined internally to satisfy filters about specific content or reporter types, the logical entity of this API is still the base discussion_board_reports table. The statistics represent derived information meant for moderation dashboards and reporting tools, not raw table rows.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics of moderation reports grouped by reason_code based on data stored in the discussion_board_reports table.

The primary purpose of this endpoint is to provide administrators with an at-a-glance view of how frequently each report reason is used across the discussion board. Each row in discussion_board_reports represents a single report, with target_type describing what was reported (for example, an article, comment, or attachment), reporter_type identifying whether a member user or admin user filed the report, reason_code indicating the main category such as "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", or "other", description capturing optional free-text justification when needed, status tracking workflow stage (like "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved"), action capturing the final moderation decision (like "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", or "restrict_user"), and created_at/updated_at storing timestamps. The aggregation logic groups these report rows by reason_code, and computes counts and possibly percentages for each reason.

From an authorization and security perspective, only administrative staff should see this level of moderation analytics, because it reveals internal categorization and volumes of problematic content, which are not intended for regular members. Therefore the endpoint is restricted to the adminUser actor via authorizationActors set to ["adminUser"]. Actual authentication and session management are handled by other parts of the system; this operation assumes it is invoked only when an admin user has been properly authenticated.

The request body, typed as IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics.IRequest, is designed to express a rich set of filters. For example, an administrator can limit the statistics to a particular date range using created_at or updated_at boundaries, focus only on certain target_type values (like only "article" reports), restrict to specific reporter_type values, or combine filters on status and action to understand how many reports of each type remain unresolved or have led to content removal or user restriction. The implementation will translate these filters into WHERE conditions over discussion_board_reports (and, when necessary, joins to subsidiary link tables such as discussion_board_report_of_articles, discussion_board_report_of_comments, discussion_board_report_of_attachments, discussion_board_report_of_memberusers, and discussion_board_report_of_adminusers), before performing the GROUP BY reason_code aggregation.

The response body uses the IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics DTO. This type does not map one-to-one to any Prisma model; instead, it represents computed rows where each entry includes a reason_code and aggregated metrics such as total_count, and possibly additional derived values depending on the project’s analytics design. Typically, the DTO encapsulates a collection of statistics rows, each corresponding to a single reason_code.

Errors such as invalid filter shapes, unsupported reason_code values, or contradictory conditions must be reported according to the shared error-handling conventions of the API (for example, using structured validation errors). The endpoint is intended to be used by moderation dashboards and reporting UIs that need to chart or tabulate report volumes by reason over selected time periods.
operations.summary: Get aggregated report statistics by reason_code based on discussion_board_reports.

responseBody.description: Aggregated statistics of reports grouped by reason_code, returned as analytical rows with counts and related metrics derived from discussion_board_reports.

operations.specification:
This operation computes aggregated report statistics grouped by status from the discussion_board_reports Prisma table. It is a read-only analytics endpoint that filters report rows according to options provided in the request body and then groups the filtered set by the status column, computing counts (and possibly additional metrics) for each distinct status value.

The discussion_board_reports model stores one record per moderation report, with fields including target_type (e.g. "article", "comment", "attachment"), reporter_type ("memberuser" or "adminuser"), reason_code (such as "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", "other"), description (optional free-text explanation when reason_code is not sufficient), status (workflow stage such as "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved"), action (decision like "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", "restrict_user"), and timestamps created_at and updated_at. By grouping on status and counting matched rows, this endpoint provides an overview of the moderation pipeline, highlighting how many reports are pending review versus already resolved.

The PATCH method is used because the operation accepts a complex filtering request body of type IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics.IRequest. The server applies incoming filters as WHERE conditions over discussion_board_reports, optionally involving joins to subsidiary tables when queries reference content or reporter specifics. Once filtering is complete, it aggregates by status. No data modifications are performed on discussion_board_reports or any related tables; the operation strictly reads from the database to produce analytical results.

Although link entities such as discussion_board_report_of_articles, discussion_board_report_of_comments, discussion_board_report_of_attachments, discussion_board_report_of_memberusers, and discussion_board_report_of_adminusers describe polymorphic targets and reporters, their role in this API is only to help narrow which base report rows are considered during filtering. The aggregation itself is always based on the status field in the base discussion_board_reports table, ensuring that statistics are consistent with the core moderation workflow.
operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated statistics of moderation reports grouped by status based on the discussion_board_reports table.

This endpoint lets administrators monitor the state of the moderation queue by counting how many reports exist for each status value. Each record in discussion_board_reports carries a status such as "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved", alongside related information like target_type, reporter_type, reason_code, description, action, and timestamps created_at and updated_at. The service applies filters from the request body to the discussion_board_reports table and then groups the remaining rows by status, computing per-status counts and potentially additional metrics needed for dashboards.

Only admin users should access this endpoint because it exposes internal workload and decision distributions that would not be appropriate for general members. To reflect this, authorizationActors is set to ["adminUser"]. Authentication, session validation, and any role-based access control enforcement are delegated to the surrounding infrastructure; by the time this operation executes, it assumes that the caller represents a valid admin user.

The request body is structured as IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics.IRequest and is intended to support rich filtering scenarios. Administrators may specify created_at or updated_at time ranges to focus on recent reports, restrict by target_type to view only article-related or attachment-related workloads, constrain by reporter_type to examine memberuser versus adminuser submissions, or filter by specific reason_code and action combinations to understand how certain categories are progressing through the workflow. Internally, these filters become conditions over discussion_board_reports, with optional joins to link tables such as discussion_board_report_of_articles, discussion_board_report_of_comments, discussion_board_report_of_attachments, discussion_board_report_of_memberusers, and discussion_board_report_of_adminusers when deeper scoping is needed.

The response uses the IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics DTO, which encapsulates analytical rows instead of direct Prisma entities. Each row typically includes a status value and associated counts (and potentially derived metrics like proportions), and the DTO normally represents a collection of such per-status statistics entries.

Any invalid filter structures, unsupported literal values for status or related fields, or contradictions in the request should be reported back following the project’s standard validation and error-handling conventions. These statistics are intended to drive moderation dashboards, SLA monitoring panels, and other internal tools that visualize report handling performance over time.
operations.summary: Get aggregated report statistics by status based on discussion_board_reports.

operations.specification:
Retrieve the current notification preference settings for the authenticated discussion board member user.

This operation reads from the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` Prisma table, which stores a single row per member user indicating their personal choices for activity, digest, and marketing notifications. It will use the authenticated member user's identity (linked to `discussion_board_memberusers.id`) to locate the corresponding preferences row via the unique `discussion_board_memberuser_id` foreign key.

On invocation, the implementation MUST derive the target member from the authenticated session context and MUST NOT accept any client-supplied user identifier. If a preferences row already exists, it is loaded and returned. If no row exists yet for the member, the service MAY either create a default preferences row (for example, using system-wide default values) or return a not-found error depending on higher-level requirements; however, the contract of this operation is that on success it returns exactly one preference object for the calling member.
operations.description:
Get the notification preference settings for the currently authenticated member user.

This endpoint provides a simple way for a logged-in member to inspect which types of notifications the system is allowed to send to them. It operates on the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` table, whose description states that it "stores per-member configuration flags controlling which categories of notifications the system is allowed to send, such as activity on the user’s own content, digest summaries, and optional marketing or non-essential announcements." The table is in a strict 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_memberusers` via the non-null, unique foreign key `discussion_board_memberuser_id`.

From a security perspective, this operation is restricted to authenticated member users only and does not take any path or query parameter identifying a different user. The server implementation MUST derive the `discussion_board_memberuser_id` from the authenticated session context and MUST ignore any attempt by the client to influence which member’s preferences are read. This ensures that a member can only see their own preferences, never preferences for another account. Administrative viewing or editing of member preferences, if required, would be implemented through separate admin-focused endpoints.

On success, the API returns an `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserNotificationPreference` object that reflects the current values of `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled`, along with `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps described in the Prisma schema. Client applications can call this API before rendering a notification settings screen so that the UI checkboxes or toggles accurately mirror the stored configuration. Typical errors include authentication failures when no valid member session is present, and implementation-defined handling when a preference record has not yet been created for the user. The service SHOULD document whether it auto-creates a default row or returns a 404/204 response when no preferences exist yet.
operations.summary: Get notification preferences for the current member user from discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences.

responseBody.description: Current notification preference settings for the authenticated member user.

operations.name: at

Member comments on articles are another key activity type that can produce notifications; creating comments ensures there is discussion activity for which preferences are consulted.
Uploading attachments to articles can also generate notification events; creating attachments establishes attachment-related activity controlled by the member's notification preferences.

Administrative restriction records can influence whether notifications are delivered or suppressed for a member; creating a restriction establishes moderation state that may be evaluated in conjunction with notification preferences.

operations.specification:
Update or create the notification preference settings for the authenticated discussion board member user.

This operation writes to the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` Prisma table, which enforces a 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_memberusers` through the unique, non-null `discussion_board_memberuser_id` foreign key. The request body supplies new values for the three boolean preference flags controlling whether the system may send activity, digest, and marketing notifications.

On invocation, the implementation identifies the target row using the authenticated member user's ID from the session context and MUST NOT trust any user-identifying fields in the request body. If a preferences row already exists for that member, the operation updates it and refreshes the `updated_at` timestamp. If no row exists yet, the implementation creates one while honoring the uniqueness constraint on `discussion_board_memberuser_id`. For a given member and request body, repeated PUT calls are idempotent: they will leave the stored preference state unchanged after the first successful application.
operations.description:
Change the notification preference settings for the currently authenticated member user.

This endpoint allows an authenticated member user to manage the categories of notifications they are willing to receive. The underlying `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` table is described as storing "per-member configuration flags" that indicate consent for activity notifications, digest summaries, and optional marketing or non-essential announcements. Each record is strictly associated with one row in `discussion_board_memberusers` via the unique foreign key `discussion_board_memberuser_id`, ensuring that each member has at most one preference set.

Security-wise, only the member associated with the current authenticated session is permitted to call this API. The server MUST derive the `discussion_board_memberuser_id` from the authenticated context and MUST ignore any attempt by the client to specify another user or override the target identity in the payload. This API is not intended for administrators to override or inspect member choices; such functionality, if needed, would be handled through admin-specific operations.

The request body uses `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserNotificationPreference.IUpdate` and is expected to include boolean fields corresponding to `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled`. The Prisma schema notes that these fields are non-nullable, so the implementation should validate that all required flags are supplied with explicit true/false values. Upon successful update (or creation, if the member did not yet have a row), the API responds with the full `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserNotificationPreference` object, including the updated preference flags and the `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps. Clients typically call this operation when a user saves changes from a notification settings screen, and should handle validation errors for malformed payloads as well as authentication failures when no valid member session is present. Because this endpoint follows PUT semantics on a per-member resource, repeating the same request body for the same authenticated member is idempotent and safe for retries in the presence of transient network failures.
operations.summary: Update notification preferences for the current member user in discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences.

responseBody.description: Updated notification preference settings for the authenticated member user.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves the current notification preference settings for the authenticated admin user from the Prisma table `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences`. The table has a strict 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_adminusers` through the unique foreign key `discussion_board_adminuser_id`, ensuring that each admin user has at most one preference record.

The endpoint is implemented as a GET on `/notifications/adminUser/preferences` without path parameters, because the target record is determined from the authenticated admin user context rather than from an explicit identifier in the URL. The provider logic will resolve the admin user from the authentication/session context and then load the preferences row whose `discussion_board_adminuser_id` matches that admin’s ID.

The response body returns a DTO mapped from the Prisma model fields: `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled`, along with metadata fields such as `created_at` and `updated_at`. Following the service prefix `DiscussionBoard` and singularized table name, the DTO type is named `IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPreference`. This operation is read-only and does not modify any data.
operations.description:
Retrieve the current notification preference configuration for the authenticated admin user.

This operation reads from the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` table, whose schema description explains that it stores per-admin configuration flags controlling which categories of notifications the system is allowed to send. Each record is strictly associated with exactly one `discussion_board_adminusers` row via the non-null foreign key `discussion_board_adminuser_id`, and a unique index on that column guarantees that each admin user can have at most one preference set. The primary key `id` uniquely identifies each row, while boolean fields `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled` determine whether the admin receives notifications about activity on content they authored, periodic digest or summary notifications, and optional marketing-style or non-essential announcements. The `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps track when the record was first created and when it was last updated.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated admin users, expressed using the `authorizationActors: ["adminUser"]` configuration. The controller and provider implementations must obtain the current admin user identity from the authentication or session layer and then select the preferences row whose `discussion_board_adminuser_id` matches the authenticated admin. Clients are not allowed to specify a different admin identifier in the path or query parameters, which prevents them from reading the preferences of other administrators. If no preference record exists for the authenticated admin user, the service may either return a 404 Not Found or synthesize and return default preferences, depending on higher-level business rules defined elsewhere.

In terms of business workflow, this endpoint is typically used by administrative frontends to load the current state of the admin’s notification settings before rendering a configuration screen. The interface can then display toggle switches or checkboxes for activity notifications, digest notifications, and marketing notifications based on the values returned by this operation. The corresponding update operation, PUT `/notifications/adminUser/preferences`, is used to modify these flags and will update the underlying `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` row. Error handling should cover missing authentication, absence of an associated admin user, and database errors, always returning appropriate HTTP status codes and avoiding any leakage of internal implementation details.

Because the operation is read-only, it has no side effects beyond standard access logging and metrics collection. It simply exposes exactly what is stored in the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` table for the current admin user, maintaining a consistent contract for clients that need to reflect the saved notification configuration in their UI.

The table has a 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_adminusers` enforced by a unique index on the non-null foreign key `discussion_board_adminuser_id`, ensuring that each admin user can own at most one preference record.

The endpoint uses the PUT method on `/notifications/adminUser/preferences` without path parameters, as the target row is determined by the currently authenticated admin user rather than an explicit identifier in the URL. The provider implementation will resolve the admin user from the authentication context, locate the preferences row whose `discussion_board_adminuser_id` matches that user, and then apply updates to the boolean flags `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled`. The persistence layer is responsible for updating the `updated_at` timestamp while leaving `created_at` unchanged, reflecting the last modification time of these settings.

The request body is defined by the DTO type `IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPreference.IUpdate`, which contains updatable fields corresponding to the preference columns in the Prisma model. On success, the operation returns the updated preference record mapped to `IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPreference`, allowing clients to immediately see the final stored configuration.
operations.description:
Update the notification preference configuration for the authenticated admin user.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` table, which the schema describes as storing per-admin configuration flags for notification categories such as activity on the admin’s own content, digest summaries of relevant activity, and optional marketing or non-essential announcement notifications. The mandatory foreign key field `discussion_board_adminuser_id` establishes a 1:1 association with `discussion_board_adminusers`, and a unique index on that field enforces that each admin user has at most a single preference row. The business fields `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, and `marketing_notifications_enabled` are non-nullable booleans, so the update DTO must always provide explicit true or false values when these fields are being modified. The `created_at` and `updated_at` datetime fields capture when the preference record was created and when it was most recently changed.

Security is strict for this endpoint. Only authenticated admin users, represented here with `authorizationActors: ["adminUser"]`, may modify their own notification preferences. The implementation must ignore any attempt by the client to specify a different admin user in the request and must always derive the `discussion_board_adminuser_id` from the authenticated admin’s identity. This prevents unauthorized modifications of other admins’ notification configurations. If no preference row exists yet for the authenticated admin, the service may either create a new row with the provided values or respond with an error that instructs the client to initialize preferences through a separate workflow, depending on the broader system design.

The request body uses the `IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPreference.IUpdate` type, which contains fields corresponding directly to the Prisma columns that can be updated. Validation logic should enforce that boolean values are supplied where required and may optionally apply additional business rules, such as disallowing certain combinations if, for example, marketing notifications must always be optional and cannot be forced on. When the update succeeds, the operation returns the full `IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPreference` representation of the updated row, including current values of `activity_notifications_enabled`, `digest_notifications_enabled`, `marketing_notifications_enabled`, and the updated `updated_at` timestamp.

This operation is tightly coupled with the GET `/notifications/adminUser/preferences` endpoint. Clients typically call the GET operation first to render current preferences, allow admins to adjust toggles for activity, digest, and marketing notifications, and then invoke this PUT operation to persist the changes. Error handling should cover missing authentication, attempts by non-admin actors to access the endpoint, validation failures in the request body, and database-level failures, returning appropriate HTTP codes and messages while preserving the confidentiality of internal implementation details.

prerequisites.description: An article must exist only when creating a new article; however, updating admin user notification preferences does not depend on articles, so no article-related prerequisites are required.
Article categories are unrelated to notification preference updates, so no category creation is required as a prerequisite.
Like creation is unrelated to notification preference updates; there is no business dependency between these resources.
Comment creation does not need to precede updating admin notification preferences.
Admin comments on articles are not required before updating admin notification preferences.
Creating attachments for articles does not affect or gate notification preference updates.
Member restriction records concern moderation state of members, not admin notification preference rows.
Submitting reports is unrelated to the ability of an admin to toggle their own notification preferences.

current.description:
Current page index in the paginated result set.

This value represents the page that the backend actually resolved and returned in the response. It is expressed as a zero‑based non‑negative integer (0 for the first page, 1 for the second, and so on).

In typical usage, this corresponds to the `page` value requested by the client (from `IPage.IRequest.page`), but may be adjusted by the server if the requested page is out of range (for example, requesting a page beyond the last page may be clamped to the last available page).

limit.description:
Maximum number of records that can appear in a single page of results.

This value is the effective page size used when computing the current result window. It is always a non‑negative integer and is typically derived from the client's requested `limit` value, subject to service‑side defaults and maximum caps.

When `limit` is 0, the system should be interpreted as returning no records per page while still reporting pagination metadata, although most production usages will enforce a positive minimum such as 10 or 20 items per page.

records.description:
Total number of records that match the applied query conditions before pagination.

This count is calculated **after** all filters, search terms, and access‑control rules are applied, but **before** any paging window is sliced out. As a result, `records` tells consumers the full size of the filtered dataset, not just the number of items in the current page.

The value is always a non‑negative integer. A value of `0` means that there are no records matching the query, in which case the `pages` value also reflects that there are no available pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available for the current query, derived from `records` and `limit`.

This value is computed using a ceiling division of `records / limit` when `limit` is greater than zero. For example, with `records = 23` and `limit = 10`, the `pages` value becomes `3`.

When `records` is `0`, `pages` is reported as `0` to indicate that the result set is empty. When `limit` is `0`, the service should define a consistent behavior (for example, reporting `pages` as `0` and leaving `current` at `0`), and this DTO simply exposes the chosen behavior without redefining it.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata describing how a complete result set is partitioned into pages.

This DTO is used in list and search responses to provide clients with enough information to navigate through large datasets. It reports both the effective paging parameters (`current` and `limit`) and the overall dataset size (`records` and derived `pages`).

The values in this object are typically derived from the underlying storage layer (for example, a Prisma query with `take`/`skip` and a separate `count`), and they are always consistent with the filters and access‑control rules applied to the current request.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the current slice of article results.
