This property is an `IPage.IPagination` object that exposes the current 1-based page index, the requested page size, the total number of matching article records, and the computed total number of pages. It allows clients to implement paging controls (next/previous buttons, page number links) consistently across endpoints that return `IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary` items.

data.description:
Ordered collection of article summary records for the requested page.

Each element in this array is an `IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary` instance derived from the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model and its related category/author summary projections. The array can be empty when no articles match the given search and filter criteria, even though `pagination` will still describe the requested page context.

IPageIDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Paged collection of discussion board article summaries backed by the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model.

This schema is a concrete specialization of the generic `IPage<T>` pattern where `T` is `IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary`. It is used as the response body for article list and search endpoints such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles` and `PATCH /discussionBoard/memberUser/members/{memberUserId}/likedArticles`, combining pagination metadata in `pagination` with an array of article summary records in `data`.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the current slice of article category results.

This property follows the shared `IPage.IPagination` structure, exposing the current page index, page size limit, total number of matching records, and total page count. Clients use this information to render paging controls (for example, next/previous buttons) and to decide when they have reached the beginning or end of the result set when browsing categories.

data.description:
Ordered collection of article category summary records for the current page.

Each element is an `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary` DTO derived from a row in the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model and shaped for lightweight list rendering. The server applies any search, filter, and sort criteria from `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IRequest` before populating this array, so it contains only the categories that match the caller's query for this specific page.

IPageIDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISu.description:
Paginated container of discussion board article category summaries returned by search operations.

This DTO is used as the response body for the `PATCH /discussionBoard/articleCategories` endpoint, wrapping a page of `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary` records together with pagination metadata. It represents the result of querying the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model with filters, sort options, and paging parameters defined by `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IRequest`, and is optimized for navigation menus, article creation flows, and category management screens.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the current slice of comment results.

This object follows the `IPage.IPagination` contract and reports the current page index, page size, total number of comments that match the applied filters, and the computed total page count. Clients use this information to implement paged comment lists on article detail screens, including controls to move between older and newer comment pages.

data.description:
Ordered collection of comment summary records for the current page.

Each item is an `IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary` DTO representing a single row from the `discussion_board_comments` table, enriched with article and author summary context for efficient list rendering. The array contains only comments for the scoped article and matching any search, status, or sort options provided via `IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest`, making it suitable for infinite-scroll or discrete page navigation patterns.

IPageIDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Paginated container of discussion board comment summaries for a single article.

This DTO serves as the response body for the `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments` endpoint, combining pagination metadata with a page of `IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary` items. It encapsulates filtered and sorted comment data from the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model for the specified article, enabling clients to display long comment threads in manageable pages without loading the entire set at once.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the current slice of attachment results.

This object exposes the current page index, page size, total record count, and total page count used when listing attachments under a discussion board article. It directly reflects the server-side pagination state applied when querying `discussion_board_attachments` for the calling endpoint.

data.description:
Ordered collection of attachment summary records for the current page.

Each element is an `IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary` projection of a row in the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model. The array contains only the attachments that match the applied filters (such as content type or extension) for the targeted article and fit within the requested pagination window.

IPageIDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of file attachment summaries belonging to a discussion board article.

This DTO wraps a list of `IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary` objects together with pagination metadata from `IPage.IPagination`. It is the standard response shape for endpoints such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/attachments`, which list file attachments linked to a specific article row in the `discussion_board_articles` table via the `discussion_board_attachments` model.

Clients use this schema to render attachment lists with page controls, showing file name, size, and download URL while allowing the UI to navigate across multiple pages of attachments without fetching the entire dataset at once.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata describing the current window of report results.

Includes the current page index, page size, total number of reports, and total page count for the query executed over the `discussion_board_reports` table. This information enables moderation tools to implement paged navigation through large sets of reports.

data.description:
List of report summary entries returned for the current page.

Each element is an `IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary` representation of a row from the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model, optionally filtered by status, target type, reporter type, or date range. These summaries provide just enough information for administrators to triage reports in queues and listing screens without loading full report-detail payloads.

IPageIDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Paginated collection of discussion board report summaries for moderation and review.

This DTO combines pagination information from `IPage.IPagination` with an array of `IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary` items, each describing a single report stored in the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model. It is the canonical response wrapper for list-style moderation endpoints such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/reports` and `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}/reportLinks`.

Moderation UIs rely on this schema to render report queues, apply filters and sorting, and traverse through multiple pages of report summaries while keeping network payloads compact and focused on key workflow fields like status, action, and timestamps.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata that describes how the guest user search result set is sliced.

This object comes from the generic `IPage.IPagination` schema and reflects the current page index, the configured page size, the total number of guest user placeholder records that match the search criteria, and the corresponding total page count. It allows administrative tools to drive next/previous navigation and to render accurate counts based on the `discussion_board_guestusers` table.

data.description:
Ordered collection of guest user summary records for the current page.

Each element is an `IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.ISummary` projection of a single row from the `discussion_board_guestusers` Prisma model, exposing the guest identifier, opaque `anonymous_token`, and lifecycle timestamps while omitting internal implementation details. The ordering and subset of records respect the filters and sort options supplied via `IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IRequest` to the `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/guestUsers` endpoint.

IPageIDiscussionBoardGuestuser.ISummary.description:
Paginated result wrapper for guest user placeholder accounts stored in the `discussion_board_guestusers` table.

This schema is used as the response body type for administrative search operations such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/guestUsers`, where administrators request a filtered and ordered slice of guest user placeholders. The `pagination` property captures page-level metadata, while `data` contains a list of `IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.ISummary` entries that summarize individual guest identities for audit and diagnostic workflows.

By separating pagination information from the collection of guest summaries, this type supports efficient list UIs and back-office tools that need to iterate over potentially large populations of guest users without exposing internal or sensitive operational details.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata describing how the member user search results are segmented.

This object follows the `IPage.IPagination` contract and reports the current page number, page size, total number of matching member user records, and total page count. It is derived from queries executed against the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma model using the filters and sort configuration supplied in `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.IRequest`.

data.description:
Collection of member user summary projections representing the current page slice.

Each item is an `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.ISummary` DTO that wraps non-sensitive account metadata from a row in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table, such as the member identifier, display name, account_status, and creation timestamp. Credential-related fields like `password_hash` are intentionally excluded so that this page response can be safely consumed by administrative listing and moderation views.

IPageIDiscussionBoardMemberuser.ISummary.description:
Paginated result wrapper for registered member user accounts stored in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table.

This schema is used as the response body type for administrative search endpoints such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/memberUsers`, where operators query member accounts by lifecycle status, email verification state, registration windows, or activity periods. The `pagination` property describes the overall result window, while `data` contains an array of `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.ISummary` records that present concise but sufficient information for list screens and dashboards.

The design of this DTO ensures that bulk member listings expose only non-sensitive fields appropriate for back-office tooling, while more detailed account or security information remains confined to dedicated detail endpoints and internal services.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the session history of a specific member user.

These values are computed from the Prisma query executed against the `discussion_board_memberuser_sessions` table scoped by the parent member user's identifier, taking into account any date range filters or other criteria provided in `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.IRequest`.

Clients rely on this pagination block to render page controls in security and audit views, and to request previous or next slices of the member's session history in a predictable way.

data.description:
List of session summary DTOs representing individual authenticated sessions for the target member user.

Each item is an `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISummary` projection of a row in the `discussion_board_memberuser_sessions` model, providing lightweight information such as creation time, IP, URLs, and activity flags that are safe to expose in audit tooling.

The array can be empty when the member user has no sessions that match the supplied filters or when the requested page is beyond the last page, but it is always present so that consumers can treat it as a canonical container for session rows.

IPageIDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.I.description:
Paginated result wrapper for member user session summaries in the discussion board service.

This DTO encapsulates a single page of `IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISummary` objects queried from the `discussion_board_memberuser_sessions` Prisma model for a particular member user. It is used by endpoints such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}/sessions` to deliver a navigable list of sessions to administrative or security dashboards.

The `pagination` field captures the current paging state across the member's session history, while `data` contains the list of individual session summaries for the requested slice. This structure provides a read-only, audit-friendly view that allows operators or the member user themself to inspect where and when the account has been active without exposing raw tokens or low-level authentication internals.

pagination.description:
Page information.

Provides the current page, total record count, total page count, and page size for an administrator session listing. This allows administrative tools to navigate through large sets of admin sessions in a predictable and efficient way.

data.description:
List of administrator session summary records on the current page.

Each element is a summary projection of a single session from the discussion_board_adminuser_sessions table, exposing only non-sensitive metadata needed for monitoring and audit dashboards.

IPageIDiscussionBoardAdminuserSession.IS.description:
Paginated collection of administrator session summaries.

Wraps a page of admin session summary DTOs together with pagination metadata, enabling secure and efficient browsing of administrative session history without exposing any sensitive authentication material.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IJoin.description:
Request payload for guest users to join the discussion board as an anonymous placeholder account.

Carries the opaque anonymous token or fingerprint that will be mapped to the discussion_board_guestusers.anonymous_token field. This DTO is used by the POST /auth/guestUser/join endpoint and does not include any authentication or identity fields managed exclusively by the backend.

The backend uses this information to either create a new guest record or reuse an existing one based on the anonymous_token uniqueness constraint in the discussion_board_guestusers table. No passwords or personal information are included. Session context fields such as href and referrer are optional hints that can be used to establish or enrich guest session metadata; when omitted, the server may derive equivalent information from the HTTP request context.

anonymous_token.description:
Opaque anonymous token or fingerprint representing the same unauthenticated visitor across sessions.

Maps conceptually to discussion_board_guestusers.anonymous_token, which is unique per active guest record. Must be a non-empty string. The exact format is determined by the client (for example, a fingerprint or random token) but must remain stable for the same browser/client so that the same guest can be reused.

oneOf.description:
Optional client IP address associated with the guest join request.

When provided, it should be an IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation and may be recorded as part of downstream guest session metadata for security logging and anomaly detection. If omitted or null, the server may infer the IP address from the transport layer or other infrastructure signals.

Explicit null when the client chooses not to send an IP address.

In this case, the server is expected to rely on its own view of the connection to determine any IP information used in session records or security analytics.

ip.description:
Client IP address context wrapper for the guest join request.

This field models the possibility that the client may or may not send an IP string, using oneOf to represent either a concrete IP value or an explicit null marker. It is treated strictly as connection metadata, not as an authentication identifier, and is entirely optional from the business perspective.

href.description:
Current page URL from which the guest join request is being made.

Used to populate or update session context for security analytics, fraud detection, and audit logging when provided. This value typically corresponds to the browser location at the time of the join action and helps the backend understand where the session was initiated.

Supplying this field is optional. When it is omitted, the server may derive an equivalent URL from the HTTP request context or leave the related session metadata unset.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that indicates the previous page leading to the current location where the guest join request is initiated.

Recorded as part of the guest session context to support security monitoring, traffic analysis, and audit trails without exposing any authentication identity from the client side.

This field is optional. When not provided, the server can rely on standard HTTP referrer headers or other contextual information if available, or simply leave the referrer metadata empty.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IAuthorized.description:
Standard authorization response DTO for an authenticated guest user of the discussion board.

Returned by guest join and refresh endpoints after successfully materializing or validating a discussion_board_guestusers record. Contains the guest identifier and issued JWT token information for the guestUser actor role.

Sensitive authentication internals such as password hashes or refresh-token secrets are never exposed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user placeholder account.

This is the primary key discussion_board_guestusers.id and is used internally by the backend to associate future guest activity with the correct record.

anonymous_token.description:
Opaque correlation token that identifies this guest user across visits.

This maps to the `anonymous_token` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table and is typically constrained by a unique index to ensure each token identifies at most one guest record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user placeholder was created.

Maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user placeholder was last updated.

Maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table, which is refreshed whenever the record is modified.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for this guest user placeholder.

Maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table. When non-null, the record is considered closed or no longer active.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IRefresh.description:
Request payload for refreshing JWT tokens for a guestUser session in the discussion board.

This DTO carries the refresh token previously issued to the guestUser along with optional client context information that may be used for security logging or anomaly detection. The server validates the refresh token, ensures the underlying discussion_board_guestusers record is active (not logically deleted), and then issues new JWT access (and optionally refresh) tokens.

The DTO does not include any guest identity fields such as id or anonymous_token; those are derived from the refresh token subject on the server side.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token string associated with a discussion_board_guestusers record. This token was previously issued by the guestUser join or refresh operation and encodes the guestUser id as its subject. It must be presented unchanged for the refresh to succeed.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address associated with the current refresh request. When provided it should be an IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation and may be used for security logging and anomaly detection.
Explicit null when the client chooses not to send an IP address. In this case the server may infer the IP from the transport layer or leave it unset.

ip.description: Client IP address context wrapper for the refresh request. This field models the possibility that the client may or may not send an IP string, using oneOf to represent either a concrete IP value or an explicit null marker.

href.description: Current page URL from which the refresh request is being made. Used to populate or update session context for security analytics and auditing.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page that led to the current location when the refresh request is made. Used for session context and security monitoring.

IDiscussionBoardMemberUserJoin.IRequest.description:
Registration payload for creating a new member user account in the discussionBoard service backed by the discussion_board_memberusers table.

This DTO supplies business-level registration data such as email, raw password, display name, and optional profile fields. The backend hashes the password into the password_hash column and initializes lifecycle fields like account_status, created_at, and email_verified according to business rules.

The DTO intentionally omits system-managed fields (id, timestamps, lifecycle flags) and any actor identity or restriction information. It also includes session context fields used to create the initial member session and support security analytics.

email.description: Unique email address for the member user. Serves as the primary login identifier and contact address. Must not conflict with any existing discussion_board_memberusers.email value.

password.description: Raw password chosen by the user during registration. The backend hashes this value using a strong one-way hashing algorithm and stores only the resulting password_hash in the discussion_board_memberusers table.

displayName.description: Public display name (nickname) shown on articles and comments authored by the member. Must be a non-empty string and may be subject to additional validation or profanity filters.

bio.description: Optional short biography or self-introduction shown on the member profile. When provided, this text is persisted to the bio column of discussion_board_memberusers; explicitly null indicates that the member chose not to set a biography at registration time.

location.description: Optional free-form text describing the member's location, such as city, country, or region. Stored in the location column of discussion_board_memberusers when non-null; explicit null indicates that the member prefers not to disclose any location information at registration.

ip.description: Optional client IP address associated with the registration request. When present it should be an IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation and is used for security logging, fraud detection, and rate limiting. Explicit null indicates that the client did not send an IP value and the backend may infer it from the transport layer or leave it unset.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) at the time of registration. Used to create or update the initial member session context and support security analytics.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) when the registration form was submitted. Helps populate session context and analyze signup funnels.

IDiscussionBoardMemberUserLogin.IRequest.description: Login credentials and session context for authenticating an existing discussionBoard member user against the `discussion_board_memberusers` table using email and password.

email.description: Member user email address used as the unique login identifier in `discussion_board_memberusers`.

password.description: Plain-text password provided by the member user for authentication. The backend hashes this value and compares it to the stored password hash.

oneOf.description: Optional client IP address for session tracking and security analytics.

ip.description: Optional client IP address for session tracking and security analytics. When omitted or null, the backend may infer IP from the transport layer.

href.description: Current page URL from which the login request is initiated. Used for session context and security/audit logging.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) from which the user navigated before initiating login. Used for session context and security/audit logging.

IDiscussionBoardMemberUserRefresh.IReque.description:
Request payload for refreshing JWT tokens for a discussionBoard member user.

This DTO carries the refresh token that the client previously received during login or join flows and now presents in order to obtain new access and refresh tokens, without resubmitting credentials.

The payload is intentionally minimal: all identity and lifecycle checks are derived from the token and the underlying `discussion_board_memberusers` and restriction models, so no user identifiers or profile fields appear here.

refresh_token.description:
Refresh token issued previously to the member user, represented as an opaque string.

The server validates its integrity, expiry, and association with a `discussion_board_memberusers` record before issuing new tokens.

IDiscussionBoardAdminUserJoin.IRequest.description:
Request payload for registering a new administrative user for the discussionBoard service.

This DTO supplies the core credentials and profile information required to create a new row in `discussion_board_adminusers`, including login email, plain-text password, display name, and optional bio.

The service layer hashes the password into the `password_hash` column, initializes lifecycle fields such as `email_verified`, `account_status`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, and then issues initial JWT tokens via a separate authorized response schema.

In addition, this join operation immediately establishes an authenticated admin session. Therefore it also carries connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) so that the backend can create an appropriate admin session record for auditing and security analysis.

email.description:
Administrator email address to be used as the unique login identifier and primary contact channel.

Must satisfy the uniqueness constraint on `discussion_board_adminusers.email` and comply with standard email format validation.

password.description:
Plain-text password chosen by the administrator for authentication.

This value is never stored directly; instead, the service hashes it into the `password_hash` column of `discussion_board_adminusers` according to security policy.

display_name.description:
Public or semi-public display name for the administrator account.

Shown in audit trails or where admin-originated content is attributed, corresponding conceptually to the `display_name` column in `discussion_board_adminusers`.

bio.description:
Optional short profile or role description for this administrator account.

When provided, it maps to the nullable `bio` column on `discussion_board_adminusers`; when omitted or null, the profile has no additional description.

ip.description:
Optional IP address for the admin's current connection, used for session and security auditing.

When provided, this should be the client IP in a standard textual representation (IPv4 or IPv6). If omitted or null, the backend may derive the IP from the underlying HTTP request context.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) at the time the registration (join) request is initiated.

This value is stored in admin session records (for example, in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`) to provide contextual information about where the administrator started their first authenticated session. It must be a valid absolute URI representing the frontend location.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that led to the registration (join) request.

This value is used for security analysis and UX diagnostics and is also recorded in admin session tables. It should be a valid absolute URI; when there is no referrer, clients may send a generic landing URL according to frontend policy.

IDiscussionBoardAdminUserLogin.IRequest.description:
Login request payload for an administrative user of the discussion board service.

This DTO is submitted to the admin login endpoint when an existing administrator attempts to authenticate. It carries the admin's email and plain-text password along with session context information (connection metadata) used to create or update an admin session record in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`.

The service layer hashes the provided password and compares it against `discussion_board_adminusers.password_hash`. No hashed password material is ever accepted from the client, ensuring that credential handling remains strictly under backend control.

email.description:
Email address of the administrative user attempting to log in.

This must correspond to the unique `email` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. The login operation will fail with an authentication error if no matching administrator exists or if the account is not in an allowed lifecycle state.

password.description:
Plain-text password for the administrative user attempting to log in.

The backend hashes this value using the configured password hashing algorithm and compares the result with the stored `password_hash` column in `discussion_board_adminusers`. Clients must never send pre-hashed passwords; hashing is exclusively handled by the server.

oneOf.description:
Optional IP address for the admin's current connection, used for session and security auditing.

When provided, this should be the client IP in a standard textual representation (IPv4 or IPv6). If omitted or null, the backend may derive the IP from the underlying HTTP request context.

ip.description:
Optional IP address for the admin's current connection, used for session and security auditing.

When provided, this should be the client IP in a standard textual representation (IPv4 or IPv6). If omitted or null, the backend may derive the IP from the underlying HTTP request context.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) at the time the login request is initiated.

This value is stored in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` to provide contextual information about where the admin started their session. It must be a valid absolute URI representing the frontend location.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that led to the login request.

This value is used for security analysis and UX diagnostics and is also recorded in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`. It should be a valid absolute URI; when there is no referrer, clients may send a generic landing URL according to frontend policy.

IDiscussionBoardAdminUserRefresh.IReques.description:
Request payload for refreshing JWT tokens for an already authenticated discussion board administrator (adminUser).

This DTO carries the refresh token previously issued during login or a prior refresh operation. The backend validates this token against token storage or embedded claims that reference `discussion_board_adminusers.id`, checks account lifecycle fields (such as `account_status`, `deleted_at`, and `email_verified`), and confirms that an associated `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` record is still active.

No credentials or profile fields are included here; this operation is strictly for renewing tokens for an existing admin session.

refreshToken.description: Opaque refresh token string issued to the adminUser during login or an earlier refresh operation. It is used to request a new pair of JWT tokens without resubmitting credentials.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and pagination criteria for listing discussion board articles from `discussion_board_articles`.

This DTO is used by list/search endpoints such as:
- `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles` (general article listing)
- `PATCH /discussionBoard/memberUser/members/{memberUserId}/likedArticles` (liked-articles view)

It encapsulates pagination options, sorting preferences, and domain-specific filters so that the HTTP request body can evolve without overloading query parameters.

page.description: 1-based page index for pagination. When omitted, the service should default to the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of article summaries to return in a single page. The backend may enforce an upper bound regardless of the client-provided value.

search.description: Optional free-text search query applied to article text fields such as title and body. Implementations typically use full-text indexes for efficient search.

categoryId.description:
Optional filter for a single article category, represented by the UUID primary key of `discussion_board_article_categories.id`.

When provided, the service restricts results to articles whose foreign key column (for example, `discussion_board_article_category_id` in `discussion_board_articles`) matches this category identifier.

moderationState.description: Optional filter on the moderation or visibility state of articles (for example, `Active`, `Hidden`, or `UnderReview`). The exact set of allowed values is defined by the service implementation and Prisma enum for the article moderation field.

createdFrom.description: Optional lower bound (inclusive) for the article creation timestamp. Only articles with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value are included.

createdTo.description: Optional upper bound (inclusive) for the article creation timestamp. Only articles with `created_at` less than or equal to this value are included.

orderBy.description: Field name to use for sorting article results, such as `created_at` or `title`. The implementation should validate this against an allowlist of sortable fields.

orderDirection.description: Sort direction for the `orderBy` field. Typical values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending; the implementation validates and normalizes the value.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Detailed representation of a single discussion board article row stored in the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model.

This DTO exposes all public, non-sensitive fields required to render the full article detail view, including identifier, title, body, optional summary, category information, moderation status, and audit timestamps. It does not include any ownership or actor-identifying fields which are instead resolved via subtype tables or authentication context.

The entity is the primary content object in the economic and political discussion board domain and is typically loaded via GET `/discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}` after list/search results.

id.description: UUID primary key of the article row in `discussion_board_articles`.

title.description: Human-readable title of the discussion article as stored in `discussion_board_articles.title`. This field is required and typically subject to length validation in the service layer.

body.description: Full body text of the article, mapped from `discussion_board_articles.body`. Contains the main discussion content and may include long-form text.

summary.description:
Optional short summary or preview text of the article, mapped from a nullable summary-related column (for example `summary`) in `discussion_board_articles` when present.

When null, the client may derive a preview from the body or omit preview text entirely in list views.

category.description:
Summary information about the associated article category, resolved from `discussion_board_article_categories` using the foreign key column `discussion_board_article_category_id` in `discussion_board_articles`.

This object provides human-readable category context (such as code and name) used when rendering article detail and list views, and replaces the need for exposing the raw foreign key in this response DTO.

moderationState.description:
Business-level moderation or visibility state of the article as stored in the `moderation_state` column of `discussion_board_articles`.

Typical values might represent states like "Active", "Hidden", or "Deleted", but the exact enumeration is determined by the Prisma schema and service layer rules.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the article row was first created in `discussion_board_articles`, mapped from the `created_at` column.

Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC) and used for chronological sorting and audit purposes.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when the article row was last updated in `discussion_board_articles`, mapped from the `updated_at` column.

Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format (UTC). Equal to `createdAt` for articles that have never been edited.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Creation request DTO for inserting a new discussion article row into the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model.

This type includes only client-writable fields required to create an article: `title`, `body`, an optional `summary`, and the foreign key identifying the category. Server-managed columns such as `id`, `moderation_state`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` from `discussion_board_articles` are never accepted from the client and are initialized exclusively by the service according to business rules and moderation policies.

title.description:
Title of the new discussion article, mapped to the non-nullable `discussion_board_articles.title` column.

This value must be non-empty and respect any minimum and maximum length constraints defined for article titles in the business rules, because it is a required field used in both browsing and detailed reading views.

body.description:
Full body text of the new article, mapped directly to the non-nullable `discussion_board_articles.body` column.

This field contains the primary discussion content authored by the user and must satisfy any length and content validation rules applied to article bodies in the service layer.

summary.description:
Optional short summary or preview text for the article, mapped to the nullable `summary` column in `discussion_board_articles`.

When provided, this text is typically used in list or preview displays. When omitted or set to null, the server may derive a preview from the body or choose not to show a summary at all.

categoryId.description:
UUID of the category under which the article is created, mapped to the non-nullable foreign key column `discussion_board_article_category_id` in `discussion_board_articles` that references `discussion_board_article_categories.id`.

The service validates that this identifier refers to an existing, non-retired category and may leverage the index on `(discussion_board_article_category_id, created_at)` for efficient category-scoped listings.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a discussion board article category backed by the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model.

This DTO intentionally includes only lightweight identification and display fields—`id`, `code`, `name`, and optional `description`—and omits configuration and audit columns such as `order`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at`. It is optimized for list views, filters, and embedding inside other entities where full category administration metadata is not required.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the discussion board article category, mapped to the primary key `discussion_board_article_categories.id`.

This value is stable and used as the target of the foreign key column `discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_article_category_id`.

code.description:
Machine-friendly unique code for the category, mapped from `discussion_board_article_categories.code`, such as `"ECONOMY"` or `"POLITICS"`.

This value is treated as a stable identifier for backend logic and integrations, while still being readable enough to appear in configuration UIs, URLs, or filters when appropriate.

name.description:
Human-readable name of the article category, mapped from `discussion_board_article_categories.name`.

This is the label typically shown to end users in article creation forms, filter controls, and badges attached to article metadata.

description.description:
Optional longer description of what the category is intended for, mapped from the nullable `discussion_board_article_categories.description` column.

This text is primarily used in administrative or configuration screens to document the expected scope, example topics, or guidance for when this category should be applied.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing discussion board article stored in the discussion_board_articles table.

This type models the set of fields that a member user is allowed to change when updating an article via the member-facing update endpoint. It mirrors the mutable content and classification columns of the Prisma model while excluding the primary key id, all system-managed audit fields, and any moderation or ownership fields that must remain under server-side control.

All properties are optional to support partial update semantics, but when present they must satisfy the same validation rules as on creation. Application logic is responsible for enforcing constraints such as non-empty titles, valid category references, and authorization checks to ensure that only the rightful author or privileged roles may perform updates.

title.description:
Human-readable title of the article.

Must be a non-empty string within the allowed length range for article titles when provided. Used in article listings, detail views, and search results.

body.description:
Main body text of the article.

Contains the full discussion content written by the author. When supplied in an update request, it must satisfy the same minimum and maximum length constraints as during creation.

summary.description:
Optional short plain-text summary of the article.

Used in listings or previews to give a quick overview of the content. When present, it should remain within a small maximum length. A null value explicitly clears any existing summary.

discussion_board_article_category_id.description:
Foreign key referencing the category of this article.

When provided, it must correspond to an existing discussion_board_article_categories.id value. Changing this field reclassifies the article into a different category.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying article categories from the discussion_board_article_categories table.

This type encapsulates all parameters used to retrieve a filtered and paginated list of category records for use in navigation UIs, article creation workflows, and administrative tools. It allows clients to specify which slice of categories they need, how they should be ordered, and what filter criteria to apply.

The DTO is intentionally flexible and uses only request-scoped fields, so it does not map directly to a single Prisma model via x-autobe-prisma-schema. Instead, its properties drive query construction against the discussion_board_article_categories schema, including WHERE, ORDER BY, SKIP, and TAKE clauses.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination.

Controls which logical page of results is returned. When omitted, the backend should default to the first page. Values less than 1 are considered invalid and should be rejected.

limit.description:
Maximum number of category records to return in a single page.

Used together with page to implement pagination. When omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

search.description:
Optional free-text search term applied to category name and description.

When provided, the backend should perform a simple text search, typically using a trigram or ILIKE match on the name and description columns of discussion_board_article_categories. A null value explicitly disables text search filtering.

codes.description:
Optional list of category codes to include in the result set.

When this array is non-empty, only categories whose code matches one of the supplied values should be returned. This is useful when a client already knows which logical categories it cares about and wants only those records.

order_by.description:
Optional sort key used to determine the ordering of returned categories.

Typical values include "order" for display order or "created_at" for chronological ordering. When null or omitted, the backend should apply its default ordering strategy, often using the order column with a tie-breaker on created_at.

order_direction.description:
Optional sort direction corresponding to the chosen order_by field.

Common values are "asc" for ascending order and "desc" for descending order. When null or omitted, the backend should default to ascending order or follow its internal convention.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.description:
Discussion-board article category master entity for the economic and political discussion board.

Represents a single category such as "Economy" or "Politics" that can be assigned to articles for classification and filtering. Each category has a stable machine-friendly business code, a human-readable name, an optional description, a display order, and audit timestamps.

This DTO is a read model mapped directly from the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model and is used in responses for category detail retrieval and administrative management screens.

id.description: UUID primary key of the article category record in `discussion_board_article_categories`.

code.description:
Stable machine-friendly business code of the category (for example, `"ECONOMY"` or `"POLITICS"`).

This value maps to the `code` column in `discussion_board_article_categories` and is globally unique, used as the main external identifier in URLs and integrations.

name.description: Human-readable display name of the category, shown in user interfaces such as lists, dropdowns, and headings.

description.description:
Optional longer description explaining the category's scope and usage guidelines.

When null, no extra explanatory text is configured for this category.

order.description:
Integer indicating the display order of this category in lists or dropdowns.

Lower values generally appear earlier. This maps to the `order` column in `discussion_board_article_categories` and is typically used together with `created_at` for sorting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this category record was first created in the system.

Maps to the `created_at` column of `discussion_board_article_categories` and is expressed in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this category record.

Maps to the `updated_at` column of `discussion_board_article_categories` and is expressed in ISO 8601 format with timezone.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for this category.

When null, the category is considered active and can be used for new articles. When non-null, the category is treated as retired and should not be exposed through normal retrieval or list APIs for creating or editing content.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ICreate.description:
Request body DTO for creating a new discussion-board article category.

Used by administrative tools to register new category master data in the `discussion_board_article_categories` table. This DTO carries only client-editable business fields; system-managed columns such as `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded and will be populated by the backend.

On successful creation, the server returns the full `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory` representation of the newly created category.

code.description:
Stable machine-friendly business code to assign to the new category (for example, `"ECONOMY"` or `"POLITICS"`).

This value will be stored in the `code` column of `discussion_board_article_categories` and must be unique among all non-deleted categories.

name.description: Human-readable name of the new category, as displayed in user interfaces such as lists and dropdowns.

description.description:
Optional longer description for the category.

Use this field to describe the scope or intended usage of the category for administrative and editorial users. When omitted or null, the category has no extra descriptive text.

order.description:
Display order index for the new category.

Lower numbers generally place the category earlier in ordered lists or dropdowns. This will be persisted into the `order` column in `discussion_board_article_categories` and may participate in composite indexes together with `created_at`.

IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IUpdate.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing discussion board article category record in the `discussion_board_article_categories` table.

This DTO is used by administrative tooling when calling the update endpoint that identifies a category by its globally unique `code` (exposed as `categoryCode` in the path). It contains only mutable, business-facing fields such as `name`, `description`, and display `order`. Immutable and system-managed fields like `id`, `code`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` are excluded from the request body and are handled internally by the backend.

Consumers use this structure to adjust how a category such as "Economy" or "Politics" appears in the UI, including changing its human-readable name, long-form description, or ordering among other categories, while preserving database integrity and respecting Prisma constraints.

name.description:
Human-readable display name of the article category, such as "Economy" or "Politics".

This value is shown to end users in category lists and filters. Updating it allows administrators to refine the wording of category labels without changing the underlying business `code` used as a stable identifier.

description.description:
Optional longer description text explaining the purpose or scope of the category.

This may be used in administrative UIs or tooltips to clarify when the category should be applied. When omitted in the update payload, the existing description is left unchanged.

order.description:
Integer value used for ordering categories in listings and navigation menus.

Lower numbers typically appear earlier in sorted lists. The value should respect any composite index on `(order, created_at)` defined in the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model. When omitted, the existing ordering is preserved.

IDiscussionBoardArticleOfMemberusersMemb.description:
Public-facing view of the member user who authored a specific discussion board article.

This DTO is returned when retrieving member author information for an article via the `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` authorship link and the underlying `discussion_board_memberusers` table. It is designed for display in "article writer" panels and other UI components that show who wrote a given article.

The structure exposes only a curated subset of non-sensitive profile fields taken directly from the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma model (such as `display_name`, `bio`, and `location`), together with the stable member identifier. Sensitive columns like authentication credentials, lifecycle or restriction flags, and internal moderation metadata are intentionally excluded from this projection.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table.

This value maps to the `id` column and can be used as a stable reference when linking to other member-specific resources, such as profile pages or lists of articles authored by the same member.

displayName.description:
Public display name of the member user as shown in article author sections and comment headers.

This value comes from the `display_name` column in `discussion_board_memberusers` and typically represents a nickname or profile name selected by the user according to the account and profile rules of the service.

bio.description:
Optional short self-introduction text provided by the member user.

This field is mapped from the nullable `bio` column of `discussion_board_memberusers` and is suitable for public display near the author name, giving readers additional context about the author's background or interests.

location.description:
Optional free-text location or main interest area associated with the member user.

This value originates from the nullable `location` column in `discussion_board_memberusers` and is treated as descriptive text only, allowing the UI to show simple geographic or topical context for the article author without implying any verified address information.

IDiscussionBoardArticleOfAdminusersAdmin.description:
Public-facing admin author information for a discussion board article, resolved via the `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers` authorship link and the underlying `discussion_board_adminusers` profile.

This DTO is optimized for rendering administrator authorship metadata in the UI, such as the admin display name and role labels, while excluding any internal-only or sensitive administrator data. It is returned by read-only operations that, given an article identifier, locate the corresponding admin authorship record and join to the admin user account.

Only fields that are intended to be visible wherever admin-authored articles are presented should be included here. Internal moderation notes, privileged access scopes, contact details not meant for end users, and any authentication-related information are intentionally omitted.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator user in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table who authored the article.

This value is used internally to correlate admin-authored content and to support further admin-only operations that may need to reference the same administrator account.

displayName.description:
Display name of the administrator as shown to end users when rendering admin-authored articles.

This is typically a pseudonymous handle, staff name, or role-based label (for example, "Board Admin" or "Moderator Team") rather than a legal name, depending on service policy.

roleLabel.description:
Short textual label describing the administrator's visible role or rank on the discussion board.

Examples include values such as "Admin", "Moderator", "Staff", or more domain-specific labels like "Policy Team". This is intended purely for UI display to clarify that the article was posted by an administrator rather than a regular member.

IDiscussionBoardArticleLike.description:
Like engagement state for a single discussion board article in the economic and political discussion board.

This DTO aggregates per-member like records from the `discussion_board_article_likes` table together with the target article context. It is used by read operations to answer whether the current authenticated member user has liked the article and to expose the current total like count.

The DTO is deliberately limited to engagement-focused fields and does not expose underlying member profile details or full article content. It is safe to return to both authenticated member users and, where policy allows, to public callers when like counts are considered public information.

article.description:
Summary information about the article whose like engagement state is being represented.

This association is derived from the `discussion_board_articles` table and corresponds to the article primary key that backs the like aggregation. Using `IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary` here ensures clients have immediate access to the article identifier and key display fields without issuing an additional article-detail request.

totalLikeCount.description:
Total number of active like records associated with the article.

This count is typically computed by aggregating rows in `discussion_board_article_likes` for the given article, or by reading a denormalized counter on the article entity that is kept in sync with that table. The value is always non-negative.

likedByCurrentMember.description:
Flag indicating whether the current authenticated member user has an active like record for this article.

When the caller is an authenticated `memberUser`, this flag is derived from the presence or absence of a row in `discussion_board_article_likes` linking the member to the article. When the caller is unauthenticated or not a member user, service implementations may always return `false` here while still exposing the `totalLikeCount`. This field never reveals any information about other members.

IDiscussionBoardArticleLike.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating or confirming a like engagement on a specific article by the current authenticated member user.

This DTO maps to the `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma model but intentionally omits the actor and article identification fields because those are derived from the authenticated session and the `articleId` path parameter. It is designed to be idempotent at the business level: multiple submissions for the same article by the same member should not create duplicate like records.

Use this type when implementing `POST /discussionBoard/memberUser/articles/{articleId}/likes`. The server will combine the path parameter and authentication context to populate `discussion_board_article_id` and `discussion_board_memberuser_id` columns when persisting the like record.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for listing comments that belong to a single discussion article.

This DTO is used by the `PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments` operation to filter and page through rows in the `discussion_board_comments` table for a given parent article. It carries client-side preferences such as page index, page size, sort ordering, and optional keyword search while leaving the article scoping to the `articleId` path parameter.

Use this type for read-only comment listing scenarios on article detail screens where efficient pagination and lightweight filtering are required without exposing internal moderation or ownership details.

page.description:
1-based page index to retrieve when paginating comments for the specified article.

Typical clients start with page 1 for the first page. If omitted, the backend should apply a sensible default such as 1. Values less than 1 should be rejected or normalized to 1 according to service policy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of comments to return in a single page for the specified article.

This value controls page size for pagination. If omitted, the backend should apply a default such as 20. Very large values should be capped by server-side limits to protect performance and prevent abuse.

orderBy.description:
Logical sort field to use when ordering comments in the result set.

Common options include `"created_at"` for chronological ordering or `"updated_at"` when emphasizing recently edited comments. If omitted, the service should default to `"created_at"`.

orderDirection.description:
Direction in which to sort the comment list for the chosen `orderBy` field.

Use `"asc"` for ascending order (oldest first) and `"desc"` for descending order (newest first). When omitted, the backend should apply a default such as `"desc"` to show the most recent comments first.

search.description:
Optional free-text search keyword applied to the `body` column of `discussion_board_comments` for the scoped article.

When supplied, the backend should filter comments so that only those whose body text matches the keyword (for example via ILIKE or full-text search) are returned. When omitted or empty, no text filtering is applied.

status.description:
Optional logical status filter for comments included in the result.

Typical values align with the `status` column in `discussion_board_comments`, such as `"Active"`, `"Hidden"`, or `"Deleted"`. Public callers should normally omit this and rely on default visibility rules, while privileged callers may specify a status to target moderated or removed comments.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Discussion board comment entity representing a single text comment attached to an article.

This type exposes the core business fields from the discussion_board_comments table together with resolved author information and parent article context required to render a full comment detail view. It is used as the primary response DTO for comment retrieval, creation, and update operations.

The schema follows the polymorphic ownership pattern defined in the Prisma models, where actor-specific details live in subsidiary tables but are projected here through normalized author information suitable for API consumers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This value corresponds to discussion_board_comments.id and is generated by the system when the comment is created. Clients use this identifier in URLs and internal state to reference the comment, but never supply or modify it directly.

author_type.description:
Logical type of the comment author.

Values reflect the polymorphic ownership pattern implemented through the discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers and discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers tables. The value indicates whether the author is a member user or an admin user and is used by clients to adjust UI presentation for official moderator comments versus regular user comments.

body.description:
Main text content of the comment.

This string contains the full comment body as stored in discussion_board_comments.body. It must satisfy business-defined validation rules such as non-emptiness and maximum length limits, and it is returned exactly as persisted so that clients can render the comment without additional transformation.

status.description:
Business-level moderation status of the comment.

This field reflects the value of discussion_board_comments.status and indicates whether the comment is active, hidden, or logically deleted under the board's moderation rules. Application logic uses this status to decide what is visible to different actors, while administrators can use it to audit moderation actions.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was created.

This value corresponds to discussion_board_comments.created_at and is set by the application or database at insert time. It is used for chronological sorting, activity feeds, and audit trails and is never modified after initial creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the comment was last updated.

This field mirrors discussion_board_comments.updated_at and is refreshed whenever editable properties of the comment, such as the body text or status, change. Consumers can compare it with created_at to detect whether a comment has been edited since its original posting.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the comment, if any.

This value maps to discussion_board_comments.deleted_at and, when non-null, indicates that the comment has been logically removed according to data retention and moderation policies. In normal end-user views, comments with a non-null deleted_at are typically excluded or shown in a specially marked state depending on business rules.

article.description:
Parent article summary that this comment belongs to.

This object replaces the raw foreign key discussion_board_article_id and provides contextual information about the article associated with the comment. It enables clients to render comment details together with key article metadata without additional lookups, while avoiding circular references by using the article summary variant.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Request payload for creating a new discussion board comment on an article.

This DTO represents the subset of discussion_board_comments fields that clients are allowed to supply when posting a new comment. It excludes system-managed fields such as id, article foreign key, and timestamps, which are derived from the path parameters and authenticated actor context.

The payload focuses on the user-provided comment body and any optional structural metadata supported by the schema. Server-side logic fills in the remaining columns and creates appropriate ownership subtype records to link the comment to either a member user or an admin user.

body.description:
Text content of the comment to be created.

This value will be stored in discussion_board_comments.body after passing validation rules for minimum length, maximum length, and content policy constraints. It must contain the full visible text of the comment as entered by the user.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for an existing top-level text comment in the discussion board.

This DTO is used when a memberUser or adminUser updates a comment that already belongs to a specific article. Only business-editable fields from the `discussion_board_comments` model are exposed here. System-managed identifiers, article linkage, author linkage, and timestamps are intentionally excluded and are validated via path parameters and authentication context instead of the request body.

Typical usage is with PUT `/discussionBoard/{actor}/articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}` where `articleId` and `commentId` come from the URL path and must not be duplicated in this body. The backend maps only these mutable fields to the Prisma update operation after enforcing ownership and restriction rules.

body.description:
Updated textual body of the comment.

Represents the main message content authored by the user. Validation rules such as minimum and maximum length, allowed characters, and formatting are enforced according to the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma schema and business requirements for civility and readability.

When omitted in an update payload, the existing body remains unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest.description:
Search, sorting, and pagination parameters for listing attachments of a discussion board article.

This DTO is used as the request body for the PATCH `/discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/attachments` endpoint. It defines how clients can page through attachments, control sort order, and optionally filter by file-related attributes. The parameters here determine which rows from the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model will be included in the paginated result for the specified article.

None of the properties are required; sensible defaults are applied by the backend when they are omitted. This keeps the API simple for typical use (e.g., first page, default sort) while still enabling more advanced querying scenarios when needed.

page.description:
1-based index of the results page to retrieve.

If omitted, the backend applies a default (commonly page 1). Must be a positive integer. Combined with `limit`, it determines the offset into the list of attachments for the given article.

limit.description:
Maximum number of attachment records to return in a single page.

If omitted, the backend applies a sensible default while enforcing a maximum upper bound to protect performance. Used together with `page` to implement server-side pagination over `discussion_board_attachments`.

sortField.description:
Logical field name used to sort attachments in the results.

Typical values may include fields like `uploadedAt`, `fileName`, or `fileSize`, depending on how the listing is implemented on top of the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model. The backend validates the value against an allowed whitelist and falls back to a default sort when invalid or omitted.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction to apply when ordering attachments.

Common values are `asc` for ascending and `desc` for descending order. When omitted, the backend applies its default ordering policy, typically descending by uploaded timestamp so that the most recent attachments appear first.

fileExtension.description:
Optional filter for attachments by file extension (e.g., `pdf`, `jpg`, `png`).

When provided, only attachments whose stored extension matches this value (case-insensitively, depending on implementation) are returned. This is useful for UIs that allow users to focus on specific file types.

contentType.description:
Optional filter for attachments by MIME content type.

Examples include `application/pdf`, `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, or other MIME types stored on the `discussion_board_attachments` records. When provided, the result set is limited to attachments whose MIME type matches the given value.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.description:
Discussion board article attachment metadata.

Represents a single file attachment record stored in the discussion_board_attachments table and owned by exactly one article in discussion_board_articles. Contains only metadata and lifecycle information; the actual file content is obtained by dereferencing file_uri via the storage layer.

id.description: Unique identifier of this attachment record in discussion_board_attachments.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Identifier of the parent article in discussion_board_articles that owns this attachment.

Used internally to enforce the subsidiary relationship between attachments and articles and to validate that an attachment belongs to the article context in article-scoped operations.

file_uri.description:
Absolute or storage-relative URI pointing to the stored file object associated with this attachment.

Clients use this URI with the underlying storage system or CDN to download or display the file content. The API itself does not stream the binary data from this field.

file_name.description:
User-visible file name for this attachment.

May be derived from the original upload name or normalized according to storage rules, and is used when rendering attachment lists to end users.

content_type.description:
MIME-like media type of the stored file (for example, "image/jpeg", "image/png", "application/pdf").

Used by clients to decide preview behavior and by validation logic to enforce allowed file types.

file_size.description:
Size of the stored file in bytes.

Used for validation against maximum upload limits and for display in attachment metadata UIs.

order_in_article.description:
Display order of this attachment within its parent article.

Combined with discussion_board_article_id it is unique so that each attachment for a given article has a distinct position. Lower values are typically shown earlier in attachment lists.

status.description:
Business lifecycle and moderation status of this attachment.

Common values indicate whether the attachment is active, hidden, or otherwise restricted. Application logic and higher-privileged APIs interpret and enforce allowed values.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this attachment record was first created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this attachment record was last updated.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for this attachment.

When non-null, the attachment is considered deleted or hidden from normal user-facing operations even though the row may still exist in the database for audit or recovery purposes.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate.description:
Creation payload for a new discussion board article attachment.

Used by POST endpoints that insert a row into discussion_board_attachments for a specific parent article. The parent article identity is provided via the path parameter, so discussion_board_article_id is not part of this DTO. Only client-editable metadata fields are exposed; server-managed identifiers and timestamps are excluded.

file_uri.description:
Pre-uploaded file URI pointing to the stored file object for this attachment.

The file must already exist in the storage layer; this API only registers its metadata and association with an article.

file_name.description:
User-visible file name to associate with the attachment.

Typically derived from the original upload name but may be edited by the client at creation time.

content_type.description:
MIME-like media type for the file being attached (for example, "image/jpeg", "image/png", "application/pdf").

Validated against the allowed set of content types configured for the discussion board service.

file_size.description:
Size of the file in bytes.

Used for server-side validation against maximum attachment size limits and for later display to end users.

order_in_article.description:
Desired display order of this attachment within the parent article.

Must be unique per article together with other attachments and may be used to sort attachments in article views.

status.description:
Initial business lifecycle or moderation status for the new attachment.

Typical values indicate that the attachment is active and visible, or in a pending/hidden state according to business rules.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for discussion board attachment metadata and moderation fields.

Represents the subset of discussion_board_attachments columns that clients are allowed to modify when updating an attachment belonging to a specific article. Immutable identifiers and audit fields such as id, discussion_board_article_id, file_size, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are excluded and controlled exclusively by the server.

file_name.description:
Human-readable file name label shown to users for this attachment.

Maps to the discussion_board_attachments.file_name column. Used as the display name in article views and download links. When omitted in an update request, the existing value is preserved.

content_type.description:
MIME content type string describing the attachment payload, such as "application/pdf" or "image/png".

Maps to the discussion_board_attachments.content_type column. May be updated when the file has been reclassified or the original type was inferred incorrectly.

order_in_article.description:
Display ordering index of the attachment within its parent article.

Maps to the discussion_board_attachments.order_in_article column. The backend enforces uniqueness of this value per article according to the unique index on (discussion_board_article_id, order_in_article). Clients can change this value to reorder attachments.

status.description:
Moderation and lifecycle status of the attachment.

Maps to the discussion_board_attachments.status column. Typical values include statuses such as "active" or "hidden" to indicate whether the attachment is visible in the UI. The application layer validates allowed transitions and concrete enumeration values.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for querying discussion board reports.

Represents complex search criteria, filters, sorting options, and pagination settings used when listing discussion_board_reports for moderation screens. This DTO is used both for global report listings and for scoped queries such as reports associated with a specific attachment on an article.

page.description:
1-based page index for paginated report listings.

Determines which page of results to return. Combined with the limit field to control pagination window.

limit.description:
Maximum number of report summary records to return per page.

Used together with the page parameter to paginate large report sets. The backend may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

status.description:
Filter for report status.

Represents the current moderation workflow state of the report, such as "open", "in_review", or "resolved". The exact allowed values are enforced by the application layer and correspond to the status field in discussion_board_reports.

target_type.description:
Filter by the type of content that has been reported.

Typically distinguishes between reports targeting an "article", a "comment", or an "attachment". When omitted, reports of all target types are included.

reporter_type.description:
Filter by the account type of the reporting actor.

Used to restrict results to reports created by a particular reporter category, such as "guestUser", "memberUser", or "adminUser". The backend interprets and validates concrete values based on business rules.

created_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the report creation timestamp range filter.

When provided together with created_to, constrains the listing to reports whose created_at value in discussion_board_reports falls within the specified range.

created_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the report creation timestamp range filter.

Used with created_from to filter reports by creation date window for moderation review.

order_by.description:
Column or logical field name used to sort report results.

Typical values include "created_at" or "status" so that moderators can view the most recent or specific-state reports first. The backend validates allowed sort keys to prevent arbitrary column access.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction indicator for ordered report listings.

Usually either "asc" for ascending or "desc" for descending order. Invalid values are rejected by server-side validation.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.description:
Guest user placeholder account entity for the discussion board service.

Represents an unauthenticated or minimally identified visitor tracked by the system for actions such as content browsing, simple interactions, or reporting without requiring full member registration. The record is identified by a UUID primary key and is primarily used by administrative and operational tools for auditing and abuse investigation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the guest user placeholder record.

This maps to the `id` primary key column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table.

anonymous_token.description:
Opaque correlation token that identifies this guest user across visits.

This maps to the `anonymous_token` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table and is typically constrained by a unique index to ensure each token identifies at most one guest record.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user placeholder was created.

Maps to the non-nullable `created_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user placeholder was last updated.

Maps to the non-nullable `updated_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table, which is refreshed whenever the record is modified.

deleted_at.description:
Logical deletion timestamp for this guest user placeholder.

Maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column of the `discussion_board_guestusers` table. When non-null, the record is considered closed or no longer active.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for querying guest user placeholder accounts.

Used by the `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/guestUsers` endpoint to express complex search conditions, sorting, and pagination over the `discussion_board_guestusers` table. This DTO is strictly read-only and is consumed only as a filter definition, never to create or update records.
