page.description:
1-based page index for paginated results.

If omitted, the backend should assume a sensible default such as page 1.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return per page.

If omitted, the backend should use a service-level default and may enforce an upper bound to protect performance.

oneOf.description:
Field by which to order the guest user records.

Typical options include `created_at` (creation time), `updated_at` (last modification time), or `deleted_at` (logical deletion time).

Field by which to order the guest user records.

Typical options include `created_at` (creation time), `updated_at` (last modification time), or `deleted_at` (logical deletion time).

Field by which to order the guest user records.

Typical options include `created_at` (creation time), `updated_at` (last modification time), or `deleted_at` (logical deletion time).

order_by.description:
Field by which to order the guest user records.

Typical options include `created_at` (creation time), `updated_at` (last modification time), or `deleted_at` (logical deletion time).

oneOf.description:
Sort direction to apply to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order.

Sort direction to apply to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order.

order_direction.description:
Sort direction to apply to the `order_by` field.

Use `asc` for ascending order or `desc` for descending order.

created_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `created_at` greater than or equal to this value should be returned.

created_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the creation timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `created_at` less than or equal to this value should be returned.

updated_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the last-updated timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `updated_at` greater than or equal to this value should be returned.

updated_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the last-updated timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `updated_at` less than or equal to this value should be returned.

deleted_from.description:
Lower bound (inclusive) of the logical deletion timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `deleted_at` greater than or equal to this value should be returned. Records with `deleted_at = null` are typically excluded unless business rules define otherwise.

deleted_to.description:
Upper bound (inclusive) of the logical deletion timestamp range filter.

When provided, only guest users with `deleted_at` less than or equal to this value should be returned.

anonymous_token.description:
Optional filter on the `anonymous_token` correlation value.

When specified, only guest user placeholder records whose `anonymous_token` exactly matches this value should be returned.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary projection of a guest user placeholder account within the discussion board service.

Guest user records represent optional persisted identities for unauthenticated visitors. This summary exposes only the opaque tracking token and lifecycle timestamps needed for diagnostics, analytics, or potential migration flows, without any personal profile or permission information.

It is suitable for administrative tooling or internal dashboards where operators need to see the existence and age of guest records without detailed activity expansion.

id.description:
Primary identifier of the guest user placeholder.

This maps to `discussion_board_guestusers.id` and uniquely distinguishes one guest record from another for internal reference and debugging.

anonymous_token.description:
Opaque token that represents this guest user across visits.

The token is stored in `discussion_board_guestusers.anonymous_token` and may be encoded into cookies or other client-side storage. It must not be interpreted by clients and is treated purely as an identifier for correlation and potential migration to a full member account.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this guest user record was initially created.

Derived from `discussion_board_guestusers.created_at`, this is used to understand the age of the guest identity and to drive cleanup or retention policies.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest user record was last updated.

This value mirrors `discussion_board_guestusers.updated_at` and changes when any server-side maintenance or correlation operation modifies the guest record.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the guest user record.

When `null`, the guest account is considered active or at least retained. When populated with a date-time value from `discussion_board_guestusers.deleted_at`, the record is logically closed and may be pending physical cleanup depending on data retention rules.

IDiscussionBoardGuestUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for guest user placeholder accounts stored in the discussion_board_guestusers table.

This type is used by administrative tooling to adjust mutable attributes of a guest user placeholder record, such as rotating the anonymous_token used to correlate a guest across visits or marking the record as logically deleted through the deleted_at lifecycle field.

The id primary key and the created_at timestamp are intentionally excluded from this DTO to preserve the integrity of the original creation event, while updated_at is managed by the backend when changes are persisted.

anonymous_token.description:
Opaque token or fingerprint that represents this guest user across visits.

In the underlying discussion_board_guestusers Prisma model this field is constrained by a unique index, ensuring that no two guest placeholder records share the same token. When present in this update DTO, the value must respect that uniqueness constraint and any conflict will surface as a validation or conflict error.

Administrative tooling may use this field to rotate or correct the correlation token under controlled circumstances.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp used to mark the guest user placeholder as closed or no longer in active use.

When set to a valid ISO 8601 date-time string, the record is treated as logically deleted by higher-level business logic while remaining in storage for historical or analytical purposes. A null value indicates that the record is currently active.

This field maps directly to the nullable deleted_at column in the discussion_board_guestusers Prisma model and must not be used to backdate creation or other lifecycle events.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.IReque.description:
Search and pagination parameters for listing member user sessions.

This DTO is used when querying discussion_board_memberuser_sessions for a single parent member user, as identified by the memberUserId path parameter on the API. It encapsulates filtering and paging concerns without exposing any authentication secrets or token internals.

Typical requests specify a page/limit combination, and may constrain the time window of sessions to recent history or a particular audit period. These criteria allow administrative and security dashboards to efficiently browse a member’s session activity.

page.description:
Page number for paginated session results.

This value controls which slice of the member’s session list is returned from discussion_board_memberuser_sessions. Page numbering is one-based by convention, but the exact convention is enforced by the application layer.

Clients should provide positive integers and combine this with the limit property to implement stable pagination across repeated queries.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return in a single response page.

This property defines the page size when listing rows from discussion_board_memberuser_sessions for a given member user. Service implementations typically enforce an upper bound to prevent excessively large result sets from impacting performance.

When omitted, the backend may apply a sensible default page size so that callers are not required to specify this field for common use cases.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the creation timestamp range filter for sessions.

When provided, only sessions whose created_at value on discussion_board_memberuser_sessions is greater than or equal to this timestamp are eligible to appear in the results. This allows callers to focus on recent sessions or a particular investigative window.

If null or omitted, no lower time bound is applied and all older sessions for the member user may be considered by the query.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the creation timestamp range filter for sessions.

When set, the listing includes only sessions whose created_at value on discussion_board_memberuser_sessions is less than or equal to this timestamp. Combined with created_from, this enables querying sessions within a precise auditing interval.

If null or not supplied, no upper time bound is enforced and newer sessions remain eligible to appear in the paginated result set.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.description:
Discussion board member user session entity representing a single authenticated browsing session for a registered member.

This DTO mirrors the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions Prisma model and is used as a read-only response type when administrators inspect an individual member session. It exposes identifying information, the owning member reference, and connection context such as IP and entry URLs to support audit and security review flows.

The type is never used for login, logout, or any session lifecycle mutation. It is only returned from administrative inspection APIs and therefore omits any actor identity fields that come from authentication context, focusing purely on persisted session attributes.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user session.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table and uniquely distinguishes each persisted session row for a member user. It is generated by the system and is immutable for the lifetime of the record.

discussion_board_memberuser_id.description:
Identifier of the member user who owns this session.

This field stores the foreign key that links the session record back to the parent member user in the discussion_board_memberusers table. It is used only for read-side traceability and authorization checks and is never supplied by clients when reading session data.

ip.description:
IP address from which the member user established this session.

The value captures the remote IP observed at the time the session was created and is used for security analysis, anomaly detection, and audit trails. Implementations may normalize IPv4 and IPv6 representations but always expose the final stored string from the underlying Prisma model.

href.description:
Full URL that the member user accessed when this session was created.

This value records the entry URL used when the session was first established, such as the page where the user logged in or first arrived. It helps administrators reconstruct navigation context during security investigations.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL, if any, that led the member user into the application for this session.

The value reflects the HTTP referrer recorded when the session started, allowing audit tooling to understand how the user reached the site or login flow. It may be an empty or generic URL depending on client behavior but always reflects the stored database value.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this member session was created.

The value is stored in the database as a datetime column and represents the moment the session was first persisted. It is written once at session creation and never modified afterwards, enabling chronological analysis of session history.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when this member session was considered expired or terminated, or null while still active.

When populated, this datetime marks the point at which the session is no longer considered valid for authentication or tracking purposes. While the session remains active, the field stays null, allowing consumers to easily distinguish active from closed sessions.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuserSession.IReques.description:
Search and filtering request for listing admin user sessions belonging to a specific administrator.

This DTO encapsulates query, filter, and pagination parameters used by the admin session search endpoint that operates over the discussion_board_adminuser_sessions Prisma model. It allows callers to narrow results based on common auditing dimensions such as time ranges and connection context, while delegating the actual admin user identity to the path parameter.

The structure is intentionally focused on read-only inspection flows and does not participate in session lifecycle management. All fields are optional so that callers can combine filters as needed, and implementations are expected to apply sensible defaults when values are omitted.

page.description:
One-based page index to retrieve when listing admin user sessions.

When provided, this value selects which logical page of results should be returned, with 1 representing the first page. If omitted, the backend may default to the first page according to its pagination strategy.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin session records to return in a single page.

This value controls the page size for the session listing. Implementations may enforce an upper bound regardless of the client-supplied value to protect system performance and should apply a sensible default when the field is not provided.

from_created_at.description:
Inclusive lower bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

When specified, only sessions whose created_at value is greater than or equal to this datetime are included in the result set. Use this field together with to_created_at to define an auditing window for admin session analysis.

to_created_at.description:
Exclusive upper bound for the session creation timestamp filter.

When provided, sessions whose created_at value is greater than or or equal to this datetime may be excluded according to the implementation's range semantics, effectively closing the time window started by from_created_at. If null or omitted, the upper bound is unbounded.

ip.description:
Optional filter for the originating IP address of admin sessions.

When present, only sessions whose stored IP value matches this string are considered for inclusion in the result set. This allows administrators to inspect activity from a specific source address as part of security monitoring or incident investigation.

href.description:
Optional filter for the entry URL recorded when the admin session was created.

Supplying this value restricts the search to sessions that began on the specified URL, which can be useful when analyzing usage patterns of particular administrative pages or entry points within the system.

referrer.description:
Optional filter for the referrer URL associated with admin sessions.

When provided, the search is constrained to sessions whose recorded referrer matches this value. This helps auditors understand access originating from a particular external or internal navigation path.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuserSession.description:
Represents a single administrator session record within the discussion board system.

This DTO is a read-only projection of the discussion_board_adminuser_sessions Prisma model, used by administrative audit APIs to expose when and how an admin user connected to the system. It captures the linkage to the owning admin account, the originating IP address, the entry URL, optional referrer context, and lifecycle timestamps.

The data in this type is security sensitive and is only returned to authenticated administrative actors. It is never accepted as input from clients, and session creation and expiration are managed exclusively by the authentication subsystem rather than by normal REST handlers.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session.

This value maps to the primary key of the discussion_board_adminuser_sessions table and is used as the stable handle for referencing the session in audit APIs and logging. It is generated by the backend and is never provided by clients.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin user established this session.

The value is captured by the backend from the incoming HTTP request at login time and stored for audit and security analysis. It may contain either IPv4 or IPv6 representations, depending on the deployment environment.

href.description:
Full URL that the administrator accessed when this session was created.

This field allows auditors to understand the entry point of the admin into the system, including path and query parameters. It is stored exactly as observed at session establishment time and is not modified afterwards.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that led the administrator into the application for this session, if available.

The value is derived from the HTTP Referer header at the time the session was established and helps correlate navigation flows between external systems and the admin console.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session was created.

This value records the exact moment the login was established and the session row was inserted in the database. It is managed solely by the backend and is always stored in a consistent server-side time basis, typically UTC.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin session expired or was explicitly terminated.

When null, the session is still considered active according to the session subsystem. When populated, the timestamp indicates the moment at which the session became invalid for further authentication, either due to timeout or explicit logout.

adminUser.description:
Summary information about the administrator who owns this session.

This association is a BELONGS-TO reference to the `discussion_board_adminusers` entity and is exposed as a summary DTO so that audit and monitoring tools can easily correlate sessions with admin profiles without issuing additional lookups.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction.description:
Represents the current moderation restriction state for a single member user account in the discussion board.

This DTO is backed by the discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions Prisma model, which holds at most one active row per member user. It describes how the member’s ability to post articles, comments, or attachments is constrained, along with high-level reason categorization and timing information.

The type is used by both member-facing and admin-facing APIs to surface whether a member is blocked, partially restricted, or allowed to participate normally. Creation and updates are performed only by administrative workflows, while member-facing APIs consume this type read-only to adjust UI behavior and permission checks.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the restriction record.

This is the primary key of the discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions table. It is generated by the backend when the restriction is created and remains stable for the lifetime of the record.

restriction_level.description:
Level of moderation restriction applied to the member user.

Typical values include business-specific codes such as posting_restriction or full_block, indicating whether the member is prevented from posting entirely or subject to narrower limitations. The exact allowed values are governed by moderation policy and should be validated by service logic.

reason_category.description:
High-level category describing why the restriction was applied.

Examples include repeated_violations, hate_abuse, or spam_advertising. This categorization helps administrators filter and report on restriction reasons across the discussion board and can be used in analytics and moderation dashboards.

started_at.description:
Timestamp when this restriction became effective for the member user.

This value marks the beginning of the moderation window and is used by downstream permission checks to determine whether the restriction is currently in force. It is typically set at creation time and is not modified except when correcting administrative errors.

ended_at.description:
Timestamp when this restriction was lifted or scheduled to end.

When null, the restriction is considered ongoing and remains in effect until explicitly updated. When populated, permission logic compares this timestamp to the current time to decide whether the member is still restricted.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this restriction record was created.

This field is managed by the backend when the row is inserted and provides an audit trail for when moderation action was initially taken against the member account.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this restriction record was last updated.

Each administrative modification to the restriction, such as changing the level, adjusting the reason category, or setting an end time, updates this value. It enables administrators to track how recently moderation decisions were changed.

memberUser.description:
Summary information about the member user to whom this restriction applies.

This association replaces the raw foreign key `discussion_board_memberuser_id` and provides a lightweight view of the owning member account, such as identifier and display attributes, without introducing circular references.

Admin-facing tools can use this summary to display who is restricted directly within restriction listings and detail views, while more detailed member information can be retrieved via dedicated member user APIs when necessary.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction.IC.description:
Create DTO for registering a new restriction state for a discussion-board member user.

This type is used exclusively by administrative moderation workflows when applying a fresh restriction row into the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table for a target member account stored in `discussion_board_memberusers`. The actual member user identifier is supplied as a path parameter on the endpoint and mapped to the `discussion_board_memberuser_id` foreign key on the server side, so it is intentionally omitted from this DTO.

The DTO focuses on business attributes that describe the restriction itself, including the restriction level, the high‑level reason category, and the time window in which the restriction is effective. It mirrors the non‑key, non‑system columns of the Prisma model while excluding system‑managed timestamps such as `created_at` and `updated_at`, which are populated automatically by the backend when the record is created.

restriction_level.description:
Restriction level applied to the target member user account.

This value corresponds to the `restriction_level` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table and describes how strongly the user is limited, for example values like `posting_restriction` or `full_block` as used by the moderation domain.

API implementations should treat this field as a business enumeration backed by configuration or validation logic, ensuring that only supported restriction levels can be stored. Clients must always provide a non‑empty value when creating a restriction.

reason_category.description:
High‑level category that explains why the restriction is being applied.

This field mirrors the `reason_category` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` Prisma model and is intended for coarse‑grained grouping of moderation reasons, such as `repeated_violations`, `hate_abuse`, or `spam_advertising`.

Administrative tools use this value for reporting, filtering, and summarizing moderation actions, so clients should select a value from the allowed set defined by product policy.

started_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the restriction becomes effective for the member user.

This property maps directly to the non‑nullable `started_at` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table and must be provided for every created restriction row. The value should be expressed as an ISO 8601 date‑time string in UTC.

Downstream article, comment, and attachment posting logic compares this value with the current time to determine whether the restriction is already in effect.

ended_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the restriction stops being effective for the member user, or null for an ongoing restriction.

This field corresponds to the nullable `ended_at` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table. When provided as a date‑time value, it marks the moment after which the restriction is considered inactive.

If omitted or set to null at creation time, the restriction is treated as open‑ended until it is later updated by an administrative workflow via the update endpoint.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserRestriction.IU.description:
Update DTO for modifying an existing restriction state for a discussion‑board member user.

This type is used by administrative moderation tools to adjust or lift a previously created restriction row in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table. The target record is resolved on the server side using the `memberUserId` path parameter, which is mapped to the `discussion_board_memberuser_id` foreign key, so no identifier fields are included in this DTO.

All properties are optional and represent mutable business attributes of the restriction: administrators may escalate or downgrade the restriction level, adjust the reason category after review, or change the active time window by editing the `started_at` and `ended_at` timestamps. System‑managed timestamps such as `created_at` and `updated_at` are excluded and remain under backend control.

restriction_level.description:
New restriction level to apply to the existing restriction record, if it needs to be changed.

This field maps to the `restriction_level` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table. When present in an update request, it instructs the backend to modify the persisted level, for example escalating from `posting_restriction` to `full_block` or relaxing the restriction according to moderation policy.

If omitted, the existing restriction level is left unchanged.

reason_category.description:
Updated high‑level reason category that explains why the restriction is in place.

This property corresponds to the `reason_category` column in the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` model. Administrative users may revise it to better reflect the outcome of a review process or to correct the classification of the underlying behavior while preserving the historical record.

If not provided in the update payload, the reason category stored on the restriction row remains unchanged.

started_at.description:
Revised timestamp indicating when the restriction becomes effective, if the active window should be shifted.

This property maps to the non‑nullable `started_at` column of the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table. When supplied, the backend updates the start time used by downstream authorization checks to determine whether the restriction currently applies.

If this field is omitted from the update request, the existing `started_at` value on the restriction record is preserved.

ended_at.description:
New end timestamp for the restriction, or null to clear any previously set end time.

This field corresponds to the nullable `ended_at` column of the `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions` table. Providing a concrete date‑time value adjusts when the restriction is considered no longer active, while sending null explicitly clears the end time and makes the restriction open‑ended again.

If the property is not included in the update request at all, the stored `ended_at` value remains unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardReport.description:
Primary entity representing a single report filed against an article, comment, or attachment in the discussion board.

Each record in this schema corresponds to a row in the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model and captures core moderation metadata such as the type of content being reported, the type of reporter, the reason code, free-text description, workflow status, and chosen administrative action.

The report lifecycle is independent from the lifecycle of the underlying content or reporter account and provides an append-only audit trail for moderation activities.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the report stored in `discussion_board_reports.id`.

This value is used as the primary reference for all operations that retrieve, relate, or audit this report record.

Link tables such as `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers` reference this identifier via their `discussion_board_report_id` columns.

target_type.description:
Discriminator describing the type of content targeted by this report.

Typical values are `"article"`, `"comment"`, or `"attachment"`, representing whether the report is against a post, a comment, or an attached file respectively.

The allowed values and their semantics are enforced at the application layer based on business rules from the discussion board requirements.

reporter_type.description:
Discriminator indicating the actor type that submitted this report.

Common values include `"memberuser"` for regular members and `"adminuser"` for administrator-originated reports.

This field is used to determine which reporter link table (`discussion_board_report_of_memberusers` or `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`) should have an associated row and to drive authorization and UI logic in moderation tools.

reason_code.description:
Machine-friendly code identifying the primary reason category for this report.

Example values are `"hate_abuse"`, `"harassment"`, `"spam"`, `"off_topic"`, `"dangerous_misleading"`, and `"other"`, matching the content moderation and reporting rules defined for the service.

Validation of allowed codes and the mapping to localized display labels are handled at the application layer and in the front-end, not by the database schema.

description.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter to add detail beyond the reason code.

Business rules typically require this field when `reason_code` is set to `"other"`, so that moderators have enough context to act, but at the schema level the column is nullable to support existing data and flexibility.

When present, the contents should be short, human-readable text that respects the service's civility and privacy guidelines.

status.description:
Current workflow status of the report.

Typical values are `"submitted"`, `"in_review"`, or `"resolved"`, representing new, actively handled, and completed reports respectively.

Moderation queues and dashboards filter by this field to separate unprocessed reports from those already handled or closed.

action.description:
Administrative decision applied as a result of this report.

Examples include `"none"`, `"keep"`, `"hide_content"`, `"delete_content"`, and `"restrict_user"`, corresponding to the range of moderation outcomes supported by the business rules.

The combination of `status` and `action` communicates both the lifecycle stage and the final moderation result for the reported content.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was created and initially submitted by the reporter.

This value is used for chronological ordering, time-based filtering, and for auditing when a report entered the system.

It is set once at creation and is not modified during subsequent status or action changes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report record was last updated.

This is typically advanced when moderators change the `status`, update the `action`, or edit other moderation-related attributes.

Audit and monitoring tools use this value to track recent activity in the reporting system and to identify reports that may have been stale for too long.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion board report.

Used by authenticated member users (and in some cases admin users) when reporting problematic content on the board. Captures the report category, free-text reason, and target content identifiers. The implementation will translate these fields into a primary report row in `discussion_board_reports` and appropriate link records in subsidiary tables such as `discussion_board_report_of_articles`, `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, and `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`.

The `category` field is mapped onto the `reason_code` column of the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model and must be one of the allowed business reason codes such as `"hate_abuse"`, `"harassment"`, `"spam"`, `"off_topic"`, `"dangerous_misleading"`, or `"other"`. The free-text `reason` is persisted into the nullable `description` column and is typically required by business rules when the category corresponds to a generic or "other" reason.

Reporter identity and workflow fields such as `reporter_type`, `target_type`, `status`, `action`, and timestamps are derived entirely from the authenticated context and server logic. Callers cannot influence these internal moderation fields; they are managed by administrator-only workflows after the report has been created.

Exactly one of `target_article_id`, `target_comment_id`, or `target_attachment_id` must be provided. The service infers `target_type` from which of these identifiers is present and then creates the appropriate link record to associate the new report with an article, comment, or attachment. Requests that omit all target identifiers or that specify more than one will be rejected by validation logic.

category.description:
High-level category of the report selected by the reporting user (for example, hate, spam, misinformation, or personal attack).

At persistence time, this business-level choice is mapped to the `reason_code` column of the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model. Typical allowed reason codes include values such as `"hate_abuse"`, `"harassment"`, `"spam"`, `"off_topic"`, `"dangerous_misleading"`, and `"other"`, and the application layer enforces which codes are valid for the service.

Clients should treat this field as a constrained set of values exposed by the UI rather than an arbitrary string, ensuring consistent moderation reporting and accurate aggregation of report statistics.

reason.description:
Free-text explanation describing why the target content should be considered problematic from the reporter’s perspective.

This text is stored in the nullable `description` column of the `discussion_board_reports` table and gives moderators additional context beyond the high-level category. Business rules typically require a non-empty explanation when the selected `category` / `reason_code` corresponds to a generic or "other" option.

Content entered here should follow the service’s civility and privacy guidelines, avoiding unnecessary disclosure of personal information while giving enough detail for a reviewer to understand the concern.

target_article_id.description:
Identifier of the article being reported when the target is an article.

This value must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing row in the `discussion_board_articles` table that is in a reportable state according to business rules. Exactly one of `target_article_id`, `target_comment_id`, or `target_attachment_id` should be supplied for a single report creation request.

When this field is present (and the comment and attachment identifiers are absent), the service infers the `target_type` as `"article"` and creates a link row in `discussion_board_report_of_articles` that associates the newly created report with the specified article.

target_comment_id.description:
Identifier of the comment being reported when the target is a comment.

This value must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing row in the `discussion_board_comments` table that can be reported. Exactly one of `target_article_id`, `target_comment_id`, or `target_attachment_id` should be supplied for a single report creation request.

When this field is present (and the article and attachment identifiers are absent), the service infers the `target_type` as `"comment"` and creates a link row in `discussion_board_report_of_comments` that associates the newly created report with the specified comment.

target_attachment_id.description:
Identifier of the attachment being reported when the target is an attachment.

This value must be a valid UUID corresponding to an existing row in the `discussion_board_attachments` table that is eligible for reporting. Exactly one of `target_article_id`, `target_comment_id`, or `target_attachment_id` should be supplied for a single report creation request.

When this field is present (and the article and comment identifiers are absent), the service infers the `target_type` as `"attachment"` and creates a link row in `discussion_board_report_of_attachments` that associates the newly created report with the specified attachment.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IUpdate.description:
Mutable fields for updating a discussion board report in the `discussion_board_reports` table.

This DTO is used by administrative moderation tools when changing the workflow status or resolution outcome of an existing report record. It intentionally exposes only those fields that are allowed to change after creation and never includes immutable identifiers, reporter identity, or target linkage.

The shape of this type is derived directly from the `discussion_board_reports` Prisma model and follows the business rules described in the reporting and moderation requirements. Fields such as `target_type`, `reporter_type`, and `reason_code` remain read-only at the API level and are therefore not present in this update contract.

status.description:
Workflow status of the report.

This value reflects the current position of the report in the moderation lifecycle, for example `submitted`, `in_review`, or `resolved`. Only administrators are allowed to change the status, and the service layer must enforce valid transitions according to the moderation rules (e.g., from `submitted` to `in_review`, or from `in_review` to `resolved`).

When updating, this field is optional so that callers can change only other mutable fields without forcing a status change.

action.description:
Administrative action chosen as the resolution for this report.

Typical values include `none`, `keep`, `hide_content`, `delete_content`, and `restrict_user`. The allowed set is enforced on the application side and should be consistent with the moderation policy documentation.

During an update, this field may be supplied together with `status` to mark the report as resolved with a specific outcome, but it can also be omitted when only the workflow status is being adjusted.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfArticle.description:
Composite view of a discussion board report that specifically targets an article.

This DTO aggregates the base report information from the `discussion_board_reports` primary model with the article-link information from the `discussion_board_report_of_articles` subsidiary model. It is designed for administrative moderation tools that need to inspect both the report metadata and the associated article context in a single response.

The type does not contain any collections or reverse relationships and is strictly read-only at the API level. It reflects current database state without exposing any mutation-specific fields.

report.description:
Base report information drawn from the `discussion_board_reports` table.

This nested object contains the core metadata of the report such as `id`, `target_type`, `reporter_type`, `reason_code`, `description`, `status`, `action`, and timestamps. It provides moderators with the full audit context around why the report exists and how it has been processed so far.

Because the underlying report is the central entity for all targets, this property is always present for article-targeting reports.

article.description:
Summary information about the article that is the target of this report.

This property represents the association from the report to the underlying `discussion_board_articles` row via the `discussion_board_report_of_articles` link entity. It exposes only the summary DTO so that moderators can see which article is being reported, without inlining the full article composition tree.

Using the `.ISummary` variant here follows the standard association pattern for response DTOs, enables atomic read of report context in a single call, and prevents circular or overly heavy nesting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report-to-article association was created.

The value is stored on the `discussion_board_report_of_articles` link row and usually matches or closely follows the `created_at` timestamp of the underlying report. It is included here so that moderators can see when this particular association was recorded without having to inspect the link table directly.

This field is managed by the persistence layer and is immutable after insertion.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfComment.description:
Aggregated DTO representing a single discussion board report that targets a comment.

This type composes the primary report row from the `discussion_board_reports` table together with its one-to-one link row from `discussion_board_report_of_comments`. It is designed for administrative moderation flows that need to inspect why a comment was reported and which exact comment is involved.

The structure exposes core moderation workflow fields from the base report (reason, status, action, reporter and target type, timestamps) alongside the identifier of the reported comment and the timestamp when the association between the report and comment was created. It does not include any heavy collections or comment detail arrays, which are retrieved via separate endpoints when needed.

id.description:
Primary key of the report.

This value comes directly from `discussion_board_reports.id` and uniquely identifies the report across the moderation system. It is used as the path parameter `reportId` in the corresponding GET operation and serves as the join key to subsidiary link entities such as `discussion_board_report_of_comments`, `discussion_board_report_of_attachments`, or other target-specific tables.

target_type.description:
Discriminator describing which type of content this report targets.

The underlying `discussion_board_reports.target_type` column indicates whether the report is for an article, comment, or attachment. For this DTO the logical expectation is that the value is "comment", but the field is exposed so that moderation tools can detect and guard against mismatches.

Allowed values are enforced at the application layer based on business rules rather than a strict database enum.

reporter_type.description:
Discriminator describing which actor type submitted the report.

Backed by `discussion_board_reports.reporter_type`, this string captures the coarse-grained origin of the report, such as `memberuser` or `adminuser`. It allows administrators to distinguish between user-submitted reports and system or staff-initiated reports during moderation review.

reason_code.description:
Machine-friendly code representing the primary category for this report.

This is mapped from `discussion_board_reports.reason_code` and encodes the main reason chosen by the reporter, for example `hate_abuse`, `harassment`, `spam`, `off_topic`, `dangerous_misleading`, or `other`. Validation of the allowed codes and additional business rules are implemented at the service layer rather than a strict database enum.

description.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter.

This corresponds to the nullable `discussion_board_reports.description` column. It typically contains human-readable detail that elaborates on the selected `reason_code`. When the reason code is `other`, business rules often require this field to be non-empty, but the schema allows null to keep the database flexible.

When null, no additional textual explanation was supplied beyond the reason code.

status.description:
Current workflow status of the report.

Backed by `discussion_board_reports.status`, this field tracks the moderation lifecycle, with typical values such as `submitted`, `in_review`, or `resolved`. It is used to drive moderator queues, filters, and escalation flows.

Transitions between statuses are controlled by dedicated update operations and must not be changed by this read-only retrieval endpoint.

action.description:
Administrative decision applied for this report.

This string maps to `discussion_board_reports.action` and captures how moderators have decided to handle the reported content. Example values include `none`, `keep`, `hide_content`, `delete_content`, or `restrict_user`. Combined with `status`, it documents the outcome of review and is important for audit and compliance.

The value is maintained exclusively through moderation workflows and is immutable from client-side read operations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was created.

This is taken from `discussion_board_reports.created_at` and reflects the point in time when the reporter submitted the report. It is used for moderation queue ordering, SLA tracking, and audit purposes.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was last updated.

Mapped from `discussion_board_reports.updated_at`, this timestamp changes whenever moderators adjust fields such as `status` or `action`. It allows clients to detect stale views and helps track the history of moderation activity at a coarse level.

discussion_board_comment_id.description:
Identifier of the comment that this report targets.

This value originates from `discussion_board_report_of_comments.discussion_board_comment_id` and points to the primary key of the reported comment in `discussion_board_comments`. It is intentionally kept as a raw foreign key in this DTO so that the parent report does not embed the full comment object and avoids circular structures.

Clients that need the comment content or additional metadata must call the dedicated comment retrieval endpoints using this id, keeping this report-focused DTO lightweight while still providing a precise navigation key.

comment_link_created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report-to-comment association was created.

This maps to `discussion_board_report_of_comments.created_at`. It records when the system persisted the link between the report and the comment, which may be useful for debugging or audit scenarios where the association time differs from the original report creation time.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IInve.description:
Inverted composition DTO centered on a single attachment-targeting report.

This type is optimized for moderation views that start from a report identifier and need, in one response, both the link between the report and the attachment and a compact view of the underlying report and attachment metadata.

It composes the `discussion_board_report_of_attachments` link row together with a summary of the base report from `discussion_board_reports` and the attachment metadata from `discussion_board_attachments`. To avoid circular references and heavy payloads, it excludes any collections or nested lists; consumers retrieve related articles or further attachment usage via separate endpoints if needed.

id.description:
Primary key of the attachment-report link.

This is the unique identifier from `discussion_board_report_of_attachments.id`, representing the specific association between a single report record and a single attachment. Multiple link rows may point to different reports for the same attachment, but each association has its own id.

discussion_board_report_id.description:
Identifier of the report that targets an attachment.

Backed by `discussion_board_report_of_attachments.discussion_board_report_id`, this field joins the link entity to the central `discussion_board_reports` row. It is usually identical to the `reportId` path parameter used when calling the detail endpoint that returns this DTO.

discussion_board_attachment_id.description:
Identifier of the attachment that has been reported.

This value comes from `discussion_board_report_of_attachments.discussion_board_attachment_id` and points to the primary key of the file in `discussion_board_attachments`. It allows clients to fetch additional attachment or article details when necessary.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this report-to-attachment association was created.

Mapped from `discussion_board_report_of_attachments.created_at`, this time is recorded when the system first linked the report to the attachment. It is useful for auditing the sequence of moderation events and for debugging linkage timing.

report.description:
Compact view of the base report associated with this attachment link.

This object summarizes key fields from the underlying `discussion_board_reports` row, such as reason code, workflow status, action, and timestamps. It intentionally omits any collections or reverse relations to avoid circular structures while still giving moderators the information needed to understand why the attachment was reported.

attachment.description:
Compact metadata for the attachment that was reported.

This object summarizes key fields from `discussion_board_attachments`, including file name, URI, content type, size, ordering within the parent article, and moderation status. It is designed to give moderators enough context to decide whether to keep, hide, or delete the file without loading unrelated article or board-level aggregates.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IRepo.description:
Summary view of a discussion board report for use inside attachment-targeting report DTOs.

This type captures the most important moderation fields from `discussion_board_reports` when the report appears as a nested object within `IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IInvert`. It is intentionally lightweight and omits any child collections or polymorphic link details.

Consumers use this summary to understand who reported the attachment, why it was reported, and what the current moderation status and action are, without needing to issue a separate report-detail query in simple decision flows.

id.description:
Primary key of the report.

Copied from `discussion_board_reports.id`, this value uniquely identifies the report row associated with the reported attachment.

target_type.description:
Discriminator describing the type of content targeted by this report.

Taken from `discussion_board_reports.target_type`. For this invert usage, the logical expectation is that the value is `attachment`, but it is exposed so clients can verify the target type and guard against misuse.

reporter_type.description:
Discriminator describing which actor type submitted the report.

Backed by `discussion_board_reports.reporter_type`, such as `memberuser` or `adminuser`. This allows moderation tools to understand the origin of the report when reviewing it in attachment-specific contexts.

reason_code.description:
Machine-friendly code representing the primary reason category for this report.

Mapped from `discussion_board_reports.reason_code`. Typical values include `hate_abuse`, `harassment`, `spam`, `off_topic`, `dangerous_misleading`, and `other`. The exact allowed set is governed by business rules.

description.description:
Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter.

This corresponds to the nullable `discussion_board_reports.description` column. It contains additional description that elaborates on the selected `reason_code`, or is null when no extended explanation was provided.

status.description:
Current workflow status of the report.

Backed by `discussion_board_reports.status`, representing states such as `submitted`, `in_review`, or `resolved`. Moderation tools rely on this field to drive queues and identify which reports still need action.

action.description:
Administrative decision applied in response to this report.

Mapped from `discussion_board_reports.action`. Example values include `none`, `keep`, `hide_content`, `delete_content`, and `restrict_user`. Together with `status`, this field documents the outcome of moderation over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was created.

This is taken from `discussion_board_reports.created_at` and indicates when the report was originally submitted by the reporter.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the report was last updated.

Taken from `discussion_board_reports.updated_at`, this field updates whenever moderators change the report's status, action, or other mutable fields, and is useful for tracking the freshness of moderation decisions.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfAttachment.IAtta.description:
Summary view of a discussion board attachment for use inside attachment-targeting report DTOs.

This type reflects key metadata from the `discussion_board_attachments` table needed for moderation, including file URI, name, content type, size, ordering within the article, moderation status, and relevant timestamps. It intentionally omits heavy article or board-level relational data to keep the nested structure small and focused.

Moderators use this summary to quickly understand what file was reported and how it is currently treated by the system, while any deeper article or author context is loaded via separate dedicated endpoints if required.

id.description:
Primary key of the attachment record.

This value comes from `discussion_board_attachments.id` and uniquely identifies the stored attachment within the board.

discussion_board_article_id.description:
Identifier of the parent article to which this attachment belongs.

This field is mapped from `discussion_board_attachments.discussion_board_article_id`. It allows clients or internal tools to navigate to the article that owns this attachment when additional context is needed.

file_uri.description:
URI location of the stored file object.

Backed by `discussion_board_attachments.file_uri`, this value points to the storage location used by the application to retrieve or stream the attachment. It is a URL-style string managed by the file storage subsystem.

file_name.description:
User-visible file name of the attachment.

Taken from `discussion_board_attachments.file_name`, this string typically represents the original client file name adjusted for safety and consistency. It is displayed in UIs when listing or previewing attachments.

content_type.description:
MIME-like content type for the attachment.

This field maps to `discussion_board_attachments.content_type` and indicates how the file should be interpreted or previewed, such as `image/jpeg` or `application/pdf`.

file_size.description:
Size of the attachment file in bytes.

Backed by `discussion_board_attachments.file_size`, this integer is used to enforce per-file and per-article size limits and for presenting approximate size to users in moderation tools or article views.

order_in_article.description:
Display order of this attachment within its parent article.

Mapped from `discussion_board_attachments.order_in_article`, this integer determines the ordering of attachments when rendered. Lower values appear earlier in UI lists. The pair `(discussion_board_article_id, order_in_article)` is unique at the database level.

status.description:
Moderation and lifecycle status of the attachment.

This string reflects `discussion_board_attachments.status` and typically carries values such as `active`, `hidden`, or `deleted`, aligned with the board's overall content visibility rules. Moderation operations change this field when hiding or removing attachments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the attachment record was created.

Taken from `discussion_board_attachments.created_at`, this marks when the file was first associated with its article.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the attachment record was last updated.

Mapped from `discussion_board_attachments.updated_at`, this value changes when metadata or status fields are modified.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp of the attachment.

This field corresponds to the nullable `discussion_board_attachments.deleted_at` column. When null, the attachment is not soft-deleted and may be visible depending on its `status`. When set, it indicates the time at which the attachment was logically deleted for business purposes even if its metadata remains stored for audit or recovery.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a discussion board report used in listing and cross-reference contexts.

This summary focuses on the core workflow fields of a report such as target and reporter types, high-level reason category, current status, action decision, and key timestamps, without exposing any link-table level details.

It is typically returned in paginated admin queues, member "my reports" views, or contextual embeddings when only headline information about the report is required rather than full relation expansion.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the report.

This maps directly to `discussion_board_reports.id` and is used to reference the report in detail views and moderation actions.

target_type.description:
Type of content that this report targets.

Values are constrained at the application layer and typically include codes such as `article`, `comment`, or `attachment`. Clients should treat this as an opaque discriminator string used only for display and routing, not for business logic branching.

reporter_type.description:
Actor type that submitted the report.

Common values are `memberuser` for regular discussion participants and `adminuser` when an administrator files a report in a user-like role. This allows moderation tooling to differentiate the origin of reports for prioritization or filtering.

reason_code.description:
Machine-oriented primary reason code associated with this report.

The code groups reports into categories such as hate or abuse, harassment, spam, off topic, dangerous or misleading content, or other. The exact vocabulary is enforced by server-side validation and may be localized for display on the client side.

status.description:
Current workflow status of this report.

Typical lifecycle values include `submitted` for newly filed reports, `in_review` while moderators are handling the case, and `resolved` once a final decision has been made. Status is used heavily for filtering queues and computing moderation metrics.

action.description:
Administrative action chosen as the resolution for this report.

Representative values include `none` when no change is warranted, `keep` when content is explicitly allowed, `hide_content` or `delete_content` when the target is removed from public view, and `restrict_user` when the owning member account receives a restriction. Valid combinations with `status` are constrained by business rules.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this report was first created by the reporting actor.

This value is taken from `discussion_board_reports.created_at` and is used for chronological ordering, SLA calculations, and audit trails in moderation tools.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this report was last updated.

Updates typically occur when moderators change the `status`, apply an `action`, or add internal notes. This is sourced from `discussion_board_reports.updated_at` and allows clients to highlight recently handled items.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfAdminusers.description:
Entity-level DTO representing the association between a discussion board report and an admin user who submitted that report.

This schema is based on the subsidiary Prisma model `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`, which connects one row in `discussion_board_reports` to one row in `discussion_board_adminusers` and thereby records that an administrator, rather than a regular member, filed the report.

It is intended for use in admin-facing APIs that surface audit information about reports initiated by staff, without embedding reverse collections that could introduce circular references.

id.description:
Primary key of the admin reporter association row in `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers.id`.

This identifier uniquely distinguishes a specific link between a report and an admin user and is stable over the lifetime of the association.

Audit logs and internal tools can use this value when referencing or inspecting a particular reporter-link record.

discussion_board_report_id.description:
Foreign key referencing the reported item row in `discussion_board_reports.id`.

At the database level this column enforces a one-to-one relationship between a report and its admin reporter association by being marked as unique. Each report can have at most one corresponding row in `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers`.

In application code and diagnostics this value is useful for joining back to full report details, correlating with other report-centric tables, and troubleshooting mismatches between link records and their parent reports.

discussion_board_adminuser_id.description:
Foreign key referencing the administrator account that filed the report, mapped to `discussion_board_adminusers.id`.

This column records which admin user acted as the reporting actor when the row was created. Although most business flows will rely on the richer `adminUser` summary object, exposing the raw identifier is important for low-level analytics, exports, and debugging joins.

The value participates in many-to-one relationships where a single administrator may be associated with many reports in `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers` over time.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this report-to-adminUser association was created in the `discussion_board_report_of_adminusers` table.

The value typically reflects the moment when the admin submitted the report via moderation tools or internal workflows.

It is used for audit trails, chronology, and time-based reporting in administrative dashboards.

report.description:
Summary representation of the underlying report that this association links to.

Embedding this summary alongside the association fields allows admin tools to display key report attributes—such as target type, reason code, status, and action—without requiring a separate API call.

The summary is intentionally compact and free of reverse collections to avoid circular structures and oversized payloads.

adminUser.description:
Summary view of the admin user account from `discussion_board_adminusers` that filed the report.

This nested object exposes moderation-relevant information such as the admin's identifier, display name, and account status but omits sensitive authentication details.

Including it directly in the DTO enables internal moderation and audit interfaces to show who initiated a staff-originated report without querying additional endpoints.

IDiscussionBoardReportOfMemberUser.IInve.description:
Inverted view of the association between a discussion board report and the member user who submitted it.

This DTO is centered on the subsidiary Prisma model `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`, but it enriches the link with compact representations of both the underlying report and the reporting member user so that moderation tools can render all necessary context in a single response without additional API calls.

The schema is designed specifically for admin-facing report handling flows. It intentionally excludes any reverse collections (such as all reports for a member user) to avoid circular references and oversized payloads, while still exposing all identifiers and timestamps required for auditing and workflow transitions.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the link entity in `discussion_board_report_of_memberusers`.

This value represents the primary key of the association row that connects a single `discussion_board_reports` record to the member user reporter from `discussion_board_memberusers`.

Moderation tools and audit logs can rely on this identifier to reference the exact reporter-link instance, even if the underlying report or member user evolves over time.

discussion_board_report_id.description:
Identifier of the report in `discussion_board_reports` that this link row refers to.

This field matches `discussion_board_reports.id` and allows the system to correlate the reporter association with the main report entity.

It is unique per link table by design, reflecting the 1:1 relationship between a given report and its member user reporter in this association table.

discussion_board_memberuser_id.description:
Identifier of the member user account in `discussion_board_memberusers` that submitted the report.

This field corresponds to `discussion_board_memberusers.id` and enables joins to retrieve the reporting actor's profile and status.

Although the link table enforces a 1:1 relationship at the report level, a single member user may appear in many link rows across different reports.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this report-to-memberUser association row was created.

This is typically set at the moment the report is filed by the member user and may differ from the main report's timestamps if additional normalization or background processing is performed.

The value is primarily used for audit trails and time-based filtering in internal tools.

report.description:
Compact representation of the underlying report from `discussion_board_reports`.

This summary object exposes the key attributes of the report that are relevant for moderation decisions, such as target type, reporter type, reason code, status, action, and timestamps, without including any collections that could create circular references.

Including this summary allows admin UIs to render the essential report context directly alongside the reporter information returned by this endpoint.

memberUser.description:
Summary view of the member user from `discussion_board_memberusers` who filed the report.

The summary exposes only public and moderation-relevant fields, such as display name, account status, and basic profile flags, and deliberately excludes sensitive authentication details like email or password hash.

By embedding this summary, the API enables moderators to evaluate both the report and the reporter in one response while avoiding reverse collections that would lead to circular structures.

IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget.description:
Filter and grouping parameters for computing report statistics grouped by target type from the discussion_board_reports table.

This request DTO is used by administrative dashboards and moderation analytics to specify how report data should be filtered before aggregation. Typical filters include created-at time ranges, workflow statuses, actions taken on reports, and reason codes. All filters are optional; when omitted, the API should compute statistics over the entire report set.

The filters are applied to rows of the discussion_board_reports Prisma model before grouping by target_type. This allows admins to answer questions like “How many open article reports exist in the last 7 days?” or “How many resolved attachment reports with a particular reason_code do we have?”.

This DTO is read-only in nature and does not cause any modification of report records. It is strictly used to control the scope of aggregation queries for monitoring and analytics purposes.

createdAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the created_at timestamp filter for reports.

When provided, only reports whose created_at is greater than or equal to this value are considered in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit timezone offset.

If omitted, there is no lower time bound and all earlier reports are included.

createdAtTo.description:
Exclusive upper bound of the created_at timestamp filter for reports.

When provided, only reports whose created_at is strictly less than this value are considered in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit timezone offset.

If omitted, there is no upper time bound and all later reports are included.

statusList.description:
Optional list of report workflow statuses to include in the aggregation.

When provided, only reports whose status is one of the values in this list are counted. When omitted or an empty array, reports of all statuses are considered.

Typical values are domain-specific workflow states such as "submitted", "in_review", "resolved", or "rejected". The exact allowed values should match the status column in the discussion_board_reports model.

actionList.description:
Optional list of moderation actions to include in the aggregation.

When provided, only reports whose action (the final moderation action decided for the report) is one of the listed values are counted. When omitted or an empty array, reports with any action value are included.

Typical values might include action codes such as "none", "content_removed", "user_warned", or "user_suspended", depending on the business rules and how actions are stored in discussion_board_reports.

reasonCodeList.description:
Optional list of reason_code values used to filter reports before aggregation.

When provided, only reports whose reason_code is one of the entries in this list are included in the statistics. When omitted or an empty array, reports with any reason_code are considered.

Reason codes usually represent predefined categories like "spam", "hate_speech", "misinformation", or "off_topic" as stored in the discussion_board_reports model.

IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget.description:
Aggregated statistics per target_type derived from the discussion_board_reports table.

This response DTO is used by administrative dashboards and moderation tools to display high-level statistics about user reports grouped by the type of content they target. Each bucket in the statistics array represents a single target_type (for example, "article", "comment", or "attachment") and exposes one or more numeric metrics for that content type.

The statistics are computed by running aggregation queries over the discussion_board_reports Prisma model after applying the filters from IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget.IRequest. Typical metrics include the total number of reports, the number of open (unresolved) reports, and the number of resolved reports per target_type. Additional metrics can be added in future evolutions as long as they remain consistent with this schema.

The DTO is read-only and reflects the current state of the moderation pipeline. It does not contain individual report details; instead, it provides the aggregate numbers that help admins understand where moderation attention is most needed.

buckets.description:
Array of aggregated statistics buckets, one per target_type.

Each bucket describes a single report target type (for example, "article", "comment", or "attachment") and the corresponding aggregation metrics such as total report counts and distribution by resolution status.

When there are no reports matching the specified filters, this array will be empty.

IDiscussionBoardReportStatisticsByTarget.description:
Single aggregation bucket for a specific report target_type.

Each instance of this DTO represents aggregated statistics for one target type in the discussion_board_reports table. The targetType property identifies what kind of content is being reported (for example, "article", "comment", or "attachment"). The numeric properties expose various counts derived from the filtered set of reports.

These metrics are typically used to populate charts or tables in administrative dashboards, enabling moderators to quickly see which content types are receiving the most reports and how many of those reports remain unresolved.

targetType.description:
Type of content targeted by the reports in this bucket.

Typical values include logical report target categories such as "article", "comment", or "attachment". The exact values must match how the target_type column is stored in the discussion_board_reports Prisma model.

All reports included in this bucket share the same target_type value.

totalReportCount.description:
Total number of reports for this targetType after applying all request filters.

This is the primary metric showing how many reports exist for the given target type in the selected time window and with the specified statuses, actions, and reason codes. It includes both open and resolved reports.

openReportCount.description:
Number of reports for this targetType that are considered open or unresolved.

This count is derived from the subset of reports whose status is not in a resolved terminal state. The exact mapping between status values and the notion of "open" is defined by business rules (for example, statuses like "submitted" or "in_review").

resolvedReportCount.description:
Number of reports for this targetType that are considered resolved.

This count is derived from the subset of reports whose status represents a final resolution state (for example, "resolved" or "rejected" according to the workflow). It complements openReportCount and can be used to compute resolution ratios for each target type.

IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics.description:
Filter and search criteria for computing aggregated report statistics grouped by reason_code from the discussion_board_reports table.

This DTO allows administrative clients to specify which report rows should be included in the aggregation before grouping by reason_code. It supports time range filters on created_at and updated_at, filtering by target_type and reporter_type, restricting to specific reason_code values, and narrowing by workflow status and moderation action. The filters are interpreted as logical constraints over the underlying discussion_board_reports records (and, when necessary, their subsidiary link tables) but do not directly expose any actor IDs or internal implementation details.

The backend uses this request body in a PATCH operation because the filter structure is complex and not suitable for simple query parameters. The endpoint is read-only and does not modify any stored data; it only computes analytical aggregations based on the specified conditions.

created_at_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the created_at timestamp range used to filter discussion_board_reports rows.

When provided, only reports whose created_at value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit time zone offset. If null, no lower bound filter on created_at is applied.

created_at_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the created_at timestamp range used to filter discussion_board_reports rows.

When provided, only reports whose created_at value is less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC or with an explicit time zone offset. If null, no upper bound filter on created_at is applied.

updated_at_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the updated_at timestamp range used to filter discussion_board_reports rows.

When provided, only reports whose updated_at value is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. If null, no lower bound filter on updated_at is applied.

updated_at_to.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the updated_at timestamp range used to filter discussion_board_reports rows.

When provided, only reports whose updated_at value is less than or equal to this timestamp are included in the aggregation. The value must be an ISO 8601 date-time string. If null, no upper bound filter on updated_at is applied.

items.description:
Target content type that was reported.

Typical values are implementation-defined strings such as "article", "comment", or "attachment", corresponding to the target_type column in discussion_board_reports. When this list is non-empty, only reports whose target_type is contained in this list are considered during aggregation.

target_types.description:
Optional list of target_type values used to filter discussion_board_reports rows before aggregation.

If omitted or empty, reports of all target types are included. When present, only rows whose target_type matches one of the provided values are considered.

items.description:
Reporter type indicating which kind of user created the report.

Typical values are implementation-defined strings such as "memberUser" or "adminUser", corresponding to the reporter_type column of discussion_board_reports. When this list is non-empty, only rows whose reporter_type is in this list are considered.

reporter_types.description:
Optional list of reporter_type values used to filter which reporters' submissions are included in the aggregation.

If omitted or empty, reports made by any supported reporter type are included. When provided, only reports whose reporter_type matches one of the listed values are included.

items.description:
Reason code representing the high-level category assigned to the report.

The actual set of valid codes is defined by business rules and typically includes values such as "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", or "other". This field is matched against the reason_code column in discussion_board_reports.

reason_codes.description:
Optional subset of reason_code values to include in the aggregation.

When provided, only discussion_board_reports rows whose reason_code matches one of the given values are eligible for grouping and counting. If omitted or empty, all reason_code values present in the filtered dataset are included in the aggregation.

items.description:
Workflow status value of a moderation report.

Typical values include implementation-defined codes such as "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved" that indicate the current handling state of the report in the moderation workflow.

statuses.description:
Optional list of status values used to filter report rows before aggregation.

When this array is non-empty, only reports whose status is in the list are included. If omitted or empty, reports with any status are considered.

items.description:
Moderation action taken as a result of the report.

Typical values include implementation-defined codes such as "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", or "restrict_user", representing the final moderator decision recorded in the discussion_board_reports table.

actions.description:
Optional list of moderation action values used to filter the dataset before grouping by reason_code.

If provided, only report rows whose action is one of the specified values are included. If omitted or empty, reports with any action value are considered.

IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics.description:
Aggregated moderation report statistics grouped by reason_code based on data stored in the discussion_board_reports table.

This DTO represents analytical results rather than raw database rows.
