Each statistics row corresponds to a single reason_code value and contains aggregate metrics such as the total number of reports using that reason, and optionally additional counts derived from the underlying discussion_board_reports records (for example, counts by status or action). The structure is designed for use in moderation dashboards and reporting UIs, where administrators need an at-a-glance overview of how frequently each report reason is used over a selected time range and with specific filtering criteria.

The data returned by this type is read-only and does not map directly to a single Prisma model. It is computed by grouping discussion_board_reports rows after applying filters such as created_at/updated_at ranges, target_type, reporter_type, status, and action. Because the size and shape of the analytical dataset can vary depending on the filters, the DTO uses an array of statistics row objects rather than a flat structure.

items.description:
Collection of aggregated statistics rows, one for each distinct reason_code that appears in the filtered discussion_board_reports dataset.

Each row summarizes how many reports used that reason and may include additional breakdown metrics such as counts by status or action.

IDiscussionBoardReportByReasonStatistics.description:
Single aggregated statistics row for a specific reason_code in the discussion_board_reports table.

Each instance of this type corresponds to one distinct reason_code value after filtering and grouping. It contains the reason_code identifier and aggregate metrics such as the total number of reports with that reason, and optionally more detailed counts derived from the status and action columns. These rows are primarily intended for visualization in moderation dashboards, tables, or charts summarizing report activity by reason.

reason_code.description:
Reason code for this statistics row.

The value corresponds to the reason_code column in discussion_board_reports (for example, "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", or "other"). All aggregated metrics in this row pertain to reports that share this reason_code.

total_count.description:
Total number of discussion_board_reports rows that match the request filters and have this reason_code.

This count represents the primary measure used in by-reason analytics and can be used to rank or visualize the prevalence of different report reasons over the selected time range and filter set.

submitted_count.description:
Number of reports with this reason_code whose status is currently in the initial or active workflow state (for example, "submitted" or other project-specific pending statuses).

This metric helps administrators understand how many reports with this reason have not yet been fully processed. If the underlying implementation does not distinguish submitted states, this value may be equal to zero or may mirror total_count.

in_review_count.description:
Number of reports with this reason_code that are currently in an intermediate review state (for example, "in_review" or equivalent project-specific states).

This field is optional in terms of business semantics; if the system does not explicitly model an "in review" state, it may be set to zero or omitted in future schema revisions.

resolved_count.description:
Number of reports with this reason_code that have reached a resolved status (for example, "resolved" or other terminal states indicating that moderation handling is complete).

This metric is useful for understanding how many reports of a given reason have been fully processed over the filtered time period.

action_none_count.description: Number of reports with this reason_code where the recorded moderation action is equivalent to taking no change (for example, "none"), indicating that the content or user remained unchanged after review.

action_keep_count.description: Number of reports with this reason_code where the recorded moderation action kept the content visible without significant restriction (for example, an action value such as "keep").

action_hide_content_count.description: Number of reports with this reason_code for which the moderation action hid or obscured the related content from normal user views (for example, an action value such as "hide_content").

action_delete_content_count.description: Number of reports with this reason_code where the decision was to delete the related content permanently or remove it from public access (for example, an action value such as "delete_content").

action_restrict_user_count.description: Number of reports with this reason_code that resulted in some form of restriction on the reporting target user (for example, an action value such as "restrict_user"), such as temporary suspension or other sanctions.

IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics.description:
Filter and search criteria for computing aggregated statistics of discussion_board_reports grouped by status.

This request DTO allows admin users to constrain which report rows are included in the aggregation by specifying optional filters such as created/updated time ranges, target type, reporter type, reason code, action, and status. All filters are optional and are combined using logical AND semantics: only reports matching all provided criteria are included before grouping by status.

No authentication or actor identity fields are present here; access control is enforced at the operation level using the adminUser authentication context.

createdAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the report creation timestamp window.

When provided, only reports with created_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered in the aggregation. If omitted, there is no lower bound on created_at.

createdAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the report creation timestamp window.

When provided, only reports with created_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered in the aggregation. If omitted, there is no upper bound on created_at.

updatedAtFrom.description:
Inclusive lower bound of the report update timestamp window.

When provided, only reports with updated_at greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered in the aggregation. If omitted, there is no lower bound on updated_at.

updatedAtTo.description:
Inclusive upper bound of the report update timestamp window.

When provided, only reports with updated_at less than or equal to this ISO 8601 timestamp are considered in the aggregation. If omitted, there is no upper bound on updated_at.

targetTypes.description:
Optional list of target types to include in the aggregation.

Each value corresponds to the target_type column in discussion_board_reports and typically represents which kind of content is being reported, such as "article", "comment", or "attachment". When provided, only reports whose target_type is in this list are considered.

reporterTypes.description:
Optional list of reporter types to include in the aggregation.

Each value corresponds to the reporter_type column in discussion_board_reports and typically distinguishes whether the reporter is a member user or an admin user, using values such as "memberuser" or "adminuser". When provided, only reports whose reporter_type is in this list are considered.

reasonCodes.description:
Optional list of reason codes to include in the aggregation.

Values correspond to the reason_code column in discussion_board_reports, representing why the content was reported. Typical examples include "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam", "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", and "other". When provided, only reports whose reason_code is in this list are considered.

actions.description:
Optional list of moderation actions to filter by.

Values correspond to the action column in discussion_board_reports and represent decisions taken on the report, such as "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", or "restrict_user". When provided, only reports with an action in this list are considered.

statuses.description:
Optional list of report workflow statuses to constrain the aggregation domain.

Values correspond to the status column in discussion_board_reports, such as "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved". When provided, only reports whose status is in this list participate in the aggregation. Note that the aggregation itself will still group by status within this filtered subset.

IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics.description:
Aggregated moderation report statistics grouped by status for the discussion board.

This analytical DTO represents the result of grouping filtered discussion_board_reports rows by their status column and computing per-status metrics such as the total number of reports and, optionally, derived ratios. It is designed for internal dashboards and monitoring tools used by admin users to understand the current and historical workload of the moderation pipeline.

The DTO does not expose raw report records or sensitive reporter information. Instead, it returns a collection of status-level buckets that summarize how many reports are currently in each workflow stage such as "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved".

items.description:
Collection of per-status statistics entries.

Each element summarizes all discussion_board_reports rows that share the same status value within the filtered domain, providing at minimum the status identifier and total count, and optionally additional derived metrics useful for dashboards.

IDiscussionBoardReportByStatusStatistics.description:
Single per-status statistics row derived from the discussion_board_reports table.

Each instance corresponds to one distinct status value among the filtered reports (for example, "submitted", "in_review", or "resolved"). It contains the status identifier and the total number of matching reports, and may include additional derived metrics such as proportions to support visualization and SLA tracking in moderation dashboards.

status.description:
Workflow status value for this bucket, corresponding to the status column in discussion_board_reports.

Typical values include "submitted", "in_review", and "resolved". The exact domain is controlled by the database enum or validation logic in the reports model.

count.description: Total number of discussion_board_reports rows that match this status within the filtered domain.

ratio.description:
Optional ratio of this status bucket relative to the total number of filtered reports.

This value is typically a floating point number between 0 and 1 indicating what fraction of all matched reports are currently in this status. It is provided for convenience in dashboards; if not computed by the backend, the field may be omitted.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserNotificationPr.description:
Notification preference settings for a single registered discussion board member user.

This object represents one row in the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` table, which stores boolean flags indicating what categories of notifications the system is allowed to send to a particular member. It is in a strict 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_memberusers` through the unique, non-null `discussion_board_memberuser_id` foreign key.

Service logic reads and writes this object when a logged-in member inspects or updates their own notification settings. Administrative overrides, if any, are handled through separate admin-focused APIs and are not modeled by this type.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user notification preference record.

This is the primary key of the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` table and is generated by the database or persistence layer. It uniquely identifies a single preference row among all member accounts and is used internally for joins and debugging.

Client applications receive this value in read responses but must never try to guess or fabricate it; they should treat it as an opaque identifier.

discussion_board_memberuser_id.description:
Identifier of the member user who owns these notification preferences.

This value corresponds to `discussion_board_memberusers.id` and enforces the 1:1 relationship between a member account and its preference record. The Prisma schema defines this foreign key as non-null and unique, ensuring that each member can have at most one row in the preferences table.

In member-facing APIs, this field is populated from the authenticated session context and is not supplied by clients.

activity_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether activity notifications for the member’s own content are enabled.

When this value is `true`, the system is allowed to send notifications about activity related to the member’s own articles or comments, such as replies or mentions. When `false`, non-essential notifications of this category should be suppressed according to business rules.

This flag does not affect mandatory service messages that must always be delivered for legal or operational reasons.

digest_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether digest or summary-style notifications are enabled.

When this value is `true`, the system may send periodic digests that summarize recent activity of interest to the member, such as trending discussions or updates in followed categories. When `false`, such periodic digests should not be sent.

The exact cadence and composition of digests are defined in higher-level business rules and are not controlled directly by this schema.

marketing_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether optional marketing or non-essential announcement notifications are enabled.

When this value is `true`, the member consents to receive promotional messages, feature announcements, or other non-essential communications related to the discussion board. When `false`, the system should suppress these messages and only send notifications that remain mandatory under the service’s terms.

This flag allows separation of core service notifications from marketing-style content for compliance and user experience purposes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was first created.

The value is stored as a precise date-time in the database and reflects the moment the preference row was inserted, either when a member first saves settings or when defaults are created automatically. It is managed exclusively by the backend and is never set by clients.

Consumers can use this timestamp for auditing, debugging, or displaying when the member’s preference profile originated.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was last updated.

Each time any of the preference flags change, the backend updates this field to the current server time. This allows clients and administrators to understand how recent the stored notification settings are and to resolve conflicts if multiple devices try to update preferences.

Like `created_at`, this value is read-only from the client’s perspective and is always set by the backend implementation.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserNotificationPr.description:
Request body for updating or creating notification preferences for the currently authenticated member user.

This DTO carries the desired boolean values for the three notification preference flags stored in the `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences` table: activity notifications, digest notifications, and marketing notifications. The backend uses the authenticated member’s identity from the session context to select or create the corresponding row; the client never specifies a user identifier.

All flags are required and must be provided explicitly as `true` or `false` to ensure clear, idempotent semantics for PUT-style updates. The server validates the payload against the Prisma schema, updates or inserts the row, and refreshes the `updated_at` timestamp accordingly.

activity_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether activity notifications on the member’s own content are enabled.

Clients must provide this flag explicitly as `true` or `false` when updating notification preferences. A value of `true` allows the system to send notifications about replies, mentions, or other interactions on the member’s articles and comments, subject to overall notification policy.

If this flag is omitted or sent with an invalid type, the backend should treat the request as invalid and return a validation error.

digest_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether digest or summary-style notifications are enabled.

This flag controls whether the member is eligible to receive periodic digest messages that aggregate recent relevant activity. Setting it to `true` enables such digests; setting it to `false` disables them.

Like the other preference flags, this property is required in the update payload so that the resulting row state is fully determined by a single request.

marketing_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether optional marketing and non-essential announcement notifications are enabled.

When this property is `true`, the backend may send promotional content or announcements in line with the service’s marketing policies. When it is `false`, the member opts out of such non-essential notifications while still receiving any mandatory service messages dictated by policy or regulation.

This field is required in the update request to keep the preference record consistent and avoid partially specified updates.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPre.description:
Notification preference settings for a single admin user account.

This DTO represents one row of the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` table, which is in a strict 1:1 relationship with `discussion_board_adminusers` through the unique foreign key `discussion_board_adminuser_id`. It exposes the non-sensitive preference flags and metadata timestamps needed by administrative frontends to render and manage the admin’s notification configuration.

The fields in this schema map directly to the underlying Prisma model columns, excluding internal authentication or security-related fields. It is used as the response body for reading and updating the authenticated admin user’s notification preferences, always resolved from the current admin user context rather than client-supplied identifiers.

id.description:
Primary key of the admin user notification preferences record.

This value uniquely identifies the notification preference row in `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` and is generated by the database. It is used internally for updates and joins, and clients typically treat it as an opaque identifier.

The type is a UUID string and is read-only from the API consumer’s perspective.

activity_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether the admin user wishes to receive notifications about activity on content they authored.

When this value is `true`, the system is allowed to send notifications such as replies to the admin’s articles or comments, or other activity closely related to their authored content.

When `false`, these activity-related notifications should be suppressed where allowed by business rules, reducing noise for operational accounts.

digest_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether the admin user wishes to receive periodic digest or summary notifications.

Typical digest notifications aggregate recent activity or moderation-relevant events into scheduled messages (for example, daily or weekly summaries). A value of `true` means the admin opts in to such digests.

When set to `false`, the system should not send non-essential digest summaries, although mandatory operational alerts may still be delivered according to separate rules.

marketing_notifications_enabled.description:
Flag indicating whether the admin user allows optional marketing-style or non-essential announcement notifications.

This setting controls communications such as product announcements, feature highlights, or other non-critical messages that are not strictly required for operating the discussion board.

A value of `false` indicates that the admin prefers not to receive these optional messages, while required policy or service communications may still be sent regardless of this flag.

created_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was first created.

The value is stored in the database as a datetime column and typically reflects the moment when the admin’s notification preferences were initially persisted.

It is managed exclusively by the persistence layer and is always read-only for API consumers.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was last updated.

Each successful modification of any notification preference flags should update this timestamp to reflect the most recent change time.

Like `created_at`, this field is managed by the persistence layer and cannot be directly edited by clients.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuserNotificationPre.description:
Update DTO for the notification preference configuration of the authenticated admin user.

This type is used as the request body for the PUT `/discussionBoard/adminUser/notifications/adminUser/preferences` operation. It allows the client to modify the boolean preference flags stored in the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` table for the currently authenticated admin user.

Ownership and identity fields such as `discussion_board_adminuser_id`, as well as system-managed fields like `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`, are excluded from the updatable surface and are resolved or maintained exclusively by the backend using the authenticated admin user context and persistence rules.

activity_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether the admin user should receive notifications about activity on content they authored.

When provided, this flag replaces the existing `activity_notifications_enabled` value in the underlying preference record. A value of `true` enables activity notifications, while `false` disables them as far as business rules allow.

If omitted from the request body, the current stored value remains unchanged.

digest_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether the admin user should receive periodic digest or summary notifications.

Supplying this field updates the `digest_notifications_enabled` column in the `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences` row, controlling whether aggregated digests of recent activity or moderation events are sent.

If this property is not included in the payload, the existing digest preference is preserved.

marketing_notifications_enabled.description:
New value for whether the admin user allows optional marketing-style or non-essential announcement notifications.

Providing this field in the request updates the `marketing_notifications_enabled` preference flag. A `true` value opts the admin into optional marketing or announcement messages, while `false` opts them out.

If the property is omitted, the stored marketing preference is left unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of a discussion board article backed by the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model.

This DTO is optimized for list views and for embedding article context inside other entities without loading the full article body or related collections. It focuses on identification, minimal presentation fields, and key engagement metrics while omitting heavy text content and internal moderation state.

Several properties, such as like and comment counts, are exposed as aggregated values that are typically computed from other tables (for example, `discussion_board_article_likes` and `discussion_board_comments`) or from a materialized statistics view rather than stored directly on the `discussion_board_articles` row.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the discussion board article.

This value maps directly to `discussion_board_articles.id`, the primary key of the article row in the database, and is used as the canonical reference in all article-related operations, joins, and URL path parameters.

title.description:
Short title of the article as displayed in lists and headers.

The value corresponds to the `title` column on the `discussion_board_articles` table and serves as the primary human-readable label in article listing pages, search result rows, and cross-link displays. Business rules such as length limits and required-ness are enforced at the application and database layers rather than in this summary DTO.

oneOf.description:
Short excerpt or preview text of the article content suitable for list display.

In typical implementations this preview is derived from either the optional `summary` column or from the leading part of the `body` column on `discussion_board_articles`, trimmed and sanitized to fit compact UI components.

Indicates that no explicit excerpt or preview text is available for this article.

When this value is null, client applications may choose to derive a preview from `discussion_board_articles.body` on demand or to render only the title and metadata without additional text.

excerpt.description:
Short excerpt or preview text of the article content suitable for list display.

This property is a derived projection rather than a dedicated persisted column; it typically combines or truncates information from `discussion_board_articles.summary` or `discussion_board_articles.body` to allow lightweight rendering in cards, feeds, and search results without transferring the entire article body.

category.description:
Category to which this article belongs, represented as a lightweight summary object.

Relationally, the article row uses the foreign key column `discussion_board_articles.discussion_board_article_category_id`, which references `discussion_board_article_categories.id`. Instead of exposing the raw identifier in this summary DTO, the API returns an `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.ISummary` projection so that clients can immediately display category code and name alongside the article title without an extra lookup.

author.description:
Summary information of the user who authored this article, expressed as a polymorphic association.

From a data-model perspective, authorship is modeled via subtype/link tables (for example, `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers`) that connect `discussion_board_articles.id` either to `discussion_board_memberusers.id` or to `discussion_board_adminusers.id`. The API resolves the concrete author using those associations and then projects the result into either `IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.ISummary` or `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.ISummary`, exposing only non-sensitive public profile information suitable for display in lists.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the article was created, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

This value is mapped from the `discussion_board_articles.created_at` column and is primarily used for sorting article summaries (for example, newest-first feeds) and for displaying published time metadata in UI components and audit views.

likeCount.description:
Total number of likes that this article has received, represented as a non-negative integer.

This property is not a direct column of `discussion_board_articles`. Instead, it is typically computed from rows in `discussion_board_article_likes` or from a dedicated statistics projection that aggregates per-article like engagement. Exposing it here allows list and summary views to render engagement information without issuing separate count queries.

commentCount.description:
Total number of comments that have been posted on this article, represented as a non-negative integer.

Similar to `likeCount`, this property is an aggregated metric computed from the `discussion_board_comments` table, usually by counting rows where `discussion_board_comments.discussion_board_article_id` equals this article's `id`, or by reading from a precomputed materialized view. Including the count in the summary enables clients to show comment badges and activity indicators in article listings without loading the full comment collection.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a single discussion board comment backed by the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model.

This DTO is designed for compact list contexts and for embedding comment information inside other entities (for example, recent activity panels or condensed thread previews). It deliberately omits internal moderation fields, ownership sub-entities, and the full comment body, focusing instead on identification, a short preview, and minimal article and author context.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the comment.

This value maps directly to `discussion_board_comments.id`, the primary key for comment rows, and is used across the API surface as the canonical reference when fetching, updating, or moderating individual comments.

content_preview.description:
Short preview text of the comment content suitable for list displays.

Rather than exposing the full `discussion_board_comments.body` column, which may be long or contain formatting, this property provides a truncated or otherwise condensed representation derived from that body text. It is optimized for use in feeds, notifications, and sidebars where space is limited and only a quick glimpse of the comment is required.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when the comment was created, expressed as an ISO 8601 date-time string.

The value is derived from the `discussion_board_comments.created_at` column and is used for chronological sorting of comments as well as for displaying relative or absolute creation times in list and notification views.

article.description:
Summary information of the article that this comment belongs to.

At the relational layer, the association is represented by the `discussion_board_comments.discussion_board_article_id` foreign key that references `discussion_board_articles.id`. For this summary DTO, the API resolves that relationship and inlines an `IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary` projection so that consumers can render the surrounding article context (such as title and category) without issuing an additional fetch.

author.description:
Summary information of the user who authored this comment, expressed as a polymorphic association.

The underlying data model uses the `author_type` discriminator column on `discussion_board_comments` together with ownership subtype tables such as `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` to link each comment either to a `discussion_board_memberusers` row or to a `discussion_board_adminusers` row. The API follows those links to determine the concrete author and then projects it into the corresponding summary DTO (`IDiscussionBoardMemberUser.ISummary` or `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.ISummary`), exposing only public profile fields that are safe for inclusion in list and activity views.

IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a file attachment associated with a discussion board article.

Optimized for displaying attachment lists and basic metadata without loading full article or comment structures.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the attachment.

This value corresponds to the primary key of the discussion_board_attachments table.

name.description:
Human-readable file name shown to users when listing or downloading attachments.

This is typically derived from the original upload file name but may be normalized for display.

extension.description:
File extension of the attachment without the leading dot.

Examples: "pdf", "jpg", "png", "docx".

size_bytes.description:
Size of the attachment file in bytes.

Used for displaying file size indicators and enforcing download limits.

url.description:
Public or signed URL that can be used by clients to download or display the attachment content.

This value points to the file stored in an external storage system such as S3 or a CDN.

status.description:
Moderation and lifecycle status of the attachment in the discussion board.

This field is mapped directly from the non-nullable `status` column of the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model and typically holds values such as `active`, `hidden`, or `deleted`, depending on the board's content and moderation rules.

Client applications and moderation tools can use this value to decide whether an attachment should be shown, visually de-emphasized, or treated as removed while still retaining the underlying metadata row for audit and history purposes.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISumma.description:
Lightweight summary view of a discussion board member user session.

Used in admin or support tooling when listing or inspecting sessions for a specific member user without exposing full internal details or sensitive tokens. Intended for read-only scenarios such as audit logs, security reviews, or account activity history.

id.description: Unique identifier of the member user session record. This is the primary key of the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this member user session was created. Represents the login time or the moment the session became active.

last_active_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent activity associated with this session.

Used for detecting inactive or stale sessions and for displaying activity history. When null, the session has not recorded any activity after creation.

ip.description:
IP address from which this session was established.

Stored primarily for security auditing, fraud detection, and troubleshooting suspicious activity. May contain either IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation.

href.description:
Full URL (href) of the page where this session was initiated.

Typically captured from the client at login time for audit and security monitoring. May be used to reconstruct user flows during incident response.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that indicates from which page the user navigated when starting this session.

Useful for understanding login entry points and referrer patterns in security or analytics contexts.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp at which this session was considered expired or explicitly terminated.

This property maps directly to the nullable `expired_at` column of the `discussion_board_memberuser_sessions` Prisma model. When null, the session has not recorded a definitive expiration event and may still be treated as active or implicitly expired according to server-side rules.

Administrators and support tools can combine `expired_at` with `created_at`, `last_active_at`, and `is_active` to reconstruct the full lifecycle of a session and to investigate security or access issues.

is_active.description:
Indicates whether this session is currently considered active.

Typically derived from validity period, logout events, or revocation actions. When false, the session should no longer be used for authentication.

memberUser.description:
Summary information about the member user who owns this session.

Provides lightweight identity context (such as display name and account status) for administrative and audit tools without exposing raw foreign key IDs or full member account details.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuserSession.ISummar.description:
Lightweight summary view of a discussion board admin user session.

This DTO is used for security monitoring dashboards, administrative audit logs, and support tooling when reviewing administrative access history. It exposes persisted session context from the `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` Prisma model together with a lightweight view of the owning administrator so that audit UIs can render meaningful information without additional lookups.

Because it still maps one-to-one to the session table for core fields, all scalar properties correspond directly to real columns in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`, while the `adminUser` relation is a standard association projection to the `discussion_board_adminusers` model.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin user session record.

This is the primary key of the `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` table and serves as the stable handle for referencing this session from administrative audit endpoints and internal logs.

discussion_board_adminuser_id.description:
Identifier of the administrator account that owns this session.

This value comes directly from the `discussion_board_adminuser_id` foreign key column in the `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` Prisma model and corresponds to `discussion_board_adminusers.id`. It is useful for joins, cross-references, and internal tooling that operate primarily on raw identifiers rather than embedded summary objects.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this admin user session was created.

Represents the login time or the moment the session became active. This value comes directly from the `created_at` column of the `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` model and is managed exclusively by the backend.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when this admin user session was considered expired or terminated.

This value mirrors the nullable `expired_at` column of the `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` table. It remains absent for currently active sessions and is populated once a session explicitly ends or reaches its configured expiry, allowing audit and monitoring tools to distinguish between active and historical sessions.

ip.description:
IP address from which this admin session was established.

Stored primarily for security auditing, intrusion detection, and investigation of suspicious administrative actions. Depending on deployment and proxy configuration, this contains either an IPv4 or IPv6 textual representation and is always present for persisted sessions.

href.description:
Full URL (href) of the page where this admin session was initiated.

Captured at session creation time to support security investigations and traceability of administrative access points. The value is persisted as provided by the backend and is always populated for stored session records in `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions`.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that indicates from which page the admin navigated when starting this session.

Useful for analyzing administrative access paths and for correlating events during security reviews. The value is stored in the `referrer` column of `discussion_board_adminuser_sessions` and is always set according to the capturing strategy configured by the backend.

adminUser.description:
Summary information about the administrator who owns this session.

This association projects a lightweight view of the `discussion_board_adminusers` record linked by the underlying `discussion_board_adminuser_id` foreign key. It provides enough context (such as identifier, role, and display name) for audit and monitoring UIs to show which admin account established the session without requiring an additional lookup.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for the administrator user search result set.

This object mirrors the paging state derived from the underlying Prisma query against the `discussion_board_adminusers` table, including the current page index, page size limit, total matching administrator records, and total calculated pages.

Clients use this information to render paging controls in backoffice UIs and to request subsequent pages while preserving the same filter conditions used in the associated `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.IRequest` search.

data.description:
Ordered collection of administrator account summaries returned for the current page.

Each element is an `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.ISummary` projection of a row in the `discussion_board_adminusers` model, containing non-sensitive identification and role information suitable for administrative list views.

The array may be empty when the search yields no matching administrators for the requested filter and page, but it is always present so that clients can reliably iterate without additional null checks.

IPageIDiscussionBoardAdminuser.ISummary.description:
Paginated result wrapper for administrator user summaries in the discussion board service.

This DTO represents a single page of `IDiscussionBoardAdminUser.ISummary` records backed by the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It is used as the response body for operations such as `PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/adminUsers`, where backoffice tools search, filter, and sort administrator accounts.

The `pagination` field exposes page-level metadata (current page, page size, total records, and total pages), while `data` holds the list of administrator summaries for that page. Together they provide a stable, read-only view that UI grids and management consoles can use to render result lists and navigate through large sets of administrator users without exposing sensitive authentication details.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuser.IAuthorized.description: Authorized session payload for a discussionBoard member user, combining issued JWT tokens with minimal member identity information derived from the `discussion_board_memberusers` table.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated member user, corresponding to the primary key of the `discussion_board_memberusers` record.

email.description: Login and contact email address of the member user. This is the unique identifier used for authentication in the discussionBoard service.

display_name.description:
Public display name or nickname for the member user.

This field mirrors the `display_name` column and is shown alongside articles, comments, and other contributions authored by the member.
It is intended to be human‑readable and may differ from the underlying email or account identifier while still complying with any naming guidelines defined in the business rules.

bio.description:
Optional self‑introduction text provided by the member user.

This corresponds to the nullable `bio` column and typically contains a short description of the member's interests, background, or other free‑form profile information.
When null, the member has not supplied any biography text or has explicitly cleared the field.

location.description:
Optional free‑form geographic or topical location for the member user.

The field mirrors the nullable `location` column and may hold values such as city names, countries, regions, or domain interests.
It is treated purely as descriptive text and is not used for strict geographic validation or access control.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the member user's email address has been verified.

This boolean reflects the `email_verified` column and is used by authentication and notification flows to determine if the account has completed required verification steps.
Administrative tooling may rely on this flag when reviewing account trust level or when troubleshooting delivery issues.

account_status.description:
High‑level lifecycle state of the account.

The value comes from the `account_status` column and captures coarse‑grained states such as active, suspended, closed, or banned, according to the business rules defined for the discussion board.
Administrative processes and restriction logic interpret this field to decide what actions the member is allowed to perform throughout the system.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member user account record was created.

This field is mapped from the non‑nullable `created_at` column and is set once when the account is first persisted.
It is used for audit trails, lifecycle analytics, and age‑based policies such as retention or eligibility checks.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member user account record was last updated.

The value mirrors the non‑nullable `updated_at` column and changes whenever mutable account attributes are modified by either the member or an administrator.
It allows operators to understand how recently the profile or status was adjusted and can support concurrency control strategies.

deleted_at.description:
Soft‑deletion timestamp for the member account.

This field maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column and is populated when the account is logically removed from active use while its historical content may remain for audit or compliance purposes.
A null value indicates that the account has not been soft‑deleted, whereas a non‑null value marks the effective time of logical deletion.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the last successful login for this member user.

The field reflects the nullable `last_login_at` column and is updated by authentication workflows each time the member successfully signs in.
It is used for security monitoring, dormant‑account detection, and administrative review of recent activity.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the account was explicitly closed.

This value corresponds to the nullable `closed_at` column and records when the account transitioned to a closed state, whether by user choice or by administrative action.
It may be used in combination with `account_status` and `deleted_at` to interpret long‑term retention and reactivation policies.

closed_by_admin.description:
Indicates whether the account closure was initiated by an administrator.

This boolean maps to the `closed_by_admin` column and differentiates between user‑driven closure and administrative enforcement.
It is important for moderation reporting, compliance tracking, and any business logic that treats voluntarily closed accounts differently from administratively closed or sanctioned accounts.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuser.IAuthorized.description:
Authorized administrator session payload for the discussion board service.

Represents the authentication result for an administrative user (adminUser actor) after join, login, or refresh operations. It encapsulates the administrator's identifier along with issued JWT token information and a concise admin profile snapshot derived from the `discussion_board_adminusers` table.

This DTO is used as the standard response body for administrative authentication flows, enabling clients to store the admin identity and tokens securely while keeping sensitive credential material (such as password hashes) completely hidden from the API surface.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrative user in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table.

This value is used throughout the system to correlate admin activity, associate sessions, and perform authorization checks. It must never be guessed or provided by clients; it is always issued and controlled by the backend.

loginId.description:
Login identifier or account name for the administrator user.

Used when signing into the administrative interface. Must be unique within the `discussion_board_adminusers` table according to business rules and Prisma constraints.

displayName.description:
Human-readable name displayed in administrative UIs and audit logs when referring to this administrator user.

This value corresponds to the `display_name` column in `discussion_board_adminusers` but is exposed to clients using camelCase naming for consistency with other DTOs.

email.description:
Login email address of the administrative user as stored in `discussion_board_adminusers.email`.

This field is returned so that clients can confirm which admin account is currently authenticated and display it in profile or account menus.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the administrator account as stored in `discussion_board_adminusers.account_status`.

Typical values represent states such as active, suspended, or closed according to business rules. Clients can use this value to adjust UI state or block further actions when an account is no longer allowed to operate.

role.description:
Role or permission level granted to this administrator user.

Determines what administrative actions the user may perform in the discussionBoard service, such as moderating articles and comments or handling reports.

emailVerified.description:
Indicates whether the admin's email has passed the verification process as reflected in `discussion_board_adminusers.email_verified`.

When `false`, certain flows may restrict access or encourage completion of verification depending on policy.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this administrator user record was created in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table.

Used for audit and sorting purposes in backoffice tools and to understand how long an admin account has existed.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this administrator user record in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table.

Useful for determining when profile or status changes last occurred and for cache invalidation in client applications.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuser.IRequest.description:
Search and filter DTO for retrieving a paginated list of member user accounts from the discussion_board_memberusers table.

This type encapsulates flexible administrative search criteria over registered discussion board member accounts, including optional filters on lifecycle status, email verification, creation and last login time windows, as well as free-text search across key profile fields.

It also carries pagination and sorting parameters so that back-office and moderation tools can efficiently browse large populations of member users while only exposing non-sensitive metadata in the associated summary response type.

page.description:
1-based page index indicating which slice of the result set to return.

Administrative clients should start with page 1 and increment this value when stepping through additional pages of member accounts. If omitted, the backend may default to the first page.

This field is used together with page_size to compute the database offset into the discussion_board_memberusers table when executing search queries.

page_size.description:
Number of member user records to include in a single page of results.

This value controls the page size for paginated queries over the discussion_board_memberusers table. Implementations typically enforce an upper bound (for example 100) to protect performance and prevent excessively large responses.

When omitted, the backend may apply a sensible default page size suitable for administrative list views.

email_verified.description:
Optional filter on the email verification status of member accounts.

When set to true, only accounts with email_verified = true in the discussion_board_memberusers table are included in the result set. When set to false, only accounts that have not completed email verification are returned.

A null value or omission of this property means that both verified and unverified accounts are eligible for inclusion, subject to other filters.

account_statuses.description:
Optional list of account lifecycle states to include in the search.

Each element corresponds to a value stored in the account_status column of the discussion_board_memberusers Prisma model, such as active, suspended, closed, or banned. When this array is provided and non-empty, only accounts whose account_status matches one of the specified values are returned.

If omitted or empty, no explicit filter is applied to the account_status field and all statuses are considered based on other criteria.

created_from.description:
Lower bound of the account creation timestamp window for filtering results.

When set to a date-time value, only member accounts with created_at greater than or equal to this timestamp in the discussion_board_memberusers table are included. This is commonly used to find recently registered users.

A null or omitted value indicates that there is no lower bound on created_at for the search.

created_to.description:
Upper bound of the account creation timestamp window for filtering results.

When set, only member accounts with created_at less than or equal to this date-time are returned. Combined with created_from, this allows administrators to search for accounts created within a specific time range.

A null or omitted value means there is no upper bound filter on created_at.

last_login_from.description:
Lower bound of the last_login_at window for filtering member accounts by recent activity.

When supplied, only accounts whose last_login_at is greater than or equal to this timestamp are included. This is helpful for locating recently active users or for auditing dormant accounts in combination with other filters.

Null or omission indicates that no lower bound is applied to the last_login_at field.

last_login_to.description:
Upper bound of the last_login_at window for filtering member accounts based on their most recent login.

When set, only accounts whose last_login_at is less than or equal to this timestamp are returned. Together with last_login_from this provides administrators with a flexible way to target users active in a specific period.

A null or missing value means no upper bound filter is applied to last_login_at.

search.description:
Free-text search term used to match against key member profile fields.

Implementations typically apply this value to one or more columns in the discussion_board_memberusers table, such as email, display_name, or optional profile text fields like bio and location. The exact search strategy (for example ILIKE matching or full-text indexing) is implementation-specific.

This field is particularly useful when administrators need to quickly locate a specific account without constructing detailed filter criteria.

order_by.description:
Name of the primary field used to sort the search results.

Common values include created_at, last_login_at, email, or display_name, corresponding to columns on the discussion_board_memberusers model. When omitted, the backend may default to ordering by created_at or another sensible default that supports typical administrative workflows.

This field should only accept a controlled set of column names to prevent arbitrary ordering expressions or SQL injection-like patterns.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied to the order_by field when returning paginated results.

A value of asc sorts results in ascending order (for example, oldest created_at first), while desc sorts in descending order (for example, newest created_at first). This field is only meaningful when used together with a valid order_by value.

If not provided, the backend often defaults to descending order for date-based fields so that the most recent accounts appear first in administrative lists.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuser.description:
Represents a registered member user account in the discussionBoard service.

This DTO is a detail response type mapped to the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma model and is used by administrative read and update operations that inspect or manage a single member account.
It exposes business‑relevant identity, profile, and lifecycle fields while carefully omitting sensitive authentication internals such as the raw `password_hash` column.

The type is primarily consumed by adminUser‑only endpoints like `GET /discussionBoard/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}` and `PUT /discussionBoard/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}`.
Administrators use this data to understand how a member account is configured, how it has evolved over time, and what its current status is in moderation and restriction workflows.

id.description:
Primary key of the member user account.

This value corresponds to the `id` UUID column of the `discussion_board_memberusers` table and uniquely identifies the member throughout the entire discussionBoard domain.
It is used as the `memberUserId` path parameter in administrative APIs and is immutable once created.

email.description:
Email address of the member user.

This field maps to the `email` column in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table and serves both as the primary login identifier and as the main contact address for system notifications.
The value must be unique among all member users and is expected to follow standard RFC‑compliant email formatting.

display_name.description:
Public display name or nickname for the member user.

This field mirrors the `display_name` column and is shown alongside articles, comments, and other contributions authored by the member.
It is intended to be human‑readable and may differ from the underlying email or account identifier while still complying with any naming guidelines defined in the business rules.

bio.description:
Optional self‑introduction text provided by the member user.

This corresponds to the nullable `bio` column and typically contains a short description of the member's interests, background, or other free‑form profile information.
When null, the member has not supplied any biography text or has explicitly cleared the field.

location.description:
Optional free‑form geographic or topical location for the member user.

The field mirrors the nullable `location` column and may hold values such as city names, countries, regions, or domain interests.
It is treated purely as descriptive text and is not used for strict geographic validation or access control.

email_verified.description:
Indicates whether the member user's email address has been verified.

This boolean reflects the `email_verified` column and is used by authentication and notification flows to determine if the account has completed required verification steps.
Administrative tooling may rely on this flag when reviewing account trust level or when troubleshooting delivery issues.

account_status.description:
High‑level lifecycle state of the account.

The value comes from the `account_status` column and captures coarse‑grained states such as active, suspended, closed, or banned, according to the business rules defined for the discussion board.
Administrative processes and restriction logic interpret this field to decide what actions the member is allowed to perform throughout the system.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the member user account record was created.

This field is mapped from the non‑nullable `created_at` column and is set once when the account is first persisted.
It is used for audit trails, lifecycle analytics, and age‑based policies such as retention or eligibility checks.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the member user account record was last updated.

The value mirrors the non‑nullable `updated_at` column and changes whenever mutable account attributes are modified by either the member or an administrator.
It allows operators to understand how recently the profile or status was adjusted and can support concurrency control strategies.

deleted_at.description:
Soft‑deletion timestamp for the member account.

This field maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column and is populated when the account is logically removed from active use while its historical content may remain for audit or compliance purposes.
A null value indicates that the account has not been soft‑deleted, whereas a non‑null value marks the effective time of logical deletion.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the last successful login for this member user.

The field reflects the nullable `last_login_at` column and is updated by authentication workflows each time the member successfully signs in.
It is used for security monitoring, dormant‑account detection, and administrative review of recent activity.

closed_at.description:
Timestamp when the account was explicitly closed.

This value corresponds to the nullable `closed_at` column and records when the account transitioned to a closed state, whether by user choice or by administrative action.
It may be used in combination with `account_status` and `deleted_at` to interpret long‑term retention and reactivation policies.

closed_by_admin.description:
Indicates whether the account closure was initiated by an administrator.

This boolean maps to the `closed_by_admin` column and differentiates between user‑driven closure and administrative enforcement.
It is important for moderation reporting, compliance tracking, and any business logic that treats voluntarily closed accounts differently from administratively closed or sanctioned accounts.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuser.IUpdate.description:
Administrative update payload for a discussion board member user account.

This DTO is consumed by the `PUT /discussionBoard/adminUser/memberUsers/{memberUserId}` endpoint and is designed specifically for trusted adminUser actors to modify mutable aspects of a member profile and lifecycle state.
It intentionally exposes only those columns from the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma model that business rules permit administrators to change directly and excludes immutable identifiers and sensitive authentication fields such as `id` and `password_hash`.

All properties in this update type are optional, allowing partial updates where only the provided fields are changed.
System‑managed fields like `updated_at` are set by the backend implementation, and ownership‑related columns remain outside the scope of this DTO.

email.description:
New email address for the member user when an administrator needs to adjust the primary contact or login identifier.

This field maps to the `email` column of the `discussion_board_memberusers` table and must remain unique across all member accounts.
If omitted, the email address is left unchanged; when supplied, the backend should enforce appropriate validation and any required verification workflows.

display_name.description:
Updated public display name or nickname for the member user.

The value corresponds to the `display_name` column and is what other users see alongside articles and comments authored by this member.
When provided, it replaces the previous display name; if not included in the request, the existing value remains unchanged.

bio.description:
Updated biography text for the member user profile.

This property targets the nullable `bio` column and supports both replacing the current biography with new text and explicitly clearing it by sending a null value.
If the property is omitted from the update payload, the existing biography is preserved as is.

location.description:
Updated free‑form location or main interest description for the member user.

It maps to the nullable `location` column and can contain geographic information or topical hints used purely for display purposes.
Providing null explicitly clears the existing value, whereas omitting this property from the update leaves the stored location unchanged.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating the desired verified state of the member's email address.

When supplied, this property updates the `email_verified` column and is typically manipulated only by administrative tooling or automated verification workflows.
If not present in the update payload, the existing verification state is preserved.

account_status.description:
New high‑level lifecycle state for the member account.

This field updates the `account_status` column and is central to enabling or restricting the member's capabilities across the discussion board, with values such as active, suspended, closed, or banned as defined by business rules.
The implementation must enforce valid state transitions and any additional side effects required when the status changes.

deleted_at.description:
Administrative control over the soft‑deletion timestamp of the account.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column and allows administrators or automated processes to mark or unmark an account as logically deleted.
When null is provided, any existing soft‑deletion timestamp may be cleared according to business rules; if omitted, the current value remains unchanged.

closed_at.description:
Updated closure timestamp for the member account.

The value corresponds to the nullable `closed_at` column and should only be manipulated in carefully controlled administrative workflows that manage long‑term account closure.
Explicitly setting null may reopen certain lifecycle interpretations where permitted, while omitting the field leaves the previous closure timestamp intact.

closed_by_admin.description:
Indicates whether, after this update, the account should be considered closed by an administrator rather than by the member.

This updates the `closed_by_admin` column and is typically set in conjunction with changes to `account_status` and `closed_at` when moderation or policy decisions require administrative closure.
If this property is not supplied in the update, the existing flag value is preserved.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuser.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and paginating administrator user accounts in the discussion board service.

This schema defines complex filter, sorting, and pagination parameters used by the PATCH /discussionBoard/adminUser/adminUsers endpoint to query the discussion_board_adminusers table via Prisma. It allows backoffice tools to search admin users by name or email, filter by activation status, and control result ordering and pagination. All fields are optional so that clients can combine them flexibly based on UI needs.

search.description:
Free-form search keyword applied to administrator identification fields such as login ID, display name, or email.

The service layer interprets this string to build a Prisma WHERE clause using a combination of contains/startsWith/OR conditions across multiple textual columns on discussion_board_adminusers. An empty or omitted value means no text filtering is applied.

status.description:
Optional status filter for administrator accounts.

Represents a business-level activation or visibility state for admin users, such as active vs. disabled. The exact allowed values must align with the status or state column defined on the discussion_board_adminusers Prisma model (for example, "active", "inactive", "suspended"), and are validated in the service layer. When omitted, admins of all statuses are included in the result set.

role.description:
Optional role or permission-group filter limiting results to administrators with a specific role.

The concrete domain values must match the role or permission field defined for discussion_board_adminusers (for example, "superAdmin", "moderator", or other role codes). When provided, only admins whose role matches this value are returned. When omitted, admins of all roles are included.

orderBy.description:
Field name used for sorting the administrator list.

Typical values correspond to sortable columns on the discussion_board_adminusers table, such as "createdAt", "updatedAt", "displayName", or "email". The service validates this against an allow-list of sortable fields and then maps it to a Prisma ORDER BY clause.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction applied together with orderBy when returning administrator accounts.

Supported values are typically "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending. If omitted, the service applies its default sort direction for the chosen orderBy field.
