Supported values are typically "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending. If omitted, the service applies its default sort direction for the chosen orderBy field.

orderDirection.description:
Sort direction applied together with orderBy when returning administrator accounts.

Supported values are typically "asc" for ascending and "desc" for descending. If omitted, the service applies its default sort direction for the chosen orderBy field.

page.description:
1-based page index for pagination over administrator accounts.

Represents the requested page number in the logical result set. When omitted, the service defaults to the first page. Must be a positive integer when provided.

limit.description:
Maximum number of administrator account records to return in a single page.

Used together with page to implement skip/take pagination in Prisma. The service enforces an upper bound to prevent excessively large pages. When omitted, a reasonable default page size is applied.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuser.description:
Detailed administrator user profile mapped to the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model.

This DTO is returned by administrator-focused read and update operations such as GET or PUT `/discussionBoard/adminUser/adminUsers/{adminUserId}`. It represents the full business profile of an administrator account, exposing identification, contact, lifecycle status, and audit information that is safe to surface to other authorized admins.

Sensitive authentication internals such as the `password_hash` column or any token-related data are intentionally excluded even though they exist on the underlying table. The field set instead focuses on profile metadata and operational flags that are necessary for account management, moderation, and audit tooling.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator user in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table.

This value corresponds directly to the `id` primary key column, which is stored as a UUID in the database. It is used as the path parameter value for administrator detail and update endpoints and forms the stable handle for all foreign-key and audit relationships referencing this admin account.

displayName.description:
Public or semi-public display name of the administrator account.

This property maps to the non-nullable `display_name` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It is shown in administrative user interfaces, moderation actions, and audit logs so that humans can easily recognize which administrator performed a given operation.

email.description:
Primary email address associated with this administrator account.

This property reflects the non-nullable, unique `email` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. It is used for authentication flows, administrative notifications, and contact in case of security or policy issues. The value must be a well-formed email address and must remain unique among all administrator records.

bio.description:
Optional short profile or role description for this administrator account.

This property maps to the nullable `bio` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It can contain free-form text describing the administrator’s responsibilities, team, or role in the organization. When no description has been provided, the value is stored as null in the database and may be omitted from user interface displays.

emailVerified.description:
Indicates whether the administrator’s email address has been verified.

This flag is backed by the non-nullable `email_verified` boolean column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. A value of `true` means the admin has successfully passed the email verification process, while `false` usually restricts access to certain high-risk operations until verification is completed. Changes to this field should be driven by controlled verification workflows or privileged administrative tools.

accountStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of the administrator account controlling whether the admin can actively use the system.

This value corresponds to the non-nullable `account_status` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. Typical business values include states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`, and they determine whether the admin may authenticate and perform moderation tasks. The exact domain of allowed values is enforced by application-level business rules rather than this schema.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp indicating when this administrator account record was first created.

This property mirrors the non-nullable `created_at` `DateTime` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. It is generated by the persistence layer at insert time and is used for audit trails, chronological sorting in management screens, and reporting on the growth of administrative staff over time.

updatedAt.description:
Timestamp of the most recent update to this administrator account record.

This property reflects the non-nullable `updated_at` `DateTime` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It is automatically updated whenever profile metadata or status flags on this admin account change, allowing tooling to determine how fresh the displayed information is and to support concurrency controls where needed.

deletedAt.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this administrator account, if it has been logically removed.

This property maps to the nullable `deleted_at` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. When the value is a date-time, the account is considered soft-deleted and should no longer be usable for authentication or regular operations, although it may still appear in audit views. When the value is null, the account is considered not soft-deleted.

lastLoginAt.description:
Timestamp of the last successful login for this administrator account.

This property corresponds to the nullable `last_login_at` `DateTime` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` model. It is updated whenever the admin successfully authenticates and is primarily used for security reviews, detecting stale accounts, and providing visibility in account management dashboards about when an admin last accessed the system.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuser.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for a discussionBoard administrator user profile.

This DTO represents the subset of columns on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model that are allowed to change through profile maintenance APIs. It intentionally excludes identity and authentication-related fields such as the primary key and `password_hash`, focusing instead on profile metadata and account lifecycle flags.

All properties are optional so that clients can perform partial updates. The service layer is responsible for applying validation rules, enforcing uniqueness constraints on the `email` column, and controlling which actors are allowed to change sensitive flags such as `email_verified` or `account_status`.

email.description:
Administrator email address used for authentication and notifications.

This property maps directly to the non-nullable, unique `email` column of the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. During an update, the value may be changed to reflect a new contact address, but the service must ensure that the email remains unique among all administrator accounts and that it conforms to standard email formatting rules.

display_name.description:
Display name of the administrator account in snake_case form.

This field writes to the `display_name` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It is maintained for compatibility with code paths or generators that refer to the column name directly. Clients may supply either this snake_case property or the camelCase `displayName` property to update the administrator’s human-readable name.

displayName.description:
Human-readable display name of the administrator account in camelCase form.

This property is a convenience alias for the underlying `display_name` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. It is typically preferred in TypeScript and JSON APIs where camelCase naming is standard, while still updating the same database column and carrying the same semantic meaning as the `display_name` property.

bio.description:
Optional short profile or role description for this administrator.

This property maps to the nullable `bio` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. Providing a non-null value stores or updates the description, while explicitly sending null clears the existing text. The text may be surfaced in internal administrative interfaces to provide context about the admin’s responsibilities.

email_verified.description:
Email verification flag for the administrator account in snake_case form.

This property writes to the `email_verified` boolean column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. It is kept for compatibility with column-oriented naming. Only controlled workflows or privileged administrative tools should update this flag, as it indicates whether the admin’s email address has been successfully verified.

emailVerified.description:
Email verification flag for the administrator account in camelCase form.

This property is a camelCase alias for the `email_verified` column of the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. Setting this value to true or false updates the same underlying field as `email_verified` and should follow the same business rules and audit requirements related to email verification.

account_status.description:
Lifecycle status of the administrator account in snake_case form.

This property updates the `account_status` column on the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. It is maintained in snake_case for callers or tooling that work directly with database column names. Typical values include `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`, and they control whether the admin may authenticate and perform moderation duties.

accountStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of the administrator account in camelCase form.

This property is a camelCase alias for the `account_status` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` model. It updates the same underlying field as `account_status` but aligns with usual JSON and TypeScript naming conventions. Application-level rules determine which status values are allowed and what effects they have on administrator capabilities.

IDiscussionBoardMemberuser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a discussion board member user, optimized for list views, embeddings, and moderation tooling.

This DTO is backed by the `discussion_board_memberusers` Prisma model and exposes only public and moderation-relevant scalar fields, avoiding any sensitive authentication data or reverse collections.

It is typically embedded into other response DTOs (for example, report or comment views) whenever a compact representation of the member user is required without loading the full account record.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the member user in the discussion board system.

This value maps directly to `discussion_board_memberusers.id` and is used as the stable primary key for joins and references in other entities such as articles, comments, and reports.

display_name.description:
Public display name or nickname for the member user.

This property corresponds to the `discussion_board_memberusers.display_name` column and is shown alongside articles, comments, and other user-generated content.

It is intentionally included in the summary so that UIs can render meaningful author or reporter labels without fetching the full member user detail record.

account_status.description:
High-level lifecycle state of the member user account.

This field is mapped from the `discussion_board_memberusers.account_status` column and indicates whether the account is active, suspended, closed, banned, or in a similar business-defined state.

Including this value in the summary allows moderation and administrative views to quickly assess whether the reporter or author is currently restricted or fully active.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this member user account was created.

This value is sourced from the `discussion_board_memberusers.created_at` column and is useful for sorting and for quickly understanding the relative age of an account in list and audit views.

IDiscussionBoardAdminuser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a discussion board administrator user account derived from the discussion_board_adminusers Prisma model.

This DTO is optimized for administrative list screens, moderation history, and audit trails where many administrator rows are shown at once. It exposes only non-sensitive profile, contact, status, and activity fields that are safe to include in responses while still allowing operators to quickly identify who an admin is and what state their account is in.

The summary aligns closely with the underlying database columns: it includes identifiers, the administrator’s email and display name, key lifecycle flags such as email verification and account_status, and important timestamps like created_at and last_login_at. Sensitive authentication details such as password_hash are never exposed here, and fields that would require full-detail views can be added through more specific DTOs if needed.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the administrator account in the discussion board system.

This value corresponds directly to the `id` primary key column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model and is generated as a UUID when the admin account is created.

It is used throughout the system as the stable reference for linking sessions, moderation actions, and audit records back to this admin user.

email.description:
Login and contact email address for the administrator account.

This value maps to the `email` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table, which is unique among administrator accounts. It is used both for authentication and for delivering critical notifications such as security alerts or moderation workflow messages.

In list and summary views, this field helps operations staff quickly identify the specific admin account they are inspecting or acting upon.

display_name.description:
Human-friendly display name for the administrator shown in dashboards, logs, and moderation views.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `display_name` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. It is the primary name shown to other administrators when attributing actions, such as “article removed by {display_name}”.

Unlike internal identifiers, the display name is intended to be easily recognizable and may follow organizational naming conventions or role-based labels.

profile_image_url.description:
Optional public URL of the administrator's profile image used in the UI.

This value is expected to be a pre-uploaded URL pointing to an image stored in an external storage service (for example, an object storage bucket or CDN). The backend never accepts raw binary or base64 image data in this field; only the resolved URL is persisted and exposed.

When not set or when the administrator has not configured an avatar, this property may be omitted from responses and client applications should fall back to a default placeholder image.

email_verified.description:
Flag indicating whether the administrator's email address has been verified.

This property reflects the `email_verified` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model. When true, the account has successfully completed whatever email verification process the system requires, which may be a prerequisite for performing sensitive actions.

In administrative summaries, this field helps security and platform teams quickly identify accounts that are operating with unverified contact details and may require additional review or restrictions.

account_status.description:
Lifecycle status code representing the current state of the administrator account.

This property corresponds to the non-nullable `account_status` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. Typical business values include states such as `active`, `suspended`, or `closed`, but the exact set of codes is defined by the domain.

In list views, this field allows operators to see at a glance whether an admin can sign in and exercise privileges, or whether access has been restricted due to policy violations, security concerns, or organizational changes.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the administrator account record was created.

The value maps to the `created_at` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` Prisma model and is stored as an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC. It typically corresponds to the moment the account was first registered or provisioned by another admin.

This field is frequently used in audit and reporting contexts to understand how long an administrator has existed in the system and to segment accounts by tenure or onboarding wave.

last_login_at.description:
Timestamp of the most recent successful login for this administrator account, when available.

This property reflects the nullable `last_login_at` column in the `discussion_board_adminusers` table. When present, it indicates the last time the admin successfully authenticated and began a session. For newly created or unused accounts, this column may be null and the field may be omitted in responses.

Administrative dashboards can use this value to highlight dormant accounts, detect unusual activity patterns, or support security reviews by showing when an admin last accessed the system.
